entries.literal: Its orudo was on the Helu River; the tomb was south of Zu prefecture.

entries.zh: 正戶八千，蕃漢轉戶一萬，出騎軍一萬。
entries.en: Regular households 8,000; tribal and Han rotational households 10,000; fielding 10,000 cavalry.
entries.literal: Regular households 8,000; tribal and Han rotational households 10,000; producing 10,000 cavalry.

entries.zh: 孤穩斡魯朵，承天太后置。
entries.en: The Guwen orudo, established by Empress Chengtian.
entries.literal: Guwen orudo, Empress Chengtian established.

entries.zh: 是為崇德宮。
entries.en: This is the Chongde Palace.
entries.literal: This was the Chongde Palace.

entries.zh: 玉曰「孤穩」。
entries.en: In the national language "jade" is "Guwen."
entries.literal: National language "jade" is "Guwen."

entries.zh: 以乾、顯、雙三州戶置。
entries.en: It was established from households of Qian, Xian, and Shuang prefectures.
entries.literal: Set up using households of Qian, Xian, and Shuang prefectures.

entries.zh: 其斡魯朵在土河東，陵祔景宗皇帝。
entries.en: Its orudo was east of the Tu River; the tomb adjoined Emperor Jingzong's.
entries.literal: Its orudo was east of the Tu River; the tomb adjoined Emperor Jingzong's.

entries.zh: 正戶六千，蕃漢轉戶一萬，出騎軍一萬。
entries.en: Regular households 6,000; tribal and Han rotational households 10,000; fielding 10,000 cavalry.
entries.literal: Regular households 6,000; tribal and Han rotational households 10,000; producing 10,000 cavalry.

entries.zh: 女古斡魯朵，聖宗置。
entries.en: The Nügu orudo, established by Shengzong.
entries.literal: Nügu orudo, Shengzong established.

entries.zh: 是為興聖宮。
entries.en: This is the Xingsheng Palace.
entries.literal: This was the Xingsheng Palace.

entries.zh: 金曰「女古」。
entries.en: In the national language "gold" is "Nügu."
entries.literal: National language "gold" is "Nügu."

entries.zh: 以國阿輦、耶魯碗、蒲速碗三斡魯朵戶置。
entries.en: It was established from households of the Guoalian, Yeluwan, and Pusuwan orudo.
entries.literal: It was established from households of the Guoalian, Yeluwan, and Pusuwan orudo.

entries.zh: 其斡魯朵在女混活直，陵寢在慶州南安。
entries.en: Its orudo was at Nühunhuozhi; the tomb was at the southern peace of Qing prefecture.
entries.literal: Its orudo was at Nühunhuozhi; the tomb was at the southern peace of Qing prefecture.

entries.zh: 正戶一萬，蕃漢轉戶二萬，出騎軍五千。
entries.en: Regular households 10,000; tribal and Han rotational households 20,000; fielding 5,000 cavalry.
entries.literal: Regular households 10,000; tribal and Han rotational households 20,000; producing 5,000 cavalry.

entries.zh: 阿思斡魯朵，道宗置。
entries.en: The Asi orudo, established by Daozong.
entries.literal: Asi orudo, Daozong established.

entries.zh: 是為太和宮。
entries.en: This is the Taihe Palace.
entries.literal: This was the Taihe Palace.

entries.zh: 寬大曰「阿思」。
entries.en: In the national language "broad and generous" is "Asi."
entries.literal: National language "broad and generous" is "Asi."

entries.zh: 以諸斡魯朵御前承應人及興中府戶置。
entries.en: It was established from attendants before the throne of the various orudo and households of Xingzhong prefecture.
entries.literal: It was established from attendants before the throne of the various orudo and households of Xingzhong prefecture.

entries.zh: 其斡魯朵在好水濼，陵寢在上京慶州。
entries.en: Its orudo was at Haoshui Bo; the tomb was at Shangjing Qing prefecture.
entries.literal: Its orudo was at Haoshui Bo; the tomb was at Shangjing Qing prefecture.

entries.zh: 正戶一萬，蕃漢轉戶二萬，出騎軍一萬五千。
entries.en: Regular households 10,000; tribal and Han rotational households 20,000; fielding 15,000 cavalry.
entries.literal: Regular households 10,000; tribal and Han rotational households 20,000; producing 15,000 cavalry.

entries.zh: 營衛誌上
entries.en: Treatise on Camps and Guards, Part 1
entries.literal: Treatise on Camps and Guards, Part 1

entries.zh: 夏捺缽：無常所，多在吐兒山。
entries.en: The summer napo had no fixed place and was mostly at Tuer Mountain.
entries.literal: Summer napo: no fixed place, mostly at Tuer Mountain.

entries.zh: 道宗每歲先幸黑山，拜聖宗、興宗陵，賞金蓮。
entries.en: Each year Daozong first visited Black Mountain, paid respects at the tombs of Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong, and admired the golden lotus.
entries.literal: Daozong each year first visited Black Mountain, paid respects at Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong's tombs, and rewarded golden lotus.

entries.zh: 乃幸子河避暑。
entries.en: Then he visited Zi River to escape the summer heat.
entries.literal: Then visited Zi River to escape summer heat.

entries.zh: 吐兒山在黑山東北三百里，近饅頭山。
entries.en: Tuer Mountain lies three hundred li northeast of Black Mountain, near Mantou Mountain.
entries.literal: Tuer Mountain is three hundred li northeast of Black Mountain, near Mantou Mountain.

entries.zh: 黑山在慶州北十三里，上有池，池中有金蓮。
entries.en: Black Mountain is thirteen li north of Qing prefecture; on its summit is a pool, and in the pool are golden lotus.
entries.literal: Black Mountain is thirteen li north of Qing prefecture; above it is a pool, and in the pool are golden lotus.

entries.zh: 子河在吐兒山東北三百里。
entries.en: Zi River is three hundred li northeast of Tuer Mountain.
entries.literal: Zi River is three hundred li northeast of Tuer Mountain.

entries.zh: 懷州西山有清涼殿，亦為行幸避暑之所。
entries.en: West Mountain of Huai prefecture has a Cool Breeze Hall, also used as a traveling residence to escape summer heat.
entries.literal: West Mountain of Huai prefecture has a Cool Breeze Hall, also a traveling residence for escaping summer heat.

entries.zh: 四月中旬起牙帳，卜吉地為納涼所，五月末旬、六月上旬至。
entries.en: In the middle ten days of the fourth month the tented camp was raised and an auspicious site chosen as the cool retreat; they arrived in the last ten days of the fifth month or the first ten days of the sixth month.
entries.literal: In the middle ten days of the fourth month the tented camp was raised; an auspicious site chosen as the cool retreat; arrived in the last ten days of the fifth month and the first ten days of the sixth month.

entries.zh: 居五旬。
entries.en: They dwelt there fifty days.
entries.literal: Dwelling fifty days.

entries.zh: 與北、南臣僚議國事，暇日遊獵。
entries.en: With northern and southern officials they deliberated state affairs; on leisure days they hunted.
entries.literal: With northern and southern officials they deliberated state affairs; on leisure days they hunted.

entries.zh: 七月中旬乃去。
entries.en: In the middle ten days of the seventh month they departed.
entries.literal: In the middle ten days of the seventh month they departed.

entries.zh: 奇首八部為高麗、蠕蠕所侵，僅以萬口附於元魏。
entries.en: Qishou's eight bu were invaded by Goryeo and Rouran; only about ten thousand mouths attached to Northern Wei.
entries.literal: Qishou's eight bu were invaded by Goryeo and Rouran; only about ten thousand mouths attached to Northern Wei.

entries.zh: 生聚未幾，北齊見侵，掠男女十萬餘口。
entries.en: Barely had they multiplied when Northern Qi invaded and carried off men and women numbering more than one hundred thousand mouths.
entries.literal: Barely had they multiplied when Northern Qi invaded and carried off men and women numbering more than one hundred thousand mouths.

entries.zh: 繼為突厥所逼。
entries.en: Then they were pressed by the Turks.
entries.literal: Then they were pressed by the Turks.

entries.zh: 寄處高麗，不過萬家。
entries.en: Dwelling with Goryeo, they did not reach ten thousand households.
entries.literal: Dwelling with Goryeo, not reaching ten thousand households.

entries.zh: 部落離散，非復古八部矣。
entries.en: The bu were scattered and dispersed, no longer the ancient eight bu.
entries.literal: The bu were scattered and dispersed, no longer the ancient eight bu.

entries.zh: 別部有臣附突厥者，內附於隋者，依紇臣水而居。
entries.en: Another bu had subjects attaching to the Turks; those attaching inward to Sui dwelt along the Heichen River.
entries.literal: Another bu had subjects attaching to the Turks; those attaching inward to Sui dwelt along the Heichen River.

entries.zh: 部落漸眾，分為十部，有地遼西五百餘里。
entries.en: The bu gradually grew numerous, divided into ten bu, with territory more than five hundred li in eastern Liaoxi.
entries.literal: The bu gradually grew numerous, divided into ten bu, with territory more than five hundred li in eastern Liaoxi.

entries.zh: 唐世大賀氏仍為八部，而松漠、玄州別出，亦十部也。
entries.en: In Tang times the Dahe clan still had eight bu, while Songmo and Xuan prefectures were separately established—also ten bu.
entries.literal: In Tang times the Dahe clan still had eight bu, while Songmo and Xuan prefectures were separately established—also ten bu.

entries.zh: 遙輦氏承萬榮可突於散敗之餘，更為八部，然遙輦、叠刺別出，又十部也。
entries.en: The Yaolian clan inherited the scattered remnants after Wanrong and Ketuyu's defeat and again made eight bu, yet Yaolian and Yilie separately emerged—again ten bu.
entries.literal: The Yaolian clan inherited the scattered remnants after Wanrong and Ketuyu's defeat and again made eight bu, yet Yaolian and Yilie separately emerged—again ten bu.

entries.zh: 阻午可汗析為二十部，契丹始大。
entries.en: Khan Zuwu divided them into twenty bu, and the Khitan first grew great.
entries.literal: Khan Zuwu divided them into twenty bu, and the Khitan first grew great.

entries.zh: 至於遼太祖，析九帳、三房之族，更列二十部。
entries.en: At Liao Taizu the nine accounts and three-father-house clans were further divided into twenty bu.
entries.literal: At Liao Taizu, the nine accounts and three-father-house clans were further divided into twenty bu.

entries.zh: 聖宗之世，分置十有六，增置十有八，並舊為五十四部；
entries.en: In Emperor Shengzong's time sixteen were newly placed and eighteen more added, together with the old totaling fifty-four bu;
entries.literal: In Emperor Shengzong's time sixteen were newly placed, eighteen more added, together with the old totaling fifty-four bu;

entries.zh: 內有拔裏、乙室已國舅族，外有附庸十部，盛矣！
entries.en: within were the Balin and Yishi national-uncle clans; outside were ten dependent bu—how flourishing!
entries.literal: within were the Balin and Yishi national-uncle clans, outside were ten dependent bu—how flourishing!

entries.zh: 秋捺缽：曰伏虎林。
entries.en: The autumn napo was called Crouching Tiger Forest.
entries.literal: Autumn napo: called Crouching Tiger Forest.

entries.zh: 七月中旬，自納涼處起牙帳，入山射鹿及虎。
entries.en: In the middle ten days of the seventh month they raised the tented camp from the cool retreat and entered the mountains to shoot deer and tigers.
entries.literal: In the middle ten days of the seventh month, from the cool retreat the tented camp was raised; entering the mountains to shoot deer and tiger.

entries.zh: 林在永州西北五十里。
entries.en: The forest is fifty li northwest of Yong prefecture.
entries.literal: The forest is fifty li northwest of Yong prefecture.

entries.zh: 嘗有虎據林，傷害居民畜牧。
entries.en: Once a tiger occupied the forest and harmed the livestock of local residents.
entries.literal: Once a tiger occupied the forest and harmed residents' livestock.

entries.zh: 景宗領數騎獵焉，虎伏草際，戰栗不敢仰視，上舍之，因號伏虎林。
entries.en: Emperor Jingzong led several riders to hunt there; the tiger crouched in the grass, trembling and not daring to look up; the emperor spared it, and so it was named Crouching Tiger Forest.
entries.literal: Emperor Jingzong led several riders to hunt there; the tiger crouched in the grass, trembling and not daring to look up; the emperor spared it, and so it was named Crouching Tiger Forest.

entries.zh: 每歲車駕至。
entries.en: Each year the imperial carriage arrived.
entries.literal: Each year the imperial carriage arrived.

entries.zh: 皇族而下，分布濼水側，伺夜將半，鹿飲鹽水，令獵人吹角效鹿鳴，既集而射之。
entries.en: From the imperial clan downward they were posted along the marsh water; toward midnight, when deer came to drink salt water, hunters blew horns imitating deer calls; when the deer gathered they shot them.
entries.literal: From the imperial clan downward they were distributed along the marsh water; toward midnight when deer drank salt water, hunters blew horns imitating deer calls; when gathered they shot them.

entries.zh: 謂之「舐堿鹿」、又名「呼鹿。」
entries.en: This was called "licking-salt deer" and also called "calling deer."
entries.literal: This was called "licking-salt deer" and also called "calling deer."

entries.zh: 舊《志》曰：「契丹之初，草居野次，靡有定所。
entries.en: The old "Treatise" says: "At the beginning of the Khitan they dwelt in grass and lived in the wild, without fixed place.
entries.literal: The old "Treatise" says: "At the beginning of the Khitan, they dwelt in grass and lived in the wild, without fixed place.

entries.zh: 至涅裏始制部族，各有分地。
entries.en: From when Nieli first established the bu system, each had allotted land.
entries.literal: From when Nieli first established the bu system, each had allotted land.

entries.zh: 太祖之興，以叠剌部強熾，析為五院、六院。
entries.en: At Taizu's rise, because the Yilie bu was strong and flourishing, it was divided into Five Courts and Six Courts.
entries.literal: At Taizu's rise, because the Yilie bu was strong and flourishing, it was divided into Five Courts and Six Courts.

entries.zh: 奚六部以下，多因俘降而置。
entries.en: Below the Xi Six bu, most were established from captured and surrendered peoples.
entries.literal: Below the Xi Six bu, most were established from captured and surrendered peoples.

entries.zh: 勝兵甲者即著軍籍，分隸諸路詳穩、統軍、招討司。
entries.en: Those bearing armor as victorious troops were entered in military registers and assigned to the various routes' xiangwen, commanders-in-chief, and pacification commissioners.
entries.literal: Those bearing armor as victorious troops were entered in military registers, assigned to the various routes' xiangwen, commanders-in-chief, and pacification commissioners.

entries.zh: 番居內地者，歲時田牧平莽間。
entries.en: Those dwelling within the interior seasonally plowed and pastured on the level plains.
entries.literal: Those dwelling within the interior seasonally plowed and pastured on the level plains.

entries.zh: 邊防糺戶，生生之資，仰給畜牧，績毛飲湩，以為衣食。
entries.en: Border defense levy households: their livelihood depended on pasturing livestock, combing wool and drinking fermented milk for clothing and food.
entries.literal: Border defense levy households: their livelihood depended on pasturing livestock, combing wool and drinking fermented milk for clothing and food.

entries.zh: 各安舊風，狃習勞事，不見紛華異物而遷。
entries.en: Each kept the old ways, accustomed to labor, not seeing exotic splendors and shifting.
entries.literal: Each kept the old ways, accustomed to labor, not seeing exotic splendors and shifting.

entries.zh: 故家給人足，戎備整完。
entries.en: Thus families were provided for and people sufficient, and military readiness was complete.
entries.literal: Thus families were provided for and people sufficient, military readiness complete.

entries.zh: 卒之虎視四方，強朝弱附，東逾蟠木，西越流沙，莫不率服。
entries.en: In the end they glared like tigers on all four sides, strong states weak and attached; east beyond Panmu, west beyond the drifting sands—all did not fail to submit.
entries.literal: In the end they glared like tigers on all four sides, strong states weak and attached; east beyond Panmu, west beyond the drifting sands—all did not fail to submit.

entries.zh: 部族實為之爪牙雲。」
entries.en: The bu were truly its claws and teeth."
entries.literal: The bu were truly its claws and teeth."

entries.zh: 營衛誌中 ○行營
entries.en: Management of Guards, Part 2 ○ Mobile Camps
entries.literal: Management of Guards, Part 2 ○ Mobile Camps

entries.zh: 國舅別部。
entries.en: Imperial Maternal Uncle separate divisions.
entries.literal: Imperial Maternal Uncle separate divisions.

entries.zh: 太祖二十部，二國舅升帳分，止十八部。
entries.en: Taizu's twenty divisions—with two maternal-uncle divisions elevated to tent status, only eighteen divisions remain.
entries.literal: Taizu's twenty divisions—with two maternal-uncle divisions elevated to tent status, only eighteen divisions remain.

entries.zh: 五院部。
entries.en: Five Divisions Division.
entries.literal: Five Divisions Division.

entries.zh: 其先曰益古，凡六營。
entries.en: Its forebears were called Yigu, comprising six camps in all.
entries.literal: Its forebears were called Yigu, comprising six camps in all.

entries.zh: 阻午可汗時，與弟撒裏本領之，曰叠剌部。
entries.en: At the time of Khan Zuwu, he and his younger brother Saliben led it, called the Dieci Division.
entries.literal: At the time of Khan Zuwu, he and his younger brother Saliben led it, called the Dieci Division.

entries.zh: 傳至太祖，以夷離堇即位。
entries.en: The line passed to Taizu, who took the throne as yilieqin.
entries.literal: Transmitted to Taizu, who took the throne as yilieqin.

entries.zh: 天贊元年，以強大難制，析五石烈為五院，六爪為六院，各置夷離堇。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianzan, because it was strong and hard to control, five shile were split into the Five Divisions and six zhua into the Six Divisions, each with its own yilieqin.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianzan, because it was strong and hard to control, five shile were divided into the Five Divisions and six zhua into the Six Divisions, each with a yilieqin appointed.

entries.zh: 會同元年，更夷離堇為大王。
entries.en: In the first year of Huitong, yilieqin was changed to great king.
entries.literal: In the first year of Huitong, yilieqin was changed to great king.

entries.zh: 部隸北府，以鎮南境。
entries.en: The division was attached to the Northern Court to guard the southern frontier.
entries.literal: The division was attached to the Northern Court to guard the southern frontier.

entries.zh: 大王及都監春夏居五院部之側，秋冬居羊門甸。
entries.en: The great king and superintendent dwelt beside the Five Divisions Division in spring and summer, and at Yangmen Vale in autumn and winter.
entries.literal: The great king and superintendent dwelt beside the Five Divisions Division in spring and summer, and at Yangmen Vale in autumn and winter.

entries.zh: 石烈四：大蔑孤石烈。
entries.en: Four shile: Great Megu shile.
entries.literal: Four shile: Great Megu shile.

entries.zh: 小蔑孤石烈。
entries.en: Lesser Megu shile.
entries.literal: Lesser Megu shile.

entries.zh: 甌昆石烈。
entries.en: Oukun shile.
entries.literal: Oukun shile.

entries.zh: 太宗會同二年，以烏古之地水草豐美，命居之。
entries.en: In Taizong Huitong year 2, because the Wugu lands had rich grass and water, they were ordered to dwell there.
entries.literal: In Taizong Huitong year 2, because the Wugu lands had rich grass and water, they were ordered to dwell there.

entries.zh: 三年，益以海勒水之地為農田。
entries.en: In year 3, the Hail River lands were added as farmland.
entries.literal: In year 3, the Hail River lands were added as farmland.

entries.zh: 乙習本石烈。
entries.en: Yixiben shile.
entries.literal: Yixiben shile.

entries.zh: 會同二年，命以烏古之地。
entries.en: In Huitong year 2, they were ordered to the Wugu lands.
entries.literal: In Huitong year 2, they were ordered to the Wugu lands.

entries.zh: 品部。
entries.en: Pin Division.
entries.literal: Pin Division.

entries.zh: 其先曰拿女手，阻午可汗以其營為部。
entries.en: Its forebears were called Nanshou; Khan Zuwu made his camp a division.
entries.literal: Its forebears were called Nanshou; Khan Zuwu made his camp a division.

entries.zh: 太祖更諸部夷離堇為令穩。
entries.en: Taizu changed all divisions' yilieqin to lingwen.
entries.literal: Taizu changed all divisions' yilieqin to lingwen.

entries.zh: 統和中，又改節度使。
entries.en: In the Tonghe era, they were again changed to military commissioners.
entries.literal: In the Tonghe era, they were again changed to military commissioners.

entries.zh: 隸北府，屬西北路招討司，司徒居太子墳。
entries.en: Attached to the Northern Court, subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission; the sutu dwelt at Crown Prince's Mound.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court, subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission; the sutu dwelt at Crown Prince's Mound.

entries.zh: 凡戍軍隸節度使，留後戶隸司徒。
entries.en: All garrison troops were subordinate to the military commissioner; rear-guard households to the sutu.
entries.literal: All garrison troops were subordinate to the military commissioner; rear-guard households to the sutu.

entries.zh: 石烈二：北哲裏只石烈。
entries.en: Two shile: North Zhelizhi shile.
entries.literal: Two shile: North Zhelizhi shile.

entries.zh: 南轄懶石烈。
entries.en: South Xialan shile.
entries.literal: South Xialan shile.

entries.zh: 突呂不室韋部。
entries.en: Tulubu Shive Division.
entries.literal: Tulubu Shive Division.

entries.zh: 本名大、小二黃室韋戶。
entries.en: Originally called the Greater and Lesser Yellow Shive households.
entries.literal: Originally called the Greater and Lesser Yellow Shive households.

entries.zh: 太祖為達馬狘沙裏，以計降之，乃置為二部。
entries.en: When Taizu was damo bikh shali, he took them by stratagem and then established two divisions.
entries.literal: When Taizu was damo bikh shali, he took them by stratagem and then established two divisions.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬東北路統軍司，戍泰州東北。
entries.en: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning northeast of Taizhou.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning northeast of Taizhou.

entries.zh: 涅剌拿古部。
entries.en: Niela Nage Division.
entries.literal: Niela Nage Division.

entries.zh: 與突呂不室韋部同。
entries.en: Same as the Tulubu Shive Division.
entries.literal: Same as the Tulubu Shive Division.

entries.zh: 節度使戍泰州東。
entries.en: The military commissioner garrisoned east of Taizhou.
entries.literal: The military commissioner garrisoned east of Taizhou.

entries.zh: 叠剌叠達部。
entries.en: Dieci Dieda Division.
entries.literal: Dieci Dieda Division.

entries.zh: 本鮮質可汗所俘奚七百戶，太祖即位，以為十四石烈，置為部。
entries.en: Originally seven hundred Xi households captured by Khan Xianzhi; when Taizu took the throne they were made fourteen shile and established as a division.
entries.literal: Originally seven hundred Xi households captured by Khan Xianzhi; when Taizu took the throne they were made fourteen shile and established as a division.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬西南路招討司，戍黑山北，部民居慶州南。
entries.en: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain; the division's people dwelt south of Qingzhou.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain; the division's people dwelt south of Qingzhou.

entries.zh: 乙室奧隗部。
entries.en: Yishi Aowei Division.
entries.literal: Yishi Aowei Division.

entries.zh: 神冊六年，太祖以所俘奚戶置。
entries.en: In Shence year 6 Taizu established it from captured Xi households.
entries.literal: In Shence year 6 Taizu established it from captured Xi households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬東北路兵馬司。
entries.en: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Military Affairs Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Military Affairs Office.

entries.zh: 楮特奧隗部。
entries.en: Chute Aowei Division.
entries.literal: Chute Aowei Division.

entries.zh: 太祖以奚戶置。
entries.en: Taizu established it from Xi households.
entries.literal: Taizu established it from Xi households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬東京都部署司。
entries.en: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 品達魯虢部。
entries.en: Pindaluwo Division.
entries.literal: Pindaluwo Division.

entries.zh: 太祖以所俘達魯虢部置。
entries.en: Taizu established it from captured Daluwo households.
entries.literal: Taizu established it from captured Daluwo households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬西南路招討司，戍黑山北。
entries.en: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain.

entries.zh: 烏古涅剌部。
entries.en: Wugu Niela Division.
entries.literal: Wugu Niela Division.

entries.zh: 亦曰涅離部。
entries.en: Also called the Nieli Division.
entries.literal: Also called the Nieli Division.

entries.zh: 太祖取於骨裏戶六千，神冊六年，析為烏古涅剌及圖魯二部。
entries.en: Taizu took six thousand Gurli households; in Shence year 6 they were divided into the Wugu Niela and Tulu divisions.
entries.literal: Taizu took six thousand Gurli households; in Shence year 6 they were divided into the Wugu Niela and Tulu divisions.

entries.zh: 俱隸北府，節度使屬西南路招討司。
entries.en: Both attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Both attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Route Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 圖魯部。
entries.en: Tulu Division.
entries.literal: Tulu Division.

entries.zh: 節度使屬東北路統軍司。
entries.en: The military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.
entries.literal: The military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.

entries.zh: 已上太祖以遙輦氏舊部族分置者凡十部，增置者八。
entries.en: Above: ten divisions Taizu placed by dividing the old Yaolian clans; eight newly added.
entries.literal: Above: ten divisions Taizu placed by dividing the old Yaolian clans; eight newly added.

entries.zh: 聖宗三十四部：
entries.en: Shengzong's thirty-four divisions:
entries.literal: Shengzong's thirty-four divisions:

entries.zh: 撒裏葛部。
entries.en: The Salig Division.
entries.literal: Salige Division.

entries.zh: 奚有三營：曰撒裏葛，曰窈爪，曰耨碗爪。
entries.en: The Xi maintained three camps: Salige, Yaozhua, and Nouwanzhua.
entries.literal: The Xi had three camps: called Salige, called Yaozhua, called Nouwanzhua.

entries.zh: 太祖伐奚，乞降，願為著帳子弟。
entries.en: When Taizu attacked the Xi they begged to surrender and wished to become zhuozhang household youths.
entries.literal: When Taizu attacked the Xi they begged surrender and wished to become zhuozhang household youths.

entries.zh: 籍於宮分，皆設夷離堇。
entries.en: They were registered in palace divisions, all were given yilieqin.
entries.literal: Registered in palace divisions, all were given yilieqin.

entries.zh: 聖宗各置為部，改設節度使，皆隸南府，以備畋獵之役。
entries.en: Shengzong made each a separate division, changed to military commissioners, all attached to the Southern Court for hunting service.
entries.literal: Shengzong each established them as divisions, changed to military commissioners, all attached to the Southern Court for hunting service.

entries.zh: 居澤州東。
entries.en: They dwelt east of Ze prefecture.
entries.literal: Dwelling east of Ze prefecture.

entries.zh: 奚王府六部五帳分。
entries.en: The Xi Princely Residence comprised six divisions and five accounts.
entries.literal: Xi Princely Residence: six divisions and five accounts.

entries.zh: 其先曰時瑟，事東遙裏十帳部主哲裏。
entries.en: Formerly there was Shise, who served Zheli, lord of the Eastern Yaoli ten-account division.
entries.literal: Formerly there was Shise, who served Zheli, lord of the Eastern Yaoli ten-account division.

entries.zh: 後逐哲裏，自立為奚王。
entries.en: Later he expelled Zheli and declared himself Xi King.
entries.literal: Later he expelled Zheli and declared himself Xi King.

entries.zh: 卒，弟吐勒斯立。
entries.en: When he died, his younger brother Tulesi succeeded.
entries.literal: When he died, his younger brother Tulesi succeeded.

entries.zh: 遙輦鮮質可汗討之，俘其拒敵者七百戶，摭其降者。
entries.en: Khan Xianzhi of the Yaolian line campaigned against him, capturing seven hundred households of those who resisted and gathering those who surrendered.
entries.literal: Khan Xianzhi of the Yaolian line campaigned against him, capturing seven hundred households of those who resisted and gathering those who surrendered.

entries.zh: 以時瑟鄰睦之故，止俘部曲之半，余悉留焉。
entries.en: Because of Shise's neighborly amity, only half of the followers were taken captive; the rest were all left in place.
entries.literal: Because of Shise's neighborly amity, only half of the followers were taken captive; the rest were all left in place.

entries.zh: 奚勢由是衰矣。
entries.en: Xi power declined from this.
entries.literal: Xi power declined from this.

entries.zh: 初為五部：曰遙裏，曰伯德，曰奧裏，曰梅只，曰楚裏。
entries.en: Initially there were five divisions: Yaoli, Bode, Aoli, Meizhi, and Chuli.
entries.literal: Initially there were five divisions: called Yaoli, Bode, Aoli, Meizhi, and Chuli.

entries.zh: 太祖盡降之，號五部奚。
entries.en: Taizu brought them all to submission and styled them the Five-Division Xi.
entries.literal: Taizu brought them all to submission, calling them the Five-Division Xi.

entries.zh: 天贊二年，有東扒裏廝胡損者，恃險堅壁於箭笴山以拒命，揶諭曰：「大軍何能為，我當飲墮瑰門下矣！」
entries.en: In the second year of Tianzan, Dongbali Si Husun relied on the terrain, fortified himself at Jian'i Mountain to resist the command, and taunted them, saying: "What can the great army do? I shall drink beneath the Duigui Gate!"
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianzan, there was Dongbali Si Husun, who relied on the terrain, fortified himself at Jian'i Mountain to resist the command, and mocked them, saying: "What can the great army do? I shall drink beneath the Duigui Gate!"

entries.zh: 太祖滅之，以奚府給役戶，並括諸部隱丁，收合流散，置墮瑰部，因墮瑰門之語為名，遂號六部奚。
entries.en: Taizu destroyed him, assigned Xi Residence service households, gathered hidden men from the various divisions, collected the scattered, established the Duigui Division, named it for the words about the Duigui Gate, and styled them the Six-Division Xi.
entries.literal: Taizu destroyed him, used Xi Residence service households, also gathered hidden men from the various divisions, collected the scattered, established the Duigui Division, and because of the words about the Duigui Gate took that as the name, then called them the Six-Division Xi.

entries.zh: 命勃魯恩主之，仍號奚王。
entries.en: He appointed Boluen to head it, still styling him Xi King.
entries.literal: He ordered Boluen to head it, still styling him Xi King.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，置宰相、常袞各二員。
entries.en: When Taizong took the throne, he established two chancellors and two changgun for each.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, two chancellors and two changgun were established for each.

entries.zh: 聖宗合奧裏、梅只、墮瑰三部為一；
entries.en: Shengzong merged the Aoli, Meizhi, and Duigui three divisions into one;
entries.literal: Shengzong merged the Aoli, Meizhi, and Duigui three divisions into one;

entries.zh: 特置二克部以足六部之數。
entries.en: he specially established two ke divisions to make up the number of six divisions.
entries.literal: specially established two ke divisions to make up the number of six divisions.

entries.zh: 奚王和朔奴討兀惹，敗績，籍六部隸北府。
entries.en: Xi King Heshuonu campaigned against the Wu'er and was defeated; the six divisions were registered and placed under the Northern Court.
entries.literal: Xi King Heshuonu campaigned against the Wu'er and was defeated; the six divisions were registered and placed under the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 遼起松漠，經營撫納，竟有唐、晉帝王之器，典章文物，施及潢海之區，作史者尚可以故俗語耶？
entries.en: Liao rose from the Songmo desert, cultivated and embraced its subjects, and in the end possessed the stature of Tang and Jin emperors; its institutions and culture reached the Huanghai region—can historians still write in the old tribal tongue?
entries.literal: Liao rose from the Songmo desert, cultivated and embraced subjects, and in the end possessed the capacity of Tang and Jin emperors; its institutions and culture extended to the Huanghai region—can historians still use old tribal vernacular?

entries.zh: 舊史有《部族志》，歷代之所無也。
entries.en: The old histories contained Records of Tribal Divisions, something no previous dynasty had possessed.
entries.literal: The old histories had Records of Tribal Divisions, something no previous dynasty possessed.

entries.zh: 古者，巡守於方嶽，五服之君各述其職，遼之部族實似之。
entries.en: In antiquity the Son of Heaven made tours of the sacred peaks and the lords of the five domains each reported their duties; Liao's tribal divisions truly resembled this.
entries.literal: In antiquity the Son of Heaven toured the sacred peaks and the lords of the five domains each reported their duties; Liao's tribal divisions truly resembled this.

entries.zh: 故以部族置宮衛、行營之後雲。
entries.en: Therefore tribal divisions are placed after palace guards and traveling camps.
entries.literal: Therefore tribal divisions are placed after palace guards and traveling camps.

entries.zh: 特裏特勉部。
entries.en: The Telitemia Division.
entries.literal: Telitemian Division.

entries.zh: 初於八部各析二十戶以戍奚，偵候落馬河及速魯河側，置二十詳穩。
entries.en: Initially twenty households were taken from each of the eight divisions to garrison beside the Luoma and Sulü rivers, with twenty xiangwen established.
entries.literal: At first twenty households were taken from each of the eight divisions to garrison beside the Luoma and Sulü rivers, with twenty xiangwen established.

entries.zh: 聖宗以戶口蕃息，置為部，設節度使。
entries.en: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, set up a division and appointed a military commissioner.
entries.literal: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, established a division and appointed a military commissioner.

entries.zh: 隸南府，戍倒塌嶺，居橐駝岡。
entries.en: It was attached to the Southern Court, garrisoning Daotaling; dwelling at Camel Hillock.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court, garrisoning Daotaling; dwelling at Camel Hillock.

entries.zh: 稍瓦部。
entries.en: The Shaow Division.
entries.literal: Shaowa Division.

entries.zh: 初，取諸宮及橫帳大族奴隸置稍瓦石烈，「稍瓦」，鷹坊也，居遼水東，掌羅捕飛鳥。
entries.en: Initially, slaves from the various palaces and Horizontal Tent great clans were made Shaowa shile; "shaowa" means hawk mews, dwelling east of the Liao River, in charge of netting flying birds.
entries.literal: At first, slaves from the various palaces and Horizontal Tent great clans were made Shaowa shile; "shaowa" means hawk mews, dwelling east of the Liao River, in charge of netting flying birds.

entries.zh: 聖宗以戶口蕃息置部。
entries.en: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, set up a division.
entries.literal: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, established a division.

entries.zh: 節度使屬東京石部署司。
entries.en: Its military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Stone Deployment Office.
entries.literal: The military commissioner was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Stone Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 曷術部，初，取諸宮及橫帳大族奴隸置曷術石烈；
entries.en: Heshu Division; at first, slaves from the various palaces and Horizontal Tent great clans were made Heshu shile; — as above.
entries.literal: Heshu Division; at first, slaves from the various palaces and Horizontal Tent great clans were made Heshu shile;

entries.zh: 「曷術」，鐵也，以冶於海濱柳濕河、三黜古斯、手山。
entries.en: "heshu" means iron, smelted at coastal Willow Wet River, San Chugu, and Shoushan, as recorded above.
entries.literal: "heshu" means iron, smelted at coastal Willow Wet River, San Chugu, and Shoushan.

entries.zh: 聖宗以戶口蕃息置部。
entries.en: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, set up a division.
entries.literal: Shengzong, because households had multiplied, established a division.

entries.zh: 屬東京都部署司。
entries.en: It was subordinate to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.
entries.literal: Subordinate to the Eastern Capital Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 奧裏部。
entries.en: The Aol Division.
entries.literal: Aoli Division.

entries.zh: 統和十二年，以與梅只，墮瑰三部民籍數寡，合為一部。
entries.en: In Tonghe year 12, because the Meizhi, Duigui, and Aoli three divisions had few registered households, the court combined them into one division.
entries.literal: In Tonghe year 12, because the Mei, Duigui, and Zheli three divisions had few registered households, they were combined into one division.

entries.zh: 並上三部，本屬奚王府，聖宗分置。
entries.en: Together with the above three divisions, originally subordinate to the Xi Princely Residence; Shengzong split them off and placed them.
entries.literal: Together with the above three divisions, originally subordinate to the Xi Princely Residence; Shengzong divided and placed them.

entries.zh: 南克部。
entries.en: The South K Division.
entries.literal: South Ke Division.

entries.zh: 北克部。
entries.en: The North K Division.
entries.literal: North Ke Division.

entries.zh: 統和十二年，以奚府二克分置二部。
entries.en: In Tonghe year 12, the Xi Residence's two ke were divided into two divisions — as above.
entries.literal: In Tonghe year 12, the Xi Residence's two ke were divided into two divisions.

entries.zh: 隗衍突厥部。
entries.en: The Weiyan Tuju Division.
entries.literal: Weiyan Tujue Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗析四辟沙、四頗憊戶置，以鎮東北女直之境。
entries.en: Shengzong took households from the four Pisha and four Pibei and set it up to guard the northeastern Jurchen frontier.
entries.literal: Shengzong took households from the four Pisha and four Pibei and established it to guard the northeastern Jurchen frontier.

entries.zh: 開泰九年，節度使奏請置石烈。
entries.en: In Kaitai year 9 the military commissioner memorialized requesting shile be established — as above.
entries.literal: In Kaitai year 9 the military commissioner memorialized requesting shile be established.

entries.zh: 隸北府，屬黃龍府都部署司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court, subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court, subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 奧衍突厥部。
entries.en: The Aoyan Tuju Division.
entries.literal: Aoyan Tujue Division.

entries.zh: 與隗衍突厥同。
entries.en: Like the Weiyan Tujue.
entries.literal: Same as Weiyan Tujue.

entries.zh: 奧衍女直部。
entries.en: The Aoyan Jurche Division.
entries.literal: Aoyan Jurchen Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以女直戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Jurchen households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Jurchen households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬西北路招討司，戍鎮州境。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning the Zhenzhou frontier.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission, garrisoning the Zhenzhou frontier.

entries.zh: 自此至河西部，皆俘獲諸國之民，初隸諸宮，戶口蕃息置部。
entries.en: From here to the River West Division, all were peoples of captured states; were at first attached to the various palaces; when households multiplied, divisions were established.
entries.literal: From here to the River West Division, all were peoples of captured states; at first subordinate to the various palaces; when households multiplied, divisions were established.

entries.zh: 訖於五國，皆有節度使。
entries.en: Through the Five States, each had a military commissioner.
entries.literal: Down to the Five States, all had military commissioners.

entries.zh: 乙典女直部。
entries.en: The Yidian Jurche Division.
entries.literal: Yidian Jurchen Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以女直戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Jurchen households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Jurchen households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，居高州北。
entries.en: It was attached to the Southern Court, dwelling north of Gaozhou.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court, dwelling north of Gaozhou.

entries.zh: 斡突碗烏古部。
entries.en: The Wotuwan Wug Division.
entries.literal: Wotuwan Wugu Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以烏古戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Wugu households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Wugu households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬西南面招討司，戍黑山北。
entries.en: It was attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission, garrisoning north of Black Mountain.

entries.zh: 叠魯敵烈部。
entries.en: The Dielu Dili Division.
entries.literal: Dielu Dilie Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以敵烈戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Dilie households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Dilie households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬烏古敵烈統軍司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Wugu-Dilie Commander-in-Chief Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Wugu-Dilie Commander-in-Chief Office.

entries.zh: 室韋部。
entries.en: The Shiv Division.
entries.literal: Shive Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以室韋戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Shive households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Shive households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬西北路招討司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northwest Route Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 術哲達魯虢部。
entries.en: The Shuzhe Daluw Division.
entries.literal: Shuzhe Daluwo Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以達魯虢戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Daluwo households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Daluwo households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬東北路統軍司，戍境內，居境外。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning within the frontier while dwelling beyond it.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning within the frontier while dwelling beyond it.

entries.zh: 梅古悉部。
entries.en: The Meigus Division.
entries.literal: Meigusi Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以唐古戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Tangut households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Tangut households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬西南面招討司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 頡的部。
entries.en: The Xied Division.
entries.literal: Xiedi Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以唐古戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Tangut households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Tangut households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬西南面招討司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 北敵烈部。
entries.en: The North Dili Division.
entries.literal: North Dilie Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以敵烈戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Dilie households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Dilie households.

entries.zh: 戍隗烏古部。
entries.en: Garrisoning the Wei Wugu Division.
entries.literal: Garrisoning the Wugu Wugu Division.

entries.zh: 匿訖唐古部。
entries.en: The Niji Tangg Division.
entries.literal: Niji Tanggu Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗置。
entries.en: Shengzong established the division.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬西南面招討司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 北唐古部。
entries.en: The North Tangg Division.
entries.literal: North Tanggu Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以唐古戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Tangut households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Tangut households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬黃龍府都部署司，戍府南。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office, garrisoning south of the prefecture.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office, garrisoning south of the prefecture.

entries.zh: 南唐古部。
entries.en: The South Tangg Division.
entries.literal: South Tanggu Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗置。
entries.en: Shengzong established the division.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it.

entries.zh: 隸北府。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court.

entries.zh: 鶴剌唐古部。
entries.en: The Hela Tanggu Division.
entries.literal: Hela Tanggu Division.

entries.zh: 與南唐古同。
entries.en: Like the South Tanggu.
entries.literal: Same as South Tanggu.

entries.zh: 節度使屬西南面招討司。
entries.en: Its military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.
entries.literal: The military commissioner was subordinate to the Southwest Pacification Commission.

entries.zh: 河西部。
entries.en: The River Wes Division.
entries.literal: River West Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗置。
entries.en: Shengzong established the division.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬東北路統軍司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.

entries.zh: 薛特部。
entries.en: The Xit Division.
entries.literal: Xite Division.

entries.zh: 開泰四年，以回鶻戶置。
entries.en: In Kaitai year 4 set up from Uyghur households.
entries.literal: In Kaitai year 4 established from Uyghur households.

entries.zh: 隸北府，居慈仁縣北。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court, dwelling north of Ciren county.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court, dwelling north of Ciren county.

entries.zh: 伯斯鼻骨德部。
entries.en: The Bosi Bigud Division.
entries.literal: Bosi Bigude Division.

entries.zh: 本鼻骨德戶。
entries.en: They were originally Bigude households.
entries.literal: Originally Bigude households.

entries.zh: 初隸諸宮，聖宗以戶口蕃息置部。
entries.en: At first they were attached to the various palaces; Shengzong, because households had multiplied, established a division.
entries.literal: At first subordinate to the various palaces; Shengzong, because households had multiplied, established a division.

entries.zh: 隸北府，節度使屬東北路統軍司，戍境內，居境外。
entries.en: It was attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning within the frontier while dwelling beyond it.
entries.literal: Attached to the Northern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office, garrisoning within the frontier while dwelling beyond it.

entries.zh: 達馬鼻骨德部。
entries.en: The Dama Bigud Division.
entries.literal: Dama Bigude Division.

entries.zh: 聖宗以鼻骨德戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong set it up from Bigude households.
entries.literal: Shengzong established it from Bigude households.

entries.zh: 隸南府，節度使屬東北路統軍司。
entries.en: It was attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.
entries.literal: Attached to the Southern Court; the military commissioner was subordinate to the Northeast Route Commander-in-Chief Office.

entries.zh: 五國部。
entries.en: The Five State Division.
entries.literal: Five States Division.

entries.zh: 剖阿裏國、盆奴裏國、奧裏米國、越裏篤國、越裏吉國，聖宗時來附，命居本土，以鎮東北境，屬黃龍府都部署司。
entries.en: Poali state, Punnuli state, Aolimi state, Yuelidu state, and Yueliji state—in Shengzong's time came to attach; they were ordered to dwell in their homelands to guard the northeast frontier, subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office — as above.
entries.literal: Poali state, Punnuli state, Aolimi state, Yuelidu state, and Yueliji state—in Shengzong's time came to attach; they were ordered to dwell in their homelands to guard the northeast frontier, subordinate to the Huanglong Prefecture Deployment Office.

entries.zh: 重熙六年，以越裏吉國人尚海等訴酋帥渾尚貪汙，罷五國酋帥，設節度使以領之。
entries.en: In Chongxi year 6, because the Yueliji people Shang Hai and others accused chieftain Hunshang of corruption, the Five States chieftains were abolished and military commissioners appointed to lead them, as recorded above.
entries.literal: In Chongxi year 6, because the Yueliji people Shang Hai and others accused chieftain Hunshang of corruption, the Five States chieftains were abolished and military commissioners appointed to lead them.

entries.zh: 已上聖宗以舊部族置者十六，增置十八。
entries.en: Above: sixteen divisions Shengzong placed from old tribal groups; eighteen newly added — as above.
entries.literal: Above: sixteen divisions Shengzong placed from old tribal groups; eighteen newly added.

entries.zh: 營衛誌下部族下
entries.en: Management of Guards, Part 3 ○ Tribal Divisions, Part 2
entries.literal: Management of Guards, Part 3 ○ Tribal Divisions, Part 2

entries.zh: 軒轅氏合符東海，邑於涿鹿之阿，遷徙往來無常處，以兵為營衛。
entries.en: The Yellow Emperor united tally-signs at the Eastern Sea and settled at Zhuolu; the people moved without fixed homes and took the army as camp and guard.
entries.literal: The Yellow Emperor combined tally-signs at the Eastern Sea, settled at the ford of Zhuolu, migrated without fixed abode, and used troops as camp and guard.

entries.zh: 飛狐以北，無慮以東，西暨流沙，四戰之地，聖人猶不免於兵衛，地勢然耳。
entries.en: From north of Feihu to east of Wulü and west to the drifting sands lay a land fought on every side; even a sage could not do without military guard—such was the terrain.
entries.literal: North of Feihu, east of Wulü, west to the drifting sands—a land of four-sided warfare; even a sage could not escape military guard; such was the terrain.

entries.zh: 遼國左都遼海，右邑涿鹿，兵力莫強焉。
entries.en: The Liao state had Liaohai on the left and Zhuolu on the right; in military power none was stronger.
entries.literal: The Liao state held its left at Liaohai and its right at Zhuolu; nowhere was military strength stronger.

entries.zh: 其在隋世，依紇臣水而居，分為十部。
entries.en: During the Sui they lived by the Heichen River and were split into ten divisions.
entries.literal: In Sui times they dwelt along the Heichen River and were divided into ten divisions.

entries.zh: 兵多者三千，少者千餘。
entries.en: The larger divisions mustered three thousand men, the smaller a little over a thousand.
entries.literal: Where troops were many there were three thousand; where few, a little over a thousand.

entries.zh: 順寒暑，逐水草畜牧。
entries.en: They followed the seasons, moved with water and pasture, and raised herds.
entries.literal: They followed cold and heat, pursued water and grass, and pastured livestock.

entries.zh: 侵伐則十部相與議，興兵致役，合契而後動，獵則部得自行。
entries.en: For invasion the ten divisions met in council; to raise armies and levy service they joined tally-signs before marching, but on the hunt each division went its own way.
entries.literal: On raids the ten divisions deliberated together; to raise troops and impose service they united tally-signs before moving; on the hunt each division acted on its own.

entries.zh: 至唐，大賀氏勝兵四萬三千人，分為八部。
entries.en: Under the Tang the Dahe clan fielded forty-three thousand fighting men in eight divisions.
entries.literal: By Tang times the Dahe clan had forty-three thousand able troops, divided into eight divisions.

entries.zh: 大賀氏中衰，僅存五部。
entries.en: When the Dahe clan waned, only five divisions survived.
entries.literal: The Dahe clan declined; only five divisions remained.

entries.zh: 有耶律雅裏者，分五部為八，立二府以總之，析三耶律氏為七，二審密氏為五，凡二十部。
entries.en: Yelü Yali split the five divisions into eight, set up two offices to oversee them, broke three Yelü lineages into seven and two Shenmi lineages into five—twenty divisions in all.
entries.literal: Yelü Yali divided the five into eight, established two offices to command them, split three Yelü clans into seven and two Shenmi clans into five—twenty divisions in all.

entries.zh: 刻木為契，政令大行。
entries.en: Wooden tallies were carved for contracts, and government orders ran through the land.
entries.literal: They carved wood for tally-contracts and government orders were widely enforced.

entries.zh: 遜不有國，乃立遙輦氏代大賀氏，兵力益振，即太祖六世祖也。
entries.en: When Xun lost the realm the Yaolian clan replaced the Dahe and military power swelled—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation forebear.
entries.literal: Xun did not hold the state; the Yaolian clan was raised to replace the Dahe, military strength grew ever stronger—this was the Taizu's sixth-generation ancestor.

entries.zh: 及太祖會李克用於雲中，以兵三十萬，盛矣。
entries.en: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong his host numbered three hundred thousand—a formidable army.
entries.literal: When the Taizu met Li Keyong at Yunzhong he had three hundred thousand troops—mighty indeed.

entries.zh: 遙輦耶瀾可汗十年，歲在辛酉，太祖授鉞專征，破室韋、於厥、奚三國，俘獲廬帳，不可勝紀。
entries.en: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu was given the battle-axe and sole command; he crushed the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi and took tents and households past numbering.
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Yaonian Yelang Khan, the year xinyou, the Taizu received the battle-axe with sole command, broke the Shiwei, Yujue, and Xi states, and captured tents and households beyond counting.

entries.zh: 十月，授大叠烈府夷離堇，明賞罰，繕甲兵，休息民庶，滋蕃群牧，務在戢兵。
entries.en: In the tenth month he became yilijin of the Dayielie Office: rewards and punishments were made clear, arms were readied, the people were rested, herds were enlarged, and the aim was to still the armies.
entries.literal: In the tenth month he was appointed yilijin of the Dayielie Office, made rewards and punishments clear, repaired armor and weapons, let the people rest, increased the herds, and strove to curb warfare.

entries.zh: 十一年，總兵四十萬伐代北，克郡縣九，俘九萬五千口。
entries.en: In the eleventh year he led four hundred thousand men against northern Dai, seized nine commanderies and counties, and took ninety-five thousand captives.
entries.literal: In the eleventh year he commanded four hundred thousand troops to attack northern Dai, took nine commanderies and counties, and captured ninety-five thousand persons.

entries.zh: 十二年，德祖討奚，俘七千戶。
entries.en: In the twelfth year Dezu campaigned against the Xi and took seven thousand households.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year Dezu attacked the Xi and captured seven thousand households.

entries.zh: 十五年，遙輦可汗卒，遺命遜位於太祖。
entries.en: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and commanded that rule pass to the Taizu.
entries.literal: In the fifteenth year the Yaonian khan died and left orders that the throne pass to the Taizu.

entries.zh: 太祖即位五年，討西奚、東奚，悉平之，盡有奚、霫之眾。
entries.en: In the fifth year of his reign the Taizu attacked western and eastern Xi, subdued them entirely, and held all the Xi and Xí peoples.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of the Taizu's reign he attacked the western and eastern Xi, pacified them all, and wholly possessed the Xi and Xí peoples.

entries.zh: 六年春，親征幽州，東西旌旗相望，亙數百里。
entries.en: In the spring of the sixth year he led a personal campaign on Youzhou; banners east and west stretched for hundreds of li.
entries.literal: In the sixth spring he personally campaigned against Youzhou; eastern and western banners faced one another for several hundred li.

entries.zh: 所經郡縣，望風皆下，俘獲甚眾，振旅而還。
entries.en: Commanderies and counties along the route surrendered at his approach; booty was immense, and he marched home in triumph.
entries.literal: Every commandery and county he passed submitted at sight; captives were very many, and he returned in triumph.

entries.zh: 秋，親征背陰國，俘獲數萬計。
entries.en: That autumn he personally attacked the Beiyin state and took captives numbering in the tens of thousands.
entries.literal: In autumn he personally campaigned against the Beiyin state and captured tens of thousands.

entries.zh: 神冊元年，親征突厥、吐渾、党項、小蕃、沙陀諸部，俘戶一萬五千六百；
entries.en: In the first year of Shence he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo and took fifteen thousand six hundred households;
entries.literal: In the first year of Shence he personally campaigned against the Türks, Tuyuhun, Tangut, lesser tribes, and Shatuo—fifteen thousand six hundred households captured;

entries.zh: 攻振武，乘勝而東，攻蔚、新、武、媯、儒五州，俘獲不可勝紀，斬不從命者萬四千七百級。
entries.en: he stormed Zhenwu, drove east on the momentum, overran Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, took booty past counting, and slew fourteen thousand seven hundred who refused submission.
entries.literal: he attacked Zhenwu, pressed east on the momentum, attacked the five prefectures of Wei, Xin, Wu, Gui, and Ru, captured beyond counting, and beheaded fourteen thousand seven hundred who would not obey.

entries.zh: 盡有代北、河曲、陰山之眾，遂取山北八軍。
entries.en: He held all the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, then seized the eight armies north of the mountains.
entries.literal: He wholly possessed the peoples of northern Dai, the river bend, and the Yin Mountains, and then took the eight armies north of the mountains.

entries.zh: 四年，親征於骨裏國，俘獲一萬四千二百口。
entries.en: In the fourth year he personally attacked the Yuguri state and took fourteen thousand two hundred captives.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he personally campaigned against the Yuguri state and captured fourteen thousand two hundred persons.

entries.zh: 五年，征党項，俘獲二千六百口。
entries.en: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and took two thousand six hundred captives.
entries.literal: In the fifth year he campaigned against the Tangut and captured two thousand six hundred persons.

entries.zh: 攻天德軍，拔十有二柵，徙其民。
entries.en: He assailed the Tiande Army, carried twelve stockades, and relocated the inhabitants.
entries.literal: He attacked the Tiande Army, took twelve stockades, and moved the people away.

entries.zh: 六年，出居庸關，分兵掠檀、順等州，安遠軍、三河、良鄉、望都、潞、滿城、遂城等縣，俘其民徙內地，皇太子略定州，俘獲甚眾。
entries.en: In the sixth year he issued through Juyong Pass, sent columns to raid Tan, Shun, and other prefectures and Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland, while the crown prince overran Dingzhou with great booty.
entries.literal: In the sixth year he went out through Juyong Pass, divided troops to plunder Tan, Shun, and other prefectures, Anyuan Army, Sanhe, Liangxiang, Wangdu, Lu, Mancheng, Suicheng, and other counties, moved captives inland; the crown prince overran Dingzhou and took very many captives.

entries.zh: 天贊元年，以戶口滋繁，糺轄疏遠，分北大濃兀為二部，立兩節度以統之。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianzan, as households multiplied and oversight grew thin, northern Da Nongwu was divided in two and two commissioners were appointed to command them.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianzan, because households had grown numerous and control was loose, northern Da Nongwu was split into two divisions and two military commissioners were set to command them.

entries.zh: 三年，西征党項等國，俘獲不可勝紀。
entries.en: In the third year he marched west against the Tangut and other states and took captives past numbering.
entries.literal: In the third year he campaigned west against the Tangut and other states; captives were beyond counting.

entries.zh: 四年，又親征渤海。
entries.en: In the fourth year he again led a personal campaign against Bohai.
entries.literal: In the fourth year he again personally campaigned against Bohai.

entries.zh: 天顯元年，滅渤海國，地方五千里，兵數十萬，五京、十五府、六十二州，盡有其眾，契丹益大。
entries.en: In the first year of Tianxian he destroyed Bohai—five thousand li of territory, armies in the hundreds of thousands, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, and sixty-two districts—and held all their people; Khitan power swelled further.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianxian he destroyed the Bohai state—territory five thousand li, troops several hundred thousand, five capitals, fifteen prefectures, sixty-two prefectures—and wholly possessed their peoples; the Khitan grew greater still.

entries.zh: 會同初，太宗滅唐立晉，晉獻燕、代十六州，民眾兵強，莫之能禦矣。
entries.en: At the opening of Huitong the Taizong ended Tang and raised Jin; Jin surrendered Yan and Dai's sixteen prefectures—populous lands and strong armies that none could resist.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong the Taizong destroyed Tang and established Jin; Jin offered the sixteen prefectures of Yan and Dai—the people numerous and troops strong, none could withstand them.

entries.zh: 凡舉兵，帝率蕃漢文武臣僚，以青牛白馬祭告天地、日神，惟不拜月，分命近臣告太祖以下諸陵及木葉山神，乃詔諸道征兵。
entries.en: When armies were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han officials, offered blue ox and white horse to Heaven, Earth, and the sun—never the moon—and sent close ministers to report to the tombs from the Taizu onward and to Mount Muye's god before decreeing levies on every circuit.
entries.literal: Whenever troops were raised the emperor led Khitan and Han civil and military officials, sacrificed with blue ox and white horse to Heaven and Earth and the sun god—only not bowing to the moon—and separately ordered close ministers to announce to the tombs from the Taizu down and to the god of Mount Muye, then decreed levies from every circuit.

entries.zh: 惟南、北、奚王，東京渤海兵馬，燕京統軍兵馬，雖奉詔，末敢發兵，必以聞。
entries.en: Even the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai forces, and Yanjing commander's troops, though they received the decree, would not march until they had reported to the throne.
entries.literal: Only the southern king, northern king, Xi king, Eastern Capital Bohai troops, and Yanjing commander-in-chief's troops—though they received the decree—dared not march until they had reported.

entries.zh: 上遣大將持金魚符，合，然後行。
entries.en: The court sent a great general with the gold fish tally; only when the tallies joined did the columns march.
entries.literal: The court dispatched a great general bearing the gold fish tally; only when tallies matched did they move.

entries.zh: 始聞詔，攢戶丁，推戶力，核籍齊眾以待。
entries.en: On first hearing the decree they mustered household men, weighed each household's capacity, reconciled registers, and assembled the host to wait.
entries.literal: At first word of the decree they gathered household men, weighed household strength, checked registers, and mustered the host to wait.

entries.zh: 自十將以上，次第點集軍馬、器仗。
entries.en: From leaders of ten men upward they mustered troops and weapons in due order.
entries.literal: From commanders of ten upward they mustered troops and gear in sequence.

entries.zh: 符至，兵馬本司自領，使者不得與。
entries.en: When the tally arrived the home bureau itself led the troops; the envoy might not take them over.
entries.literal: When the tally arrived the original bureau led the troops itself; envoys might not take command.

entries.zh: 唯再共點軍馬訖，又以上聞。
entries.en: Only after a second joint muster of troops and gear did they report upward.
entries.literal: Only after jointly counting the troops again did they report upward.

entries.zh: 量兵馬多少，再命使充軍主，與本司互相監督。
entries.en: They gauged the host's size and again named an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.
entries.literal: According to the size of the force they again appointed an envoy as army commander to supervise jointly with the home bureau.

entries.zh: 又請引五方旗鼓，然後皇帝親點將校。
entries.en: They also called for the five-direction banners and drums; only then did the emperor personally review the officers.
entries.literal: They also requested the five-direction banners and drums; then the emperor personally inspected officers.

entries.zh: 又選勛戚大臣，充行營兵馬都統、副都統、都監各一人。
entries.en: Meritorious kin and great ministers were chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one of each.
entries.literal: Meritorious kin and great ministers were again chosen as camp army commander, deputy commander, and overseer, one each.

entries.zh: 又選諸軍兵馬尤精銳者三萬人為護駕軍，又選驍勇三千人為先鋒軍，又選剽悍百人之上為遠探欄子軍，以上各有將領。
entries.en: From all armies thirty thousand elite troops formed the imperial guard; three thousand daring men the vanguard; bands of a hundred or more of the boldest the distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its officers.
entries.literal: From every army the finest thirty thousand were chosen as the imperial guard corps; three thousand bold men as vanguard; groups of a hundred or more of the fiercest as distant-scout barricade horse corps—each with its own officers.

entries.zh: 又於諸軍每部。
entries.en: Again, within each army unit:
entries.literal: Again in each army unit.

entries.zh: 量眾寡，抽十人或五人，合為一隊，別立將領，以備勾取兵馬，騰遞公事。
entries.en: By strength, five or ten men were taken from each unit, formed into a squad under its own leader, to levy troops and carry urgent dispatches.
entries.literal: According to numbers, five or ten men were drawn from each unit, formed into a squad with its own leader, to requisition troops and relay official business.

entries.zh: 兵衛誌上
entries.en: Military Guards, Part 1
entries.literal: Military Guards, Part 1

entries.zh: 漢武帝多行幸之事，置期門、佽飛、羽林之目，天子始有親軍。
entries.en: Emperor Wu of Han made many inspection tours and created the Qimen, Cifei, and Yulin corps—the Son of Heaven first gained a personal guard army.
entries.literal: Han Emperor Wu often traveled on inspection tours and established the titles Qimen, Cifei, and Yulin; the Son of Heaven first had a personal guard army.

entries.zh: 唐太宗加親、勛、翊、千牛之衛，布腹心之地，防衛密矣。
entries.en: Emperor Taizong of Tang added the Qin, Xun, Yi, and Qianniu guards and stationed them in the imperial core; the protective screen grew tight indeed.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Taizong added the Qin, Xun, Yi, and Qianniu guards, posting them in the heartland; defense became dense indeed.

entries.zh: 遼太祖宗室盛強，分叠剌部為二，宮衛內虛，經營四方，未遑鳩集。
entries.en: At Liao Taizu's rise the imperial clan was powerful; he divided the Dieci tribe in two, leaving the inner palace guard thin, and while campaigning on every side had no time to muster troops.
entries.literal: When Liao Taizu rose the imperial clan was strong; he split the Dieci tribe in two, the inner palace guard was hollow, and while he campaigned on four sides he had no leisure to gather forces.

entries.zh: 皇后述律氏居守之際，摘蕃漢精銳為屬珊軍。
entries.en: While Empress Shulü kept guard at the capital she selected elite Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.
entries.literal: While Empress Shulü held the capital, she picked the finest of Fan and Han troops for the shushan army.

entries.zh: 太宗益選天下精甲，置諸爪牙為皮室軍。
entries.en: Taizong further culled the realm's finest armor-bearers and set them at claw and fang as the pishi army.
entries.literal: Taizong further chose the finest armor in the realm and placed them at his claws and teeth as the pishi army.

entries.zh: 合騎五十萬，國威壯矣。
entries.en: Combined they fielded five hundred thousand riders; national might stood full and grand.
entries.literal: Together they mustered five hundred thousand horsemen; the state's prestige was majestic.

entries.zh: 太祖以叠剌部受禪，分本部為五院、六院，統以皇族，而親衛缺然。
entries.en: Taizu took the mandate through the Dieci tribe, split the original tribe into Five Courts and Six Courts under imperial-clan control, yet personal guards were still wanting.
entries.literal: Taizu received the mandate through the Dieci tribe, divided the original tribe into Five Courts and Six Courts, and governed them with the imperial clan—yet personal guards were still lacking.

entries.zh: 乃立斡魯朵法，裂州縣，割戶丁，以強幹弱支。
entries.en: He then set up the orudo law, split prefectures and counties, and drew off household men to strengthen the center and weaken the periphery.
entries.literal: He then established the orudo law, carved up prefectures and counties, and cut off household men to strengthen the trunk and weaken the branches.

entries.zh: 詒謀嗣績，世建宮衛。
entries.en: Plans were handed down and achievements continued; palace guards were raised generation after generation.
entries.literal: Plans were entrusted and achievements inherited; generation after generation palace guards were built.

entries.zh: 入則居守，出則扈從，葬則因以守陵。
entries.en: Within they held the capital; abroad they escorted the ruler; at burial they were posted to guard the tombs.
entries.literal: When within they guarded the residence; when without they escorted on campaign; at burial they accordingly guarded the tombs.

entries.zh: 有兵事，則五京、二州各提轄司傳檄而集，不待調發州縣、部族，十萬騎軍已立具矣。
entries.en: In time of war each supervisory office of the Five Capitals and Two Prefectures passed orders and gathered troops; without waiting on prefectures, counties, or tribes, a hundred thousand cavalry were already formed.
entries.literal: When there was war, each supervisory office of the Five Capitals and Two Prefectures transmitted orders and assembled troops; without waiting to mobilize prefectures, counties, or tribes, a hundred thousand riders stood ready.

entries.zh: 恩意親洽，兵甲犀利，教練完習。
entries.en: Affection ran close, arms were keen, and drill was thorough and practiced.
entries.literal: Grace and affection were intimate, weapons and armor sharp, training complete and practiced.

entries.zh: 簡天下精銳，聚之腹心之中。
entries.en: The realm's elite were culled and massed in the imperial core.
entries.literal: The finest in the realm were selected and gathered into the belly and heart.

entries.zh: 懷舊者歲深，增新者世盛。
entries.en: Old loyalties deepened year by year; new strength waxed with every generation.
entries.literal: Those cherished from old grew deeper with the years; new additions flourished with each generation.

entries.zh: 此軍制之良者也。
entries.en: Such was the excellence of this army system.
entries.literal: This was the excellence of the army system.

entries.zh: 兵衛誌中 ○禦帳親軍
entries.en: Military Guards, Part 2 — Imperial Tent Guard Armies
entries.literal: Military Guards, Part 2 ○ Imperial Tent Guard Armies

entries.zh: 太祖建皇都於臨潢府。
entries.en: Taizu founded the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.
entries.literal: Taizu built the imperial capital at Linhuang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 太宗定晉，晉主石敬瑭來獻十六城，乃定四京，改皇都為上京。
entries.en: When Taizong pacified Jin, Shi Jingtang of Later Jin ceded sixteen prefectures; the court then fixed four capitals and renamed the imperial seat Shangjing.
entries.literal: Taizong settled Jin; Jin ruler Shi Jingtang presented sixteen prefectures, then four capitals were fixed and the imperial capital was renamed Shangjing.

entries.zh: 有丁一十六萬七千二百。
entries.en: Shangjing mustered 167,200 levies.
entries.literal: It had one hundred sixty-seven thousand two hundred ding.

entries.zh: 遼之為國，鄰於梁、唐、晉、漢、周、宋。
entries.en: Liao bordered in turn Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.
entries.literal: As a state Liao neighbored Liang, Tang, Jin, Han, Zhou, and Song.

entries.zh: 晉以恩故，始則父子一家，終則寇讎相攻；
entries.en: With Later Jin the bond began as kin-by-grace yet closed in mutual raids;
entries.literal: Jin began as father and son in one household because of favor, yet ended with raiding and mutual attack;

entries.zh: 梁、唐、周隱然一敵國；
entries.en: Liang, Tang, and Zhou each stood as a full rival power.
entries.literal: Liang, Tang, and Zhou were plainly one enemy state each.

entries.zh: 宋惟太宗征北漢，遼不能救，餘多敗衄，縱得亦不償失。
entries.en: Only when Song's Taizong campaigned against Northern Han could Liao not save it; otherwise Song mostly lost, and even victories did not repay the cost.
entries.literal: Song only in Taizong's northern Han campaign did Liao fail to save them; most other clashes ended in defeat, and even victories did not repay the cost.

entries.zh: 良由石晉獻土，中國失五關之固然也。
entries.en: The root cause was Shi Jingtang's land grant and the Central States' forfeiture of the five passes' natural defenses.
entries.literal: This truly stemmed from Shi Jingtang's cession of territory and China's loss of the five passes' natural strength.

entries.zh: 高麗小邦，屢喪遼兵，非以險阻足恃故歟。
entries.en: Small Goryeo still drained Liao forces again and again—perhaps its rugged ground alone could explain it.
entries.literal: Goryeo was a small state yet repeatedly cost Liao armies—was it not because its difficult terrain was sufficient to rely on?

entries.zh: 西夏彈丸之地，南敗宋，東抗遼。
entries.en: Western Xia, though minute, beat Song to the south and held Liao at bay in the east.
entries.literal: Western Xia was a tiny realm yet defeated Song in the south and resisted Liao in the east.

entries.zh: 雖西北士馬雄勁，元昊、諒祚智勇過人，能使党項、阻卜掣肘大國，蓋亦襟山帶河，有以助其勢耳。
entries.en: Even with strong northwestern cavalry, Yuanhao and Liangzuo's talent let Tangut and Zubu allies tie down a great empire, aided by mountains and rivers at their flank.
entries.literal: Though northwestern horses and warriors were strong, Yuanhao and Liangzuo were surpassingly clever and brave, enabling Tangut and Zubu forces to check a great power—surely mountains and rivers at their backs helped their momentum.

entries.zh: 雖然，宋久失地利，而舊《志》言兵，唯以敵宋為務。
entries.en: Yet Song had lost terrain for years while older records still framed warfare chiefly against Song.
entries.literal: Even so, Song long lacked terrain advantage, yet the old Monograph on troops treated Song alone as the enemy.

entries.zh: 逾三關，聚議北京，猶不敢輕進。
entries.en: Even after crossing the three passes and gathering councils at Beijing, Liao hesitated to push forward.
entries.literal: Crossing three passes and massing councils at Beijing, they still dared not advance lightly.

entries.zh: 豈不以大河在前，三鎮在後，臨事好謀之審，不容不然歟。
entries.en: With the Yellow River ahead and the three prefectures behind, cautious planning at the crisis point left no other choice.
entries.literal: Was it not because the Yellow River lay ahead and the three garrisons behind, and careful counsel at the moment could not permit otherwise?

entries.zh: 東京，本渤海，以其地建南京遼陽府。
entries.en: The Eastern Capital began as Bohai; the Liao built Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture on that ground.
entries.literal: Eastern Capital: originally Bohai; its territory became Nanjing Liaoyang Prefecture.

entries.zh: 統縣六，轄軍、府、州、城二十六，有丁四萬一千四百。
entries.en: It ruled six counties and twenty-six military prefectures and cities, with 41,400 levies on the rolls.
entries.literal: It governed six counties, twenty-six armies, prefectures, and walled posts, with forty-one thousand four hundred ding.

entries.zh: 天顯十三年，太宗改為東京。
entries.en: In Tianxian year 13 Taizong redesignated it the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: In the thirteenth year of Tianxian, Taizong renamed it Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 聖宗統和二十三年，城七金山，建大定府，號中京。
entries.en: Shengzong's Tonghe year 23 saw Qijin Mountain fortified and Zhongjing established at Dading Prefecture.
entries.literal: In the twenty-third year of Tonghe, Shengzong walled Qijin Mountain and founded Zhongjing at Dading Prefecture.

entries.zh: 統縣九，轄軍、府、州、城二十三。
entries.en: Zhongjing governed nine counties and twenty-three military prefectures and posts.
entries.literal: It governed nine counties and twenty-three armies, prefectures, and cities.

entries.zh: 草創末定，丁籍莫考，可見者一縣：高州三韓縣丁一萬。
entries.en: Because the seat was newly founded, levies were not fully tallied; only Gaozhou's Sanhan County is recorded at 10,000 ding.
entries.literal: Still in early founding and not yet fixed; ding rolls were unverified—only one county is visible: Gaozhou Sanhan County, ten thousand ding.

entries.zh: 兵衛誌下 ○五京鄉丁
entries.en: Military Guards, Part 3 — Five Capitals Militia Levies
entries.literal: Military Guards, Part 3 ○ Five Capitals Militia Levies

entries.zh: 中京大定府，虞為營州，夏屬冀州，周在幽州之分。
entries.en: Dading Prefecture at Zhongjing had been Ying Prefecture under Yu, Ji territory under Xia, and part of You under Zhou.
entries.literal: Zhongjing, Dading Prefecture—in Yu's time it was Ying Prefecture; in Xia it belonged to Ji; in Zhou it lay within You's division.

entries.zh: 秦郡天下，是為遼西。
entries.en: When Qin organized the empire into commanderies, the region became Liaoxi.
entries.literal: Qin divided the realm into commanderies; this was Liaoxi.

entries.zh: 漢為新安平縣。
entries.en: In Han times it was Xin'anping County.
entries.literal: Under Han it was Xin'anping County.

entries.zh: 漢末步奚居之，幅員千里，多大山深谷，阻險足以自固。
entries.en: In late Han the Bu Xi occupied the land, a thousand-li tract of high mountains and deep valleys whose passes let them stand on their own.
entries.literal: At the end of Han the Bu Xi dwelt here; the domain ran a thousand li, with many great mountains and deep valleys—defiles enough to hold themselves secure.

entries.zh: 魏武北征，縱兵大戰，降者一十餘萬，去之松漠。
entries.en: On his northern campaign Cao Cao fought a major engagement; over one hundred thousand men surrendered and were removed to Songmo.
entries.literal: Wei Wu-di on his northern campaign loosed troops in great battle; more than a hundred thousand surrendered and were sent away to Songmo.

entries.zh: 其後拓拔氏乘遼建牙於此，當饒樂河水之南，溫渝河水之北。
entries.en: Later the Tuoba, exploiting turmoil in Liaodong, pitched their headquarters here between the Raole and Wenyu rivers.
entries.literal: Later the Tuoba clan, seizing the moment in Liaodong, set their headquarters here—south of the Raole River, north of the Wenyu River.

entries.zh: 唐太宗伐高麗，駐蹕於此。
entries.en: Tang Taizong campaigned against Goryeo and encamped here on imperial progress.
entries.literal: Tang Taizong campaigning against Goryeo halted his imperial progress here.

entries.zh: 部帥蘇支從征有功，奚長可度率眾內附，為置饒樂都督府。
entries.en: Division chief Su Zhi distinguished himself on the campaign; Xi leader Kedou brought his people to submit, and the court established Raole Protectorate.
entries.literal: Division chief Su Zhi followed the campaign with merit; Xi chief Kedou led the masses to submit inward, and the Raole Protectorate was set up for them.

entries.zh: 咸通以後，契丹始大，奚族不敢復抗。
entries.en: After the Xiantong era the Khitan rose in power and the Xi ceased to resist.
entries.literal: After Xiantong the Khitan grew great and the Xi no longer dared resist.

entries.zh: 太祖建國，舉族臣屬。
entries.en: When Taizu founded the dynasty, the entire tribe submitted.
entries.literal: When the Founder established the state, the whole tribe became subjects.

entries.zh: 聖宗嘗過七金山土河之濱，南望雲氣，有郛郭樓闕之狀，因議建都。
entries.en: Shengzong once traveled the Tu River below Qijin Mountain; seeing southern mists shaped like walls and gate-towers, he debated building a capital.
entries.literal: Shengzong once passed the bank of Qijin Mountain and the Tu River; gazing south at cloud vapors shaped like outer walls and towered gates, he discussed founding a capital.

entries.zh: 擇良工於燕、薊，董役二歲，郛郭、宮掖、樓閣、府庫、市肆廊廡，擬神都之制。
entries.en: Craftsmen from Yan and Ji were recruited; for two years they built walls, palaces, towers, storehouses, and market arcades on the model of Luoyang.
entries.literal: Skilled craftsmen were chosen from Yan and Ji; construction was supervised two years—outer walls, palace quarters, towers, treasuries, markets and colonnades modeled on the Divine Capital's plan.

entries.zh: 統和二十四年，五帳院進故奚王牙帳地。
entries.en: Tonghe year 24 brought the Five Accounts Division's gift of the old Xi royal encampment grounds.
entries.literal: In Tonghe year 24 the Five Accounts Division presented the former Xi king's headquarters land.

entries.zh: 二十五年，城之，實以漢戶，號曰中京，府曰大定。
entries.en: In year 25 the walls rose and Han households settled it; the capital was named Zhongjing and the prefecture Dading.
entries.literal: Year 25 the city was walled and filled with Han households; it was styled Zhongjing, the prefecture called Dading.

entries.zh: 皇城中有祖廟，景宗、承天皇后御容殿。
entries.en: The Imperial City held ancestral shrines and portrait halls for Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.
entries.literal: Within the Imperial City were ancestral temples and portrait halls to Emperor Jingzong and Empress Chengtian.

entries.zh: 城池湫濕，多鑿井泄之，人以不便。
entries.en: The walled city sat in wet ground; numerous drainage wells were sunk, to the residents' inconvenience.
entries.literal: The city moat was damp and low; many wells were dug to drain it—people found this inconvenient.

entries.zh: 大同驛以待宋使，朝天館待新羅使，來賓館待夏使。
entries.en: The Datong hostel lodged Song missions, Chaotian Hall Silla missions, and Laibin Hall Xia missions.
entries.literal: Datong Hostel received Song envoys; Chaotian Hall received Silla envoys; Laibin Hall received Xia envoys.

entries.zh: 有七金山、馬盂山、雙山、松山、土河。
entries.en: Landmarks included Qijin, Mayu, Twin, and Song mountains and the Tu River.
entries.literal: There were Qijin Mountain, Mayu Mountain, Twin Mountain, Song Mountain, and the Tu River.

entries.zh: 統州十、縣九：
entries.en: It governed ten prefectures and nine counties:
entries.literal: Ten prefectures, nine counties:

entries.zh: 惠州，惠和軍，中，刺史。
entries.en: Hui Prefecture—Huihe Army, middle grade, with a prefect.
