entries.literal: Hui Prefecture, Huihe Army, middle grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 本唐歸義州地。
entries.en: Formerly Tang Guiyi Prefecture land.
entries.literal: Originally Tang Guiyi Prefecture territory.

entries.zh: 太祖俘漢民數百戶兔鹿山下，創城居之，置州。
entries.en: Taizu took several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, built a town, and established the prefecture.
entries.literal: Taizu captured several hundred Han households below Tulu Mountain, founded a walled settlement, and set up the prefecture.

entries.zh: 屬中京，統縣一：惠和縣。
entries.en: Under Zhongjing; one county, Huihe County.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing; governing one county: Huihe County.

entries.zh: 聖宗遷上京惠州民，括諸宮院落帳戶置。
entries.en: Shengzong relocated Hui households from Shangjing and enrolled palace and camp registers to populate it.
entries.literal: Shengzong moved Hui Prefecture households from Shangjing and gathered palace and camp registered households to settle them.

entries.zh: 高州，觀察。
entries.en: Gao Prefecture (observation commissioner).
entries.literal: Gao Prefecture, observation commissioner.

entries.zh: 唐信州之地。
entries.en: Former Tang Xin Prefecture land.
entries.literal: Tang Xin Prefecture territory.

entries.zh: 萬歲通天元年，以契丹室活部置。
entries.en: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian placed the Khitan Shihuo division here.
entries.literal: In the first year of Wansui Tongtian it was set up for the Khitan Shihuo division.

entries.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，以俘戶置高州。
entries.en: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo campaign founded Gao Prefecture with war captives.
entries.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and established Gao Prefecture with captives.

entries.zh: 有平頂山、灤河。
entries.en: It has Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.
entries.literal: There are Pingding Mountain and the Luan River.

entries.zh: 屬中京。
entries.en: Under Zhongjing.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

entries.zh: 統縣一：
entries.en: One county:
entries.literal: Governing one county:

entries.zh: 三韓縣，辰韓為扶餘，弁韓為新羅，馬韓為高麗。
entries.en: Sanhan County: Chenhan stood for Fuyu, Bianhan for Silla, Mahan for Goryeo.
entries.literal: Sanhan County—Chenhan was Fuyu, Bianhan Silla, Mahan Goryeo.

entries.zh: 開泰中，聖宗伐高麗，俘三國之遺人置縣。
entries.en: During Kaitai Shengzong's Goryeo war placed survivors of the three Han states in the county.
entries.literal: In Kaitai Shengzong campaigned against Goryeo and settled remnant people of the three states in the county.

entries.zh: 戶五千。
entries.en: 5,000 households.
entries.literal: Households 5,000.

entries.zh: 北安州，興化軍，上，刺史。
entries.en: Bei'an Prefecture—Xinghua Army, upper grade, with a prefect.
entries.literal: Bei'an Prefecture, Xinghua Army, upper grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 本漢女祁縣地，屬上谷郡。
entries.en: Formerly Han Nuqi County in Shanggu Commandery.
entries.literal: Originally Han Nuqi County territory, belonging to Shanggu Commandery.

entries.zh: 晉為馮跋所據。
entries.en: Jin times saw Feng Ba take it.
entries.literal: Under Jin it was seized by Feng Ba.

entries.zh: 唐為奚王府西省地。
entries.en: Tang made it the Xi princely house's western domain.
entries.literal: Under Tang it was western territory of the Xi princely mansion.

entries.zh: 聖宗以漢戶置北安州。
entries.en: Shengzong placed Han households and founded Bei'an Prefecture.
entries.literal: Shengzong settled Han households to establish Bei'an Prefecture.

entries.zh: 屬中京。
entries.en: Under Zhongjing.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Zhongjing.

entries.zh: 統縣一：興化縣。
entries.en: One county: Xinghua County.
entries.literal: Governing one county: Xinghua County.

entries.zh: 本漢且居縣地。
entries.en: Formerly Han Qieju County land.
entries.literal: Originally Han Qieju County territory.

entries.zh: 安昌縣。
entries.en: Anchang County.
entries.literal: Anchang County.

entries.zh: 巖州，保肅軍，下，刺史。
entries.en: Yan Prefecture—Baosu Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
entries.literal: Yan Prefecture, Baosu Army, lower grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 本漢海陽縣地。
entries.en: Formerly Han Haiyang County land.
entries.literal: Originally Han Haiyang County territory.

entries.zh: 太祖平渤海，遷漢戶雜居興州境，聖宗於此建城焉。
entries.en: Taizu after conquering Bohai mingled Han households in Xing Prefecture; Shengzong walled a city here.
entries.literal: Taizu pacified Bohai and moved Han households to mix in Xing Prefecture territory; Shengzong built a city here.

entries.zh: 隸弘義宮，來屬。
entries.en: Under Hongyi Palace, then attached to Jin Prefecture.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Hongyi Palace; came under this prefecture.

entries.zh: 統縣一：興城縣。
entries.en: One county: Xingcheng County.
entries.literal: Governing one county: Xingcheng County.

entries.zh: 興中府。
entries.en: Xingzhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 本霸州彰武軍，節度。
entries.en: Formerly Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army), military commissioner.
entries.literal: Originally Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.

entries.zh: 古孤竹國。
entries.en: Land of ancient Guzhu.
entries.literal: The ancient Guzhu state.

entries.zh: 漢柳城縣地。
entries.en: Han Liucheng County ground.
entries.literal: Han Liucheng County territory.

entries.zh: 慕容皝以柳城之北，龍山之南，福德之地，乃築龍城，構宮廟，改柳城為龍城縣，遂遷都，號曰和龍宮。
entries.en: Murong Huang deemed the tract between Liucheng and Long Mountain auspicious, built Long City with palaces and shrines, renamed Liucheng Longcheng County, moved the capital, and called it Helong Palace.
entries.literal: Murong Huang, taking the land north of Liucheng and south of Long Mountain as a place of fortune and virtue, built Long City, erected palaces and temples, changed Liucheng to Longcheng County, moved the capital, and styled it Helong Palace.

entries.zh: 慕容垂復居焉，後為北跋所滅。
entries.en: Murong Chui returned there; Northern Yan later destroyed it.
entries.literal: Murong Chui dwelt there again; later it was destroyed by Northern Yan.

entries.zh: 元魏取為遼西郡。
entries.en: Northern Wei made it Liaoxi Commandery.
entries.literal: Northern Wei took it as Liaoxi Commandery.

entries.zh: 隋平高保寧，置營州。
entries.en: Sui subdued Gao Baoning and established Ying Prefecture.
entries.literal: Sui pacified Gao Baoning and set up Ying Prefecture.

entries.zh: 煬帝廢州置柳城郡。
entries.en: Sui Yang-di abolished the prefecture for Liucheng Commandery.
entries.literal: Emperor Yang abolished the prefecture and set up Liucheng Commandery.

entries.zh: 唐武德初改營州總管府，尋為都督府。
entries.en: Early Tang Wude made it Ying chief command, soon a protectorate seat.
entries.literal: Early Tang Wude changed it to Ying Prefecture chief commandery, soon a protectorate headquarters.

entries.zh: 萬歲通天中，陷李萬榮。
entries.en: Wansui Tongtian saw it lost to Li Wanrong.
entries.literal: In Wansui Tongtian it fell to Li Wanrong.

entries.zh: 神龍初，移府幽州。
entries.en: Early Shenlong shifted the seat to Youzhou.
entries.literal: Early Shenlong moved the headquarters to Youzhou.

entries.zh: 開元四年，復治柳城。
entries.en: Kaiyuan year 4 returned government to Liucheng.
entries.literal: Kaiyuan year 4 restored administration at Liucheng.

entries.zh: 八年，西徙漁陽。
entries.en: Year 8 the seat moved west to Yuyang.
entries.literal: Year 8 it moved west to Yuyang.

entries.zh: 十年，還柳城。
entries.en: Year 10 brought it back to Liucheng.
entries.literal: Year 10 it returned to Liucheng.

entries.zh: 後為奚所據。
entries.en: The Xi later held it.
entries.literal: Later the Xi seized it.

entries.zh: 太祖平奚及俘燕民，將建城，命韓知方擇其處。
entries.en: Taizu subdued the Xi, took Yan captives, and charged Han Zhifang to choose a city site.
entries.literal: Taizu pacified the Xi and captured Yan households; intending to build a city, he ordered Han Zhifang to choose the site.

entries.zh: 乃完葺柳城，號霸州彰武軍，節度。
entries.en: Liucheng was rebuilt as Ba Prefecture (Zhangwu Army) with a military commissioner.
entries.literal: Liucheng was then repaired and styled Ba Prefecture, Zhangwu Army, military commission.

entries.zh: 統和中，制置建、霸、宜、錦、白川等五州。
entries.en: Tonghe created a frontier commission over Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan prefectures.
entries.literal: In Tonghe times the frontier commission of Jian, Ba, Yi, Jin, and Baichuan five prefectures was set up.

entries.zh: 尋落制置，隸積慶宮。
entries.en: The commission was soon dropped and the seat joined Jiqing Palace.
entries.literal: Soon the commission was abolished; it was subordinate to Jiqing Palace.

entries.zh: 後屬興聖宮。
entries.en: Later it passed to Xingsheng Palace.
entries.literal: Later it belonged to Xingsheng Palace.

entries.zh: 重熙十年升興中府。
entries.en: Chongxi year 10 elevated it to Xingzhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Chongxi year 10 it was promoted to Xingzhong Prefecture.

entries.zh: 有大華山、小華山、香高山、麝香崖，天授皇帝刻石在焉，駐龍峪、神射泉、小靈河。
entries.en: It boasts Great and Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk Cliff with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's inscription, Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.
entries.literal: There are Great Huashan, Little Huashan, Xianggao Mountain, Musk-fragrance Cliff—with the Heaven-Granted Emperor's carved stone—Zhulong Vale, Divine Archery Spring, and the Little Ling River.

entries.zh: 統州二、縣四：
entries.en: It governed two prefectures and four counties:
entries.literal: Two prefectures, four counties:

entries.zh: 弘政縣。
entries.en: Hongzheng County.
entries.literal: Hongzheng County.

entries.zh: 世宗以定州俘戶置。
entries.en: Shizong settled it with Ding captives.
entries.literal: Shizong established it with Ding Prefecture captives.

entries.zh: 民工織纴，多技巧。
entries.en: Han craftsmen weave cloth with notable skill.
entries.literal: Han laborers weave cloth; many are skilled.

entries.zh: 聞義縣。
entries.en: Wenyi County.
entries.literal: Wenyi County.

entries.zh: 世宗置。
entries.en: Shizong founded it.
entries.literal: Established by Shizong.

entries.zh: 初隸海北州，後來屬。
entries.en: It first belonged to Haibei Prefecture, then to Yi.
entries.literal: First subordinate to Haibei Prefecture, later came under this seat.

entries.zh: 建州，保靜軍，上，節度。
entries.en: Jian Prefecture—Baojing Army, upper grade, military commissioner.
entries.literal: Jian Prefecture, Baojing Army, upper grade, military commission.

entries.zh: 唐武德中，置昌樂縣。
entries.en: Changle County was set up in Tang Wude.
entries.literal: In Tang Wude, Changle County was established.

entries.zh: 太祖完葺故壘，置州。
entries.en: Taizu restored the old walls and founded the prefecture.
entries.literal: Taizu completed the old ramparts and established the prefecture.

entries.zh: 漢乾祐元年，故石晉太后詣世宗，求於漢城側耕墾自贍。
entries.en: In Han Qianyou 1 the former Jin empress dowager visited Shizong, requesting land beside Hancheng to farm and provide for herself.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianyou of Han, the former Jin empress dowager came to Shizong, asking to farm and support herself beside Hancheng.

entries.zh: 許於建州南四十里給地五十頃，營構房室，創立宗廟。
entries.en: Permission was given for fifty qing of land forty li south of Jian Prefecture, with houses built and an ancestral temple founded.
entries.literal: He granted fifty qing of land forty li south of Jian Prefecture, built houses, and founded an ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 州在靈河之南，屢遭水害，聖宗遷於河北康崇州故城。
entries.en: The seat south of Ling River suffered repeated inundation; Shengzong relocated it to the old Kangchong Prefecture city north of the river.
entries.literal: The prefecture lay south of Ling River and suffered repeated floods; Shengzong moved it to the old city of Kangchong Prefecture north of the river.

entries.zh: 初名武寧軍，隸永興宮，後屬敦睦宮。
entries.en: It was first titled the Wuning Army, under Yongxing Palace, later attached to Dunmu Palace.
entries.literal: At first named Wuning Army; subordinate to Yongxing Palace; later under Dunmu Palace.

entries.zh: 統縣二：
entries.en: Two counties:
entries.literal: Governing two counties:

entries.zh: 來州，歸德軍，下，節度。
entries.en: Lai Prefecture—Guide Army, lower grade, military commissioner.
entries.literal: Lai Prefecture, Guide Army, lower grade, military commission.

entries.zh: 聖宗以女直五部歲饑來歸，置州居之。
entries.en: Shengzong received the five Jurchen divisions in famine years and founded the prefecture to house them.
entries.literal: Shengzong, when the five Jurchen divisions came in famine, settled them and set up the prefecture.

entries.zh: 初刺史，後升。
entries.en: It began with a prefect and was later elevated.
entries.literal: At first a cishi; later promoted.

entries.zh: 隸永興宮。
entries.en: Under Yongxing Palace.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Yongxing Palace.

entries.zh: 有三州山、六州山、五脂山。
entries.en: It has Sanzhou, Liuzhou, and Wuzhi mountains.
entries.literal: There are Sanzhou Mountain, Liuzhou Mountain, and Wuzhi Mountain.

entries.zh: 統州二、縣一：來賓縣。
entries.en: It governed two prefectures and one county, Laibin County.
entries.literal: Two prefectures, one county: Laibin County.

entries.zh: 本唐來遠縣地。
entries.en: Formerly Tang Laiyuan County land.
entries.literal: Originally Tang Laiyuan County territory.

entries.zh: 隰州，平海軍，下，刺史。
entries.en: Xi Prefecture—Pinghai Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
entries.literal: Xi Prefecture, Pinghai Army, lower grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 慕容皝置集寧縣。
entries.en: Murong Huang established Jining County.
entries.literal: Murong Huang set up Jining County.

entries.zh: 聖宗括帳戶遷信州，大雪不能進，建城於此，置焉。
entries.en: Shengzong mustered registers to relocate to Xin Prefecture; snow halted the march, so a city and prefecture were founded here.
entries.literal: Shengzong gathered registered households to move to Xin Prefecture; heavy snow blocked the way, so a city was built here and the prefecture set up.

entries.zh: 隸興聖宮，來屬。
entries.en: Under Xingsheng Palace; then attached here.
entries.literal: Subordinate to Xingsheng Palace; came under this prefecture.

entries.zh: 統縣一：海浜縣。
entries.en: One county: Haibin County.
entries.literal: Governing one county: Haibin County.

entries.zh: 本漢縣。
entries.en: Formerly a Han county.
entries.literal: Originally a Han county.

entries.zh: 瀕海，地多堿鹵，置鹽場於此。
entries.en: It borders the sea on saline soil where salt pans were established.
entries.literal: Coastal; the ground is much alkaline salt; salt works were set up here.

entries.zh: 遷州，興善軍，下，刺史。
entries.en: Qian Prefecture—Xingshan Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
entries.literal: Qian Prefecture, Xingshan Army, lower grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 本漢陽樂縣地。
entries.en: Formerly Han Yangle County land.
entries.literal: Originally Han Yangle County territory.

entries.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷歸州民置，來屬。
entries.en: After pacifying Da Yanlin, Shengzong resettled Gui Prefecture people here and attached the seat.
entries.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Gui Prefecture households here; came under this prefecture.

entries.zh: 有箭笴山。
entries.en: It has Jiangan Mountain.
entries.literal: There is Jiangan Mountain.

entries.zh: 統縣一：遷民縣。
entries.en: One county: Qianmin County.
entries.literal: Governing one county: Qianmin County.

entries.zh: 潤州，海陽軍，下，刺史。
entries.en: Run Prefecture—Haiyang Army, lower grade, with a prefect.
entries.literal: Run Prefecture, Haiyang Army, lower grade, cishi.

entries.zh: 聖宗平大延琳，遷寧州之民居此，置州。
entries.en: After Da Yanlin's defeat Shengzong relocated Ning Prefecture households and founded Run Prefecture.
entries.literal: Shengzong pacified Da Yanlin and moved Ning Prefecture households here and set up the prefecture.

entries.zh: 統縣一：
entries.en: One county:
entries.literal: Governing one county:

entries.zh: 地理志三中京道
entries.en: Geography Treatise III — Zhongjing Circuit
entries.literal: Geography Treatise III: Zhongjing Circuit

entries.zh: 大同元年，太宗皇帝自晉汴京收百司僚屬伎術歷象，遷於中京，遼始有歷。
entries.en: In Datong year 1 (947), Emperor Taizong gathered officials, retainers, artisans, and calendrical specialists from the Jin capital Bianjing and moved them to the Central Capital, and the Liao first acquired a state calendar.
entries.literal: In Datong year 1, Emperor Taizong collected the officials, retainers, craftsmen, and calendrical specialists from the Jin capital Bianjing and relocated them to the Central Capital; the Liao then first had a calendar.

entries.zh: 先是，梁、唐仍用景福《崇玄曆》。
entries.en: Earlier, Liang and Tang had continued using the Jingfu Chongxuan Calendar.
entries.literal: Previously, Liang and Tang still used the Jingfu Chongxuan Calendar.

entries.zh: 晉天福四年，司天監馬重績奏上《乙未元曆》，號《調元曆》，太宗所收天汴是也。
entries.en: In Later Jin Tianfu year 4 (939), Director of Astronomy Ma Chongji presented the Yiwei Origin Calendar, titled the Tiaoyuan Calendar—the calendar Taizong had taken from Bianjing.
entries.literal: In Jin Tianfu year 4, Director of Astronomy Ma Chongji submitted the Yiwei Origin Calendar, called the Tiaoyuan Calendar; this was what Taizong collected at Bian.

entries.zh: 穆宗應歷十一年，司天王白、李正等進歷，蓋《乙未元曆》也。
entries.en: In Muzong's Yingli year 11 (961), Wang Bai, Li Zheng, and others of the Directorate of Astronomy submitted a calendar that was essentially the Yiwei Origin Calendar.
entries.literal: In Muzong Yingli year 11, Director of Astronomy Wang Bai, Li Zheng and others presented a calendar, essentially the Yiwei Origin Calendar.

entries.zh: 聖宗統和十二年，可汗州刺史賈俊進新歷，則《大明曆》是也。
entries.en: In Shengzong's Tonghe year 12 (994), Jia Jun, prefect of Kehanzhou, presented a new calendar—the Great Brightness Calendar.
entries.literal: In Shengzong Tonghe year 12, Prefect Jia Jun of Kehanzhou presented a new calendar; this was the Great Brightness Calendar.

entries.zh: 高麗所誌《大遼古今錄》稱統和十二年始頒正朔改歷，驗矣。
entries.en: The Korean work Great Liao Ancient and Modern Accounts records that the new moon and calendar reform were first promulgated in Tonghe year 12—confirmed.
entries.literal: The Korean record Great Liao Ancient and Modern Accounts states that in Tonghe year 12 the correct new moon and calendar reform were first issued; verified.

entries.zh: 《大明曆》本宋祖沖之法，具見沈約《宋書》。
entries.en: The Great Brightness Calendar ultimately derives from Zu Chongzhi's Song methods, as fully recorded in Shen Yue's Book of Song.
entries.literal: The Great Brightness Calendar ultimately derives from Zu Chongzhi's methods of Song; fully seen in Shen Yue's Book of Song.

entries.zh: 具如左。
entries.en: The particulars follow below.
entries.literal: The details are as on the left.

entries.zh: 梁武帝天監三年，沖之子恒上疏，論何承天歷乖謬不可用。
entries.en: In Tianjian 3 (504), during the reign of Emperor Wu of Liang, Zu Chongzhi's son Heng memorialized that He Chengtian's calendar was erroneous and unusable.
entries.literal: In the third year of Liang Emperor Wu's Tianjian reign, Chongzhi's son Heng submitted a memorial discussing the errors of He Chengtian's calendar, that it could not be used.

entries.zh: 九年正月，詔用祖沖之所造《甲子元曆》頒朔。
entries.en: In first month of year 9, an edict adopted Zu Chongzhi's Jiazi Epoch Calendar for issuing the new moon.
entries.literal: In the first month of the ninth year, an edict ordered the Jiazi Epoch Calendar Chongzhi had made to be used to issue the new moon.

entries.zh: 陳氏因梁，亦用祖沖之歷。
entries.en: Chen continued Liang practice and used Chongzhi's calendar.
entries.literal: Chen followed Liang and also used Chongzhi's calendar.

entries.zh: 至遼，聖宗以賈俊所進新歷，因宋《大明》舊號行之。
entries.en: Under Liao, Emperor Shengzong adopted Jia Jun's new calendar while retaining the Song name Great Brightness.
entries.literal: Reaching Liao, Emperor Shengzong took the new calendar Jia Jun presented and, keeping the old Song title Great Brightness, put it into use.

entries.zh: 金曰《重修大明曆》。
entries.en: Jin titled it the Revised Great Brightness Calendar.
entries.literal: Jin called it the Revised Great Brightness Calendar.

entries.zh: 傳至皇元亦曰《重修大明曆》。
entries.en: In the Yuan it was likewise the Revised Great Brightness Calendar.
entries.literal: Transmitted to the Yuan it was also called the Revised Great Brightness Calendar.

entries.zh: 及改《授時曆》，別立司天監存肄之，每歲甲子冬至重修其法。
entries.en: After the Season-Granting Calendar replaced it, a Directorate of Astronomy kept the old methods, revised at each jiazi winter solstice.
entries.literal: When the Season-Granting Calendar was adopted, a separate Directorate of Astronomy was established to preserve study; each jiazi year at winter solstice its methods were revised.

entries.zh: 書在太史院，禁莫得聞。
entries.en: The text remained in the Grand Astrologer's archive, barred from circulation.
entries.literal: The book was kept in the Imperial Astronomical Archive; access was forbidden.

entries.zh: 宋武帝大明六年，祖沖之上《甲子元曆》法，未及施用，因名《大明曆》。
entries.en: In the sixth year of Emperor Wu of Song's Daming reign (462 CE), Zu Chongzhi presented the Jiazi Epoch Calendar methods; before adoption they were called the Great Brightness Calendar.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Emperor Wu of Song's Daming reign, Zu Chongzhi submitted the methods of the Jiazi Epoch Calendar, which had not yet been put into use; it was therefore named the Great Brightness Calendar.

entries.zh: 上元甲子至宋大明七年癸卯，五萬一千九百三十九年算外。
entries.en: From upper-origin jiazi to Song Daming year 7 (guimao) is 51,939 years beyond the epoch count.
entries.literal: From the upper origin jiazi to the seventh year of Song Daming, guimao, is 51,939 years, outside the count.

entries.zh: 元法：五十九萬二千三百六十五。
entries.en: Origin factor (yuan fa): 592,365.
entries.literal: Origin factor: 592,365.

entries.zh: 曆象誌上
entries.en: Celestial Phenomena Treatise I
entries.literal: Celestial Phenomena Treatise, Part One

entries.zh: 月度不足，是生朔虛；
entries.en: When a lunar month runs short of a full cycle, a "new-moon deficit" arises;
entries.literal: When the measure of the month falls short, this gives rise to new-moon deficit;

entries.zh: 天行有餘，是為氣盈。
entries.en: when the sun's annual course runs long, the result is "qi surplus."
entries.literal: when heaven's motion has surplus, this constitutes qi surplus.

entries.zh: 盈虛相懸，歲月乃牉，積牉而差，寒暑互易，百谷不成，庶政不明。
entries.en: Surplus and deficit pull against each other until year and month can be brought back into alignment; let misalignment accumulate and the seasons swap places, crops fail, and government loses its rhythm.
entries.literal: Surplus and deficit hang in opposition; only then do year and month come level; accumulated misleveling produces error, cold and heat exchange places, the hundred grains fail to ripen, and common administration lacks clarity.

entries.zh: 聖人驗以斗柄，準以歲星，爰立閏法，信治百官。
entries.en: The sages checked the seasons against the Dipper's handle and Jupiter's station, established intercalation on that basis, and thereby kept the civil calendar trustworthy for every office.
entries.literal: The sages verified by the Dipper's handle, took the Year Star as standard, thereupon established the intercalary rule, and reliably ordered the hundred officials.

entries.zh: 是故閏正而月正，月正而歲正。
entries.en: Correct intercalation makes the months right; correct months make the year right.
entries.literal: Therefore when intercalation is correct the months are correct, and when the months are correct the year is correct.

entries.zh: 歲月既正，頒令考績，無有不時。
entries.en: With the calendar set right, orders go out and performance is reviewed on schedule.
entries.literal: Once year and month are correct, edicts are issued and achievements examined, and none fail to be timely.

entries.zh: 國史正歲年以敘事，莫重於此。
entries.en: The court historians align the annual record to narrate events—nothing in statecraft weighs more.
entries.literal: The national chronicle sets the year aright to narrate affairs, and nothing is weightier than this.

entries.zh: 遼始征歷梁、唐。
entries.en: At first the Liao turned to the Liang and Tang for calendrical systems.
entries.literal: Liao at the outset sought calendars from Liang and Tang.

entries.zh: 入晉之後，奄有帝制，《乙未》、《大明》，曆法再變。
entries.en: Once they held the imperial mantle after entering Jin territory, they adopted the 《Yiwei》 and 《Daming》 systems in succession—two great calendar reforms.
entries.literal: After entering Jin territory they suddenly possessed the imperial system; the 《Yiwei》 and 《Daming》 calendars saw the calendrical method change twice.

entries.zh: 穆宗應歷六年，周用顯德《欽天曆》；
entries.en: In Muzong's sixth Yingli year the Later Zhou used the Xiande-era 《Qintian Calendar》;
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Yingli under Emperor Muzong, Zhou employed the Xiande 《Qintian Calendar》;

entries.zh: 十年，宋用建隆《應天曆》。
entries.en: in his tenth Yingli year the Song adopted the Jianlong 《Yingtian Calendar》.
entries.literal: In the tenth year, Song employed the Jianlong 《Yingtian Calendar》.

entries.zh: 景宗乾亨四年，宋用《乾元曆》。
entries.en: In Jingzong's fourth Qianheng year the Song used the 《Qianyuan Calendar》.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Qianheng under Emperor Jingzong, Song employed the 《Qianyuan Calendar》.

entries.zh: 聖宗統和十九年，宋用《儀天曆》；
entries.en: In Shengzong's nineteenth Tonghe year the Song used the 《Yitian Calendar》;
entries.literal: In the nineteenth year of Tonghe under Emperor Shengzong, Song employed the 《Yitian Calendar》;

entries.zh: 太平元年，宋用《崇天曆》。
entries.en: in the first Taiping year the Song used the 《Chongtian Calendar》.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Song employed the 《Chongtian Calendar》.

entries.zh: 道宗清寧十年，宋用《明天曆》；
entries.en: In Daozong's tenth Qingning year the Song used the 《Mingtian Calendar》;
entries.literal: In the tenth year of Qingning under Emperor Daozong, Song employed the 《Mingtian Calendar》;

entries.zh: 大康元年，宋用《奉元曆》；
entries.en: in the first Dakang year the Song used the 《Fengyuan Calendar》;
entries.literal: In the first year of Dakang, Song employed the 《Fengyuan Calendar》;

entries.zh: 大安七年，宋用《觀天曆》。
entries.en: in the seventh Da'an year the Song used the 《Guantian Calendar》.
entries.literal: In the seventh year of Da'an, Song employed the 《Guantian Calendar》.

entries.zh: 天祚皇帝乾統六年，宋用《紀元曆》。
entries.en: In Tianzuo's sixth Qiantong year the Song used the 《Jiyuan Calendar》.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Qiantong under Emperor Tianzuo, Song employed the 《Jiyuan Calendar》.

entries.zh: 五代歷三變，宋凡八變，遼終始再變。
entries.en: The Five Dynasties saw three calendar reforms, the Song eight, and the Liao only two from start to finish.
entries.literal: Under the Five Dynasties the calendar changed three times; under Song it changed eight times in all; Liao from beginning to end changed twice.

entries.zh: 曆法不齊，故定朔置閏，時有不同，覽者惑焉。
entries.en: Because their systems did not match, intercalary months and new-moon dates diverged, leaving readers baffled.
entries.literal: Calendrical methods were not uniform; therefore in fixing the new moon and placing intercalary months the times sometimes differed, and readers are perplexed.

entries.zh: 作《閏考》。
entries.en: Hence this 《Study of Intercalation》.
entries.literal: Therefore the 《Study of Intercalation》 was composed.

entries.en: (Tables occupy pages 540–564 of the printed edition.)
entries.literal: (The text has tables on pages 540–564 of the book.)

entries.zh: 曆象誌中 ○閏考
entries.en: Celestial Phenomena, Part Two — Intercalation
entries.literal: Treatise on Calendars and Celestial Signs, Part Two ○ Study of Intercalation

entries.zh: 官生於職，職沿於事，而名加之。
entries.en: Offices grow out of duties, duties from tasks, and names are layered on top.
entries.literal: Offices arise from duties; duties follow from affairs; and names are imposed upon them.

entries.zh: 後世沿名，不究其實。
entries.en: Later generations kept the titles without asking what they actually did.
entries.literal: Later ages inherit the names without investigating the substance.

entries.zh: 吏部，一太宰也，為大司徒，為尚書，為中書，為門下；
entries.en: Personnel had been Grand Steward, then Grand Minister of Education, Secretariat Director, and Gate Chancellery;
entries.literal: The Ministry of Personnel—once the Grand Steward—became Grand Minister of Education, became Director of the Department of State Affairs, became Secretariat Director, became Gate-of-the-Sons Chancellery;

entries.zh: 兵部，一司馬也，為大司馬，為太尉，為樞密使。
entries.en: War had been Minister of War, then Grand Minister of War, Grand Marshal, and Privy Commissioner.
entries.literal: The Ministry of War—once the Minister of War—became Grand Minister of War, became Grand Marshal, became Privy Commissioner.

entries.zh: 沿古官名，分今之職事以配之，於是先王統理天下之法，如治絲而棼，名實淆矣。
entries.en: Later regimes kept ancient titles and mapped current duties onto them, so the old way of governing the realm became like untangling snarled silk—name and reality mixed together.
entries.literal: Inheriting ancient office names, they matched present duties to them; thus the former kings' methods for ordering all under Heaven, like sorting silk that is already tangled, names and substance were confused.

entries.zh: 契丹舊俗，事簡職專，官制樸實，不以名亂之，其興也勃焉。
entries.en: In Khitan custom affairs were few and posts focused; government was plain and did not trade on empty titles, and their rise was swift.
entries.literal: Khitan old custom: affairs were simple and duties exclusive; office institutions were plain and solid, not disturbed by names; their rise was swift indeed.

entries.zh: 太祖神冊六年，詔正班爵。
entries.en: In Taizu Shence year 6 ranks at court were fixed by edict.
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Taizu's Shence reign an edict rectified court ranks.

entries.zh: 至於太宗，兼制中國，官分南北，以國制治契丹，以漢制待漢人。
entries.en: Under Taizong the state also ruled Chinese territory; offices split into Northern and Southern branches—Khitan governed by Liao law, Han by Han law.
entries.literal: By Taizong's time he also administered China; offices were divided into Northern and Southern faces, governing Khitan by national institutions and treating Han by Han institutions.

entries.zh: 國制簡樸，漢制則沿名之風固存也。
entries.en: The native system stayed spare; within the Chinese system the habit of nominal inheritance persisted.
entries.literal: National institutions were simple and plain; in Han institutions the habit of inheriting names still remained.

entries.zh: 遼國官職，分北、南院，北面治宮帳、部族、屬國之政，南面治漢人州縣、租賦、軍馬之事。
entries.en: Liao offices split into Northern and Southern Courts—the north handled palace accounts, tribes, and subject peoples; the south handled Han districts, revenue, and cavalry.
entries.literal: Liao state offices were divided into Northern and Southern Courts: the Northern Face governed palace accounts, tribes, and subject states; the Southern Face governed Han prefectures and counties, taxes, and military horses.

entries.zh: 因俗而治，得其宜矣。
entries.en: Each branch ruled in its own way, which suited the realm.
entries.literal: Governing according to custom, they obtained what was fitting.

entries.zh: 初，太祖分叠剌夷離堇為北、南二大王，謂之北、南院。
entries.en: Taizu first split the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings—the Northern and Southern Courts.
entries.literal: At first Taizu divided the Dieci yilijin into Northern and Southern Great Kings, called the Northern and Southern Courts.

entries.zh: 宰相、樞密、宣徽、林牙，下至郎君、護衛，皆分北、南，其實所治皆北面之事，語遼官制者，可不辨。
entries.en: Chancellor, Privy Council, xuanhui, linya, langjun, and guards all had north and south posts, but in practice they handled northern affairs; commentators on Liao offices should not be misled by the labels.
entries.literal: Chancellors, Privy Council, Xuanhui, linya, down to langjun and guards—all were divided into Northern and Southern, yet in substance all governed Northern Face affairs; those who speak of Liao offices need not be confused.

entries.zh: 凡遼朝官，北樞密視兵部，南樞密視吏部，北、南二王視戶部，夷離畢視刑部，宣徽視工部，敵烈麻都視禮部，北、南府宰相總之。
entries.en: Broadly, Northern Privy Council stood for War, Southern Privy for Personnel, the two Great Kings for Revenue, yilibi for Justice, xuanhui for Works, dilie mada for Rites, with Northern and Southern Chancellors above them.
entries.literal: In general Liao offices: the Northern Privy Council corresponded to the Ministry of War, the Southern Privy Council to the Ministry of Personnel, the Northern and Southern Great Kings to the Ministry of Revenue, yilibi to the Ministry of Justice, xuanhui to the Ministry of Works, dilie mada to the Ministry of Rites, and the Northern and Southern Chancellors presided over all.

entries.zh: 惕隱治宗族，林牙修文告，於越坐而論議，以象公師，朝廷之上。
entries.en: Tithen oversaw the imperial clan, linya drafted state papers, and yuyue deliberated from his seat as a notional chief mentor at court.
entries.literal: Tithen governed the clans; linya revised documents and proclamations; yuyue sat to discuss policy, representing the duke and tutor at court.

entries.zh: 事簡職專，此遼所以興也。
entries.en: Simple tasks and focused posts were how Liao prospered.
entries.literal: Affairs simple and duties focused—this is why Liao rose.

entries.zh: 北院大王。
entries.en: Northern Great King.
entries.literal: Northern Court Great King.

entries.zh: 初名叠剌部夷離堇，太祖分北、南院，太宗會同元年改夷離堇為大王。
entries.en: Originally Dieci yilijin; Taizu split north and south; in Taizong Huitong year 1 the title became Great King.
entries.literal: Originally titled yilijin of the Dieci tribe; Taizu divided the Northern and Southern Courts; in Taizong's Huitong year 1 yilijin was changed to Great King.

entries.zh: 知北院大王事北院大師
entries.en: Acting Northern Great King; Northern Grand Preceptor
entries.literal: Knower of Northern Court Great King affairs; Northern Court Grand Preceptor

entries.zh: 大於越府。
entries.en: Great Yuyue Office
entries.literal: Great Yuyue Office.

entries.zh: 無職掌，班百僚之上，非有大功德者不授，遼國尊官，猶南面之有三公。
entries.en: Without portfolio, it ranked above all officials and was granted only for exceptional merit—Liao's highest honor, comparable to the Three Dukes in the Chinese system.
entries.literal: It had no duties; its rank stood above the hundred officials; only those of great merit and virtue received it; it was a honored office of the Liao state, like the Three Dukes on the Southern Face.

entries.zh: 太祖以遙輦氏於越受禪。
entries.en: Taizu, as yuyue of the Yaolian clan, received the abdication.
entries.literal: Taizu, as the Yaolian clan's yuyue, received the abdication.

entries.zh: 終遼之世，以於越得重名者三人：耶律曷魯、屋質、仁先，謂之三於越。
entries.en: Only three men in Liao history bore the yuyue title with real weight—Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Renxian—the Three Yuyue.
entries.literal: Through the Liao dynasty only three men gained the yuyue name for weight: Yelü Helu, Wuzhi, and Renxian—called the Three Yuyue.

entries.zh: 大惕隱司。
entries.en: Great tithen office.
entries.literal: Great Tithen Office.

entries.zh: 太祖置，掌皇族之政教。
entries.en: Taizu founded it to oversee clan discipline and education.
entries.literal: Taizu established it to govern the imperial clan's moral instruction.

entries.zh: 興宗重熙二十一年，耶律義先拜惕隱，戒族人曰：「國家三父房最為貴族，凡天下風化之所自出，不孝不義，雖小不可為。」
entries.en: In Xingzong Chongxi year 21 Yelü Yixian became tithen and warned the clan: "The Three Fathers' lines are the highest nobility and the source of public morals—no unfilial or unjust act, however slight, is permissible."
entries.literal: In Xingzong Chongxi year 21 Yelü Yixian was appointed tithen and admonished the clansmen: "The state's Three Fathers' accounts are the noblest kin; all customs under Heaven flow from them—unfilial and unrighteous acts, however small, must not be done."

entries.zh: 其妻晉國長公主之女，每見中表，必具禮服。
entries.en: His wife was the Jin State Senior Princess's daughter; she always wore full court dress when receiving kin.
entries.literal: His wife was daughter of the Jin State Senior Princess; whenever she met cousins she always wore full ceremonial dress.

entries.zh: 義先以身率先，國族化之。
entries.en: Yixian led by example and the imperial kin followed.
entries.literal: Yixian took the lead in person and the state clans were transformed by it.

entries.zh: 遼國設官之實，於此可見。
entries.en: Here one sees what Liao offices were really for.
entries.literal: The substance of how Liao established offices can be seen here.

entries.zh: 太祖有國，首設此官，其後百官擇人，必先宗姓。
entries.en: Taizu created this post at the founding; later, when filling the bureaucracy, clan members were chosen first.
entries.literal: When Taizu founded the state he first set up this office; afterward in selecting officials for the hundred offices the imperial surname always came first.

entries.zh: 肅祖長子洽昚之族在五院司，叔子葛剌、季子洽禮及懿祖仲子帖剌、季子古直之族皆在六院司。
entries.en: Suzu's eldest son Zhi Yan's line sat in the Five Courts Office; third son Ge La, youngest son Zhi Li, and Yi Zu's second son Tie La and youngest son Gu Zhi were in the Six Courts Office.
entries.literal: The eldest son Zhi Yan's line of Ancestor Suzu was in the Five Courts Office; third son Ge La, youngest son Zhi Li, and Ancestor Yi's second son Tie La and youngest son Gu Zhi were all in the Six Courts Office.

entries.zh: 此五房者，謂之二院皇族。
entries.en: These five lines formed the Two Courts imperial clan.
entries.literal: These five houses are called the Two Courts imperial clan.

entries.zh: 玄祖伯子麻鲁无后，次子岩木之后曰孟父房；
entries.en: Xuanzu's eldest son Malu left no heirs; second son Yan Mu's line is the Senior Father's House;
entries.literal: Ancestor Xuanzu's eldest son Malu had no heirs; the second son Yan Mu's descendants are the Senior Father's House;

entries.zh: 叔子釋魯曰仲父房；
entries.en: The third son Shi Lu formed the Middle Father's House;
entries.literal: The third son Shi Lu is called the Middle Father's House;

entries.zh: 季子為德祖，德祖之元子是為太祖天皇帝，謂之橫帳；
entries.en: The junior line became Dez Zu; his eldest son was Taizu the Heavenly Emperor—the Horizontal Account;
entries.literal: The youngest son was Dez Zu; Dez Zu's eldest son is Taizu the Heavenly Emperor, called the Horizontal Account;

entries.zh: 次曰剌葛，曰叠剌，曰寅底石，曰安端，曰蘇，皆曰季父房。
entries.en: Next came Cige, Dieci, Yindi Shi, Anduan, and Su—the Junior Fathers' House.
entries.literal: Next were Cige, Dieci, Yindi Shi, Anduan, and Su—all called the Junior Fathers' House.

entries.zh: 此一帳三房，謂之四帳皇族。
entries.en: That one account in three branches is the Four Accounts imperial clan.
entries.literal: This one account with three houses is called the Four Accounts imperial clan.

entries.zh: 二院治之以北、南二王，四帳治之以大內惕隱，皆統於大惕隱司
entries.en: Two Courts fell under the Northern and Southern Great Kings; Four Accounts under the Great Inner tithen—all under the Great Tithen Office
entries.literal: The Two Courts were governed by the Northern and Southern Great Kings; the Four Accounts by the Great Inner tithen—all under the Great Tithen Office

entries.zh: 大橫帳常袞司。
entries.en: Great Horizontal Account changgun office.
entries.literal: Great Horizontal Account Changgun Office.

entries.zh: 掌太祖皇帝後九帳皇族之事。
entries.en: It governed the nine post-Taizu imperial accounts.
entries.literal: It governed the nine accounts of imperial clan after Emperor Taizu.

entries.zh: 橫帳常袞。
entries.en: Horizontal Account changgun
entries.literal: Horizontal Account changgun.

entries.zh: 亦曰橫帳敞穩。
entries.en: Also called horizontal account changwen
entries.literal: Also called horizontal account changwen.

entries.zh: 橫帳太師橫帳太保
entries.en: Horizontal Account Grand Preceptor and Horizontal Account Grand Guardian
entries.literal: Horizontal Account Grand Preceptor; Horizontal Account Grand Guardian

entries.zh: 王府祗候大東丹國中臺省。
entries.en: Princes' attendants and Great Eastern Danguo Central Secretariat.
entries.literal: Princes' attendants; Great Eastern Danguo Central Secretariat.

entries.zh: 太祖天顯元年置，乾亨四年聖宗省。
entries.en: Founded in Taizu Tianxian year 1; abolished in Shengzong Qianheng year 4.
entries.literal: Established in Taizu Tianxian year 1; abolished by Shengzong in Qianheng year 4.

entries.zh: 左大相右大相
entries.en: Left chief minister and Right chief minister
entries.literal: Left chief minister; Right chief minister

entries.zh: 遼太祖有帝王之度者三：代遙輦氏，尊九帳於御營之上，一也；
entries.en: Taizu showed imperial stature in three ways: replacing the Yaolian while honoring the nine accounts above his own camp—first;
entries.literal: Among Taizu's three marks of imperial stature: he replaced the Yaolian and honored the nine accounts above his own camp—first;

entries.zh: 滅渤海國，存其族帳，亞於遙輦，二也；
entries.en: He destroyed Bohai but kept its clan registers subordinate to the Yaolian—second;
entries.literal: He destroyed Bohai yet preserved its clan accounts, placing them below the Yaolian—second;

entries.zh: 並奚王之眾，撫其帳部，擬於國族，三也。
entries.en: He absorbed the Xi king's followers and settled their tribes on a par with the imperial clan—third.
entries.literal: He absorbed the Xi king's people and soothed their account tribes, ranking them like the state clan—third.

entries.zh: 有英雄之智者三：任國舅以耦皇族，崇乙室以抗奚王，列二院以制遙輦是已。
entries.en: Three marks of strategic genius: pairing maternal uncles with the imperial line, raising Yishi to counter the Xi king, and dividing Two Courts to restrain the Yaolian.
entries.literal: Three marks of heroic wisdom: employing the imperial maternal uncles to pair with the imperial clan, elevating the Yishi to balance the Xi king, and setting Two Courts to control the Yaolian—that is enough.

entries.zh: 觀北面諸帳官，可以見之矣。
entries.en: The Northern account offices show this plainly.
entries.literal: Viewing the Northern Face account offices, one can see it.

entries.zh: 遙輦九帳大常袞司。
entries.en: Yaolian Nine Accounts Great changgun office.
entries.literal: Yaolian Nine Accounts Great Changgun Office.

entries.zh: 掌遙輦窪可汗、阻午可汗、胡剌可汗、蘇可汗、鮮質可汗、昭古可汗、耶瀾可汗、巴剌可汗、痕德堇可汗九世宮分之事。
entries.en: It tended the palace estates of nine Yaolian khans from Waqihan through Hendejian.
entries.literal: It governed the palace shares of the nine Yaolian khans: Waqihan, Zuwu Khan, Hula Khan, Su Khan, Xianzhi Khan, Zhaogu Khan, Yelan Khan, Bala Khan, and Hendejian Khan.

entries.zh: 太祖受位於遙輦，以九帳居皇族一帳之上，設常袞司以奉之，有司不與焉。
entries.en: Taizu took power from the Yaolian, set the nine accounts above the imperial clan account, and gave them a Changgun Office apart from regular government.
entries.literal: Taizu received the throne from the Yaolian and placed the nine accounts above the one imperial clan account, establishing the Changgun Office to serve them while regular offices did not interfere.

entries.zh: 凡遼十二宮、五京，皆太祖以來征討所得，非受之於遙輦也。
entries.en: Liao's twelve palaces and five capitals all came from Taizu's conquests, not from the Yaolian inheritance.
entries.literal: All twelve palaces and five capitals of Liao were gains from campaigns since Taizu, not received from the Yaolian.

entries.zh: 其待先世之厚，蔑以加矣。
entries.en: No dynasty treated its predecessors more generously.
entries.literal: Their treatment of former dynasties was as generous as could be.

entries.zh: 遼俗東向而尚左，禦帳東向，遙輦九帳南向，皇族三父帳北向。
entries.en: Liao faced east and prized the left; the imperial camp faced east, the nine Yaolian accounts south, and the Three Fathers' clan accounts north.
entries.literal: Liao custom faced east and honored the left; the Imperial Account faced east, the Yaolian nine accounts faced south, and the imperial clan Three Fathers' accounts faced north.

entries.zh: 東西為經，南北為緯，故謂御營為橫帳雲。
entries.en: East-west was the warp and north-south the weft, so the imperial camp was called the Horizontal Account.
entries.literal: East and west were warp, north and south weft; therefore the imperial camp was called the Horizontal Account.

entries.zh: 著帳郎君院。
entries.en: Account-Registered Langjun Court
entries.literal: Account-Registered Langjun Court.

entries.zh: 遙輦痕德堇可汗以蒲古只等三族害於越室魯，家屬沒入瓦裏。
entries.en: Under Yaolian Khan Hendejian, Pugu Zhi and two other lines that had harmed yuyue Shilu were enrolled in wali.
entries.literal: In the Yaolian era Khan Hendejian, because Pugu Zhi and two other clans had harmed yuyue Shilu, their families were confiscated into wali.

entries.zh: 應天皇太后知國政，析出之，以為著帳郎君、娘子，每加矜恤。
entries.en: Empress Dowager Yingtian ruled and released them as account langjun and ladies, showing them special favor.
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Yingtian governed the state and released them, making them account-registered langjun and ladies, always adding favor.

entries.zh: 世宗悉免之。
entries.en: Shizong pardoned them entirely.
entries.literal: Shizong fully exempted them.

entries.zh: 其後內族、外戚及世官之家犯罪者，皆沒入瓦裏。
entries.en: Later, crimes by imperial kin, affinal kin, or hereditary officials again brought enrollment in wali.
entries.literal: Afterward when inner kin, outer kin, and hereditary official families committed crimes, all were confiscated into wali.

entries.zh: 人戶益眾，因復故名。
entries.en: As households multiplied, the old institution was revived.
entries.literal: Households grew ever more numerous, and the old name was restored.

entries.zh: 皇太后、皇太妃帳，皆有著帳諸局。
entries.en: The empress dowager and senior consort accounts each had account-registered bureaus.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager's account and the Senior Imperial Consort's account each had account-registered bureaus.

entries.zh: 大國舅司。
entries.en: Great Imperial Maternal Uncle Office
entries.literal: Great Imperial Maternal Uncle Office.

entries.zh: 掌國舅乙室已、拔裏二帳之事。
entries.en: It oversaw the Yishi and Boliji maternal-uncle accounts.
entries.literal: It governed the two accounts of the imperial maternal uncles Yishi and Boliji.

entries.zh: 太宗天顯十年，合皇太后二帳為國舅司；
entries.en: In Taizong Tianxian year 10 the empress dowager's two accounts were merged into one maternal-uncle office;
entries.literal: In Taizong Tianxian year 10 the Empress Dowager's two accounts were combined into the Imperial Maternal Uncle Office;

entries.zh: 聖宗開泰三年，又並乙室已、拔裏二司為一帳。
entries.en: In Shengzong Kaitai year 3 the Yishi and Boliji offices were merged again into a single account.
entries.literal: In Shengzong Kaitai year 3 the Yishi and Boliji offices were again merged into one account.

entries.zh: 乙室已國舅大翁帳常袞。
entries.en: Yishi imperial maternal uncle Great Elder Account changgun
entries.literal: Yishi imperial maternal uncle Great Elder Account changgun.

entries.zh: 一作敞穩。
entries.en: Also called changwen
entries.literal: Also called changwen.

entries.zh: 官制未詳。
entries.en: Institutions not recorded in detail.
entries.literal: Office institutions not recorded in detail.

entries.zh: 國舅別部敞史。
entries.en: Imperial Maternal Uncle Separate Division changgun
entries.literal: Imperial Maternal Uncle Separate Division changgun.

entries.zh: 聖宗太平八年，見國舅別部敞史蕭塔葛。
entries.en: In Shengzong Taiping year 8 Xiao Tage held the Separate Division changgun post.
entries.literal: In Shengzong Taiping year 8 the Separate Division changgun Xiao Tage was seen.

entries.zh: 渤海帳司。
entries.en: Bohai Account Office
entries.literal: Bohai Account Office.

entries.zh: 官制未詳。
entries.en: Institutions not recorded in detail.
entries.literal: Office institutions not recorded in detail.

entries.zh: 渤海宰相
entries.en: Bohai chancellor.
entries.literal: Bohai chancellor

entries.zh: 聖宗興聖宮興宗延慶宮道宗太和宮天祚永昌宮
entries.en: Shengzong Xingsheng Palace, Xingzong Yanqing Palace, Daozong Taihe Palace, and Tianzuo Yongchang Palace
entries.literal: Shengzong Xingsheng Palace; Xingzong Yanqing Palace; Daozong Taihe Palace; Tianzuo Yongchang Palace

entries.zh: 國舅右夷離畢敞史國舅帳克國舅別部。
entries.en: Imperial maternal uncle right yilibi; changgun; imperial maternal uncle account ke; Imperial Maternal Uncle Separate Division.
entries.literal: Imperial Maternal Uncle Right Yilibi; changgun; Imperial Maternal Uncle Account ke; Imperial Maternal Uncle Separate Division.

entries.zh: 世宗置。
entries.en: Shizong established it.
entries.literal: Shizong established it.

entries.zh: 某得裏，官名未詳。
entries.en: A certain deli—title not recorded in detail.
entries.literal: A certain deli—office name not recorded in detail.

entries.zh: 太祖弘義宮太宗永興宮世宗積慶宮
entries.en: Taizu Hongyi Palace, Taizong Yongxing Palace, and Shizong Jiqing Palace
entries.literal: Taizu Hongyi Palace; Taizong Yongxing Palace; Shizong Jiqing Palace

entries.zh: 應天皇太后長寧宮穆宗延昌宮景宗彰湣宮承天皇太后崇德宮
entries.en: Empress Dowager Yingtian Changning Palace, Muzong Yanchang Palace, Jingzong Zhangmin Palace, and Empress Dowager Chengtian Chongde Palace
entries.literal: Empress Dowager Yingtian Changning Palace; Muzong Yanchang Palace; Jingzong Zhangmin Palace; Empress Dowager Chengtian Chongde Palace

entries.zh: 百官志一
entries.en: Official Posts Treatise I
entries.literal: Official Posts Treatise, Part One

entries.zh: 助教興中府知興中府事。
entries.en: Assistant instructor; Xingzhong Prefecture; acting administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture.
entries.literal: Assistant Instructor; Xingzhong Prefecture; knower of Xingzhong Prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 咸雍元年見知興中府事楊績。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianyong: Yang Ji as acting Xingzhong prefect.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianyong Yang Ji appears as knower of Xingzhong Prefecture affairs.

entries.zh: 同知興中府事
entries.en: Deputy acting administrator of Xingzhong Prefecture
entries.literal: Associate knower of Xingzhong Prefecture affairs

entries.zh: 百官志四
entries.en: Official Posts Treatise IV
entries.literal: Official Posts Treatise, Part Four

entries.zh: 道宗清寧元年，皇帝射柳訖，詣風師壇，再拜。
entries.en: In Qingning 1 (1055), after the emperor finished shooting at the willow, he went to the Wind Master altar and bowed twice.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingning under Daozong, when the emperor had finished shooting at the willow, he went to the Wind Master altar and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 初，皇帝皆親拜，至道宗始命夷離畢拜之。
entries.en: At first the emperor always bowed in person; only under Daozong was the Yelübi ordered to perform the bowing on his behalf.
entries.literal: At first the emperor always bowed in person; only from Daozong onward was the Yelübi ordered to bow in his stead.

entries.zh: 告廟儀：至日，臣僚昧爽朝服，詣太祖廟。
entries.en: Temple Announcement Rite: On the appointed day, at dawn the ministers donned court dress and proceeded to the Taizu Temple.
entries.literal: Temple Announcement Rite: On the appointed day, at dawn ministers put on court dress and went to the Taizu Temple.

entries.zh: 次引臣僚，合班，先見御容，再拜畢，引班首左上，至褥位，再拜。
entries.en: The ministers were then led in, ranks united; they first viewed the imperial portrait and bowed twice; the rank leader was led up to the left to the mat position and bowed twice.
entries.literal: Next the ministers were led in; ranks united; they first viewed the imperial portrait and bowed twice; the rank leader was led up to the left, to the mat position, and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 贊上香，揖欄內上香畢，復褥位，再拜。
entries.en: Incense was announced; they bowed within the railing and offered incense; when finished they returned to the mat position and bowed twice.
entries.literal: Incense was praised; they bowed within the railing and offered incense; when finished they returned to the mat position and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 各祗候立定。
entries.en: Each stood at attention in place.
entries.literal: Each stood at attention in place.

entries.zh: 左右舉告廟祝版，於御容前跪捧。
entries.en: Attendants on the left and right raised the temple-announcement prayer board and knelt holding it before the imperial portrait.
entries.literal: Attendants on left and right raised the temple-announcement prayer board and knelt holding it before the imperial portrait.

entries.zh: 中書舍人俯跪，讀訖，俯興，退。
entries.en: The Secretariat Drafter knelt prostrate, read the text through, rose, and withdrew.
entries.literal: The Secretariat Drafter knelt prostrate, read it through, rose prostrate, and withdrew.

entries.zh: 引班首左下，復位，又再拜。
entries.en: The rank leader was led down to the left, returned to position, and bowed twice again.
entries.literal: The rank leader was led down to the left, returned to position, and bowed twice again.

entries.zh: 分引上殿，次第進酒三。
entries.en: They were led separately into the hall and presented wine three times in succession.
entries.literal: They were led separately up the hall and presented wine three times in order.

entries.zh: 分班引出。
entries.en: They were led out in separate ranks.
entries.literal: In separate ranks they were led out.

entries.zh: 禮志一
entries.en: Treatise on Rites I
entries.literal: Rites Treatise, Part One

entries.zh: 喪葬儀：聖宗崩，興宗哭臨於菆塗殿。
entries.en: Funeral rites: When Emperor Shengzong passed away, Emperor Xingzong came to mourn at the bier in the Zangtu Hall.
entries.literal: Funeral rites: When Emperor Shengzong died, Emperor Xingzong mourned at the bier in the Zangtu Hall.

entries.zh: 大行之夕四鼓終，皇帝率群臣入，柩前三致奠，奉柩出殿之西北門，就辒京車，藉以素裀。
entries.en: On the night the late emperor died, after the fourth watch had ended, the emperor led his ministers inside. Before the bier they presented offerings three times, then carried the coffin out through the northwest gate of the hall, set it on the encoffining carriage, and laid a plain white mat underneath.
entries.literal: On the night of the late emperor's passing, when the fourth watch ended, the emperor led the officials in; before the bier they presented offerings three times, bore the bier out through the hall's northwest gate, placed it on the encoffining carriage, and spread a plain white mat beneath.

entries.zh: 巫者袚除之。
entries.en: Shamans performed the rites of purification.
entries.literal: Shamans performed purification upon it.

entries.zh: 詰旦，發引，至祭，凡五致奠。
entries.en: At dawn the funeral procession departed; from the setting out to the sacrifice, offerings were presented five times in all.
entries.literal: At dawn the procession set out; from departure to sacrifice, offerings were presented five times in all.

entries.zh: 太巫祈禳。
entries.en: The grand shaman offered prayers of expiation.
entries.literal: The grand shaman prayed for expiation.

entries.zh: 皇族、外戚、大臣、諸京官以次致祭。
entries.en: Members of the imperial clan, maternal relatives, great ministers, and officials from the various capitals offered sacrifice in succession.
entries.literal: The imperial clan, maternal kin, great ministers, and officials of the various capitals offered sacrifice in turn.

entries.zh: 乃以衣、弓矢、鞍勒、圖畫、馬駝、儀衛等物皆燔之。
entries.en: Then clothing, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, paintings, horses and camels, ceremonial regalia, and the like were all consigned to the flames.
entries.literal: Then clothing, bows and arrows, saddles and bridles, paintings, horses and camels, ceremonial guards, and the like were all burned.

entries.zh: 至山陵，葬畢，上哀冊。
entries.en: When they reached the imperial tomb and the burial was finished, the lamentation document was presented.
entries.literal: When they reached the imperial tomb and the burial was complete, the lamentation document was presented.

entries.zh: 皇帝御幄，命改火，面火致奠，三拜。
entries.en: The emperor took his seat in the imperial tent, ordered the mourning fire to be kindled anew, faced the fire to present offerings, and bowed three times.
entries.literal: The emperor sat in the imperial tent, ordered the fire to be changed, faced the fire to present offerings, and bowed three times.

entries.zh: 又東向，再拜天地訖，乘馬，率送葬者過神門之木乃下，東向又再拜。
entries.en: He then turned eastward and bowed twice to Heaven and Earth. When this was done he mounted his horse and led the funeral party past the spirit-gate tree before dismounting and bowing twice again toward the east.
entries.literal: He then faced east and bowed twice more to Heaven and Earth; when this was done he mounted his horse, led the funeral party past the spirit-gate tree before dismounting, and bowed twice again facing east.

entries.zh: 翼日詰旦，率群臣、命婦詣山陵，行初奠之禮。
entries.en: On the following morning at dawn he led the officials and titled ladies to the imperial tomb to perform the first offering rite.
entries.literal: On the morrow at dawn he led the officials and titled ladies to the imperial tomb to perform the first offering rite.

entries.zh: 升御容殿，受遺賜。
entries.en: He ascended the Hall of Imperial Portrait and received the late emperor's bequeathed gifts.
entries.literal: He ascended the Hall of Imperial Portrait and received the bequeathed gifts.

entries.zh: 又翼日，再奠如初。
entries.en: On the day after that, the second offering was performed in the same manner.
entries.literal: On the following day the second offering was performed as before.

entries.zh: 興宗崩，道宗親擇地以葬。
entries.en: When Emperor Xingzong died, Emperor Daozong personally selected the ground for his burial.
entries.literal: When Emperor Xingzong died, Emperor Daozong personally chose the burial site.

entries.zh: 道宗崩，菆塗於遊仙殿，有司奉喪服。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong died, the body was laid out in the Youxian Hall, and the responsible offices presented the mourning garments.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong died, the body was laid out at the Youxian Hall; the proper offices presented mourning garments.

entries.zh: 天祚皇帝問禮於總知翰林院事耶律固，始服斬衰；
entries.en: Emperor Tianzuo inquired about the rites from Ye Lü Gu, Supervisor of the Hanlin Academy, and then put on the deepest mourning garment of unhemmed sackcloth;
entries.literal: Emperor Tianzuo asked Supervisor of the Hanlin Academy Ye Lü Gu about the rites and then donned the deepest mourning of unhemmed sackcloth;

entries.zh: 皇族、外戚、使相、矮墩官及郎君服如之；
entries.en: the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, officials of Aidian rank, and langjun wore the same;
entries.literal: the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, officials of the Aidian rank, and langjun wore the same;

entries.zh: 餘官及承應人皆白掞衣巾以入，哭臨。
entries.en: all remaining officials and attendants entered wearing white mourning dress and headcloths to mourn at the bier.
entries.literal: all other officials and attendants entered in white mourning dress and headcloth to mourn at the bier.

entries.zh: 惕隱、三父房，南府宰相、遙輦常袞、九奚首郎君、夷離畢、國舅詳穩、十閘撒郎君、南院大王、郎君，各以次薦奠，進鞍馬、衣襲、犀玉帶等物，表列其數。
entries.en: The Tieli, the Three Fathers' House, the Southern Chancellor, Yaonian Changgun, the Nine Xishou Langjun, Yilibi, the Guojiu Xiangwen, the Ten Zhacha Langjun, the Southern Grand Prince, and the langjun—each in turn presented burial offerings, advancing saddled horses, burial garments, rhinoceros-horn and jade belts, and the like, with memorials itemizing the quantities.
entries.literal: Tieli, the Three Fathers' House, the Southern Chancellor, Yaonian Changgun, the Nine Xishou Langjun, Yilibi, Guojiu Xiangwen, the Ten Zhacha Langjun, the Southern Grand Prince, and langjun—each in order presented burial offerings, advancing saddled horses, burial garments, rhinoceros and jade belts, and the like, with memorials listing the quantities.

entries.zh: 讀訖，焚表。
entries.en: When the reading was finished, the memorial was burned.
entries.literal: When the reading was finished, the memorial was burned.

entries.zh: 諸國所賻器服，親王、諸京留守奠祭、進賻物亦如之。
entries.en: Funerary goods contributed by the various states, and the offerings and tribute presented by princes and frontier commissioners, followed the same procedure.
entries.literal: Funerary goods sent from the various states, and the offerings and tribute presented by princes and frontier commissioners, followed the same practice.

entries.zh: 先帝小斂前一日，皇帝喪服上香，奠酒，哭臨。
entries.en: On the day before the lesser dressing of the late emperor, the emperor in mourning robes burned incense, offered wine, and mourned at the bier.
entries.literal: On the day before the lesser dressing of the late emperor, the emperor in mourning robes burned incense, offered wine, and mourned at the bier.

entries.zh: 其夜，北院樞密使、契丹行宮都部署入，小斂。
entries.en: That night the Northern Chancellor and the Khitan Mobile Court Grand Deployer entered and performed the lesser dressing of the corpse.
entries.literal: That night the Northern Chancellor and the Khitan Mobile Court Grand Deployer entered and performed the lesser dressing.

entries.zh: 翼日，遣北院樞密副使、林牙，以所赗器服，置之幽宮。
entries.en: On the following day the Northern Vice Chancellor and the Linya were dispatched to place the contributed goods and garments in the inner chamber of the tomb.
entries.literal: On the following day the Northern Vice Chancellor and the Linya were sent to place the contributed goods and garments in the inner chamber.

entries.zh: 靈柩升車，親王推之，至食羖之次。
entries.en: When the spirit coffin was lifted onto the carriage, princes pushed it forward to the place of the ram sacrifice.
entries.literal: When the spirit coffin was raised onto the carriage, princes pushed it forward to the place of the ram sacrifice.

entries.zh: 蓋遼國舊俗，於此刑羖羊以祭。
entries.en: This was an old Liao custom: here a ram was slaughtered as a sacrifice.
entries.literal: For by Liao custom a ram was slaughtered here in sacrifice.

entries.zh: 皇族、外戚、諸京州官以次致祭。
entries.en: The imperial clan, maternal kin, and officials of the various capitals and prefectures offered sacrifice in succession.
entries.literal: The imperial clan, maternal kin, and officials of the various capitals and prefectures offered sacrifice in turn.

entries.zh: 至葬所，靈柩降車。
entries.en: At the burial ground the spirit coffin was lowered from the carriage.
entries.literal: At the burial ground the spirit coffin was lowered from the carriage.

entries.zh: 就舉，皇帝免喪服，步引至長福岡。
entries.en: For the interment the emperor removed his mourning robes and walked ahead on foot, leading the procession to Changfu Hill.
entries.literal: For the interment the emperor removed his mourning robes and walked ahead, leading the procession to Changfu Hill.

entries.zh: 是夕，皇帝入陵寢，授遺物於皇族、外戚及諸大臣，乃出。
entries.en: That evening the emperor entered the tomb chamber, distributed the late emperor's possessions among the imperial clan, maternal kin, and great ministers, and then withdrew.
entries.literal: That evening the emperor entered the tomb chamber, distributed the late emperor's possessions among the imperial clan, maternal kin, and great ministers, and then came out.

entries.zh: 命以先帝寢幄，過於陵前神門之木。
entries.en: He ordered the late emperor's sleeping tent to be carried past the spirit-gate tree before the tomb.
entries.literal: He ordered the late emperor's sleeping tent to be carried past the spirit-gate tree before the tomb.

entries.zh: 帝不親往，遣近侍冠服赴之。
entries.en: The emperor did not go in person but sent close attendants in formal caps and robes in his stead.
entries.literal: The emperor did not go in person but sent close attendants in formal caps and robes.

entries.zh: 初奠，皇帝、皇后率皇族、外戚、使相、節度使、夫人以上命婦皆拜祭，循陵三匝而降。
entries.en: For the first offering, the emperor and empress led the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, military governors, and titled ladies of third rank and above in bowing and sacrifice; they circled the tomb three times before descending.
entries.literal: For the first offering, the emperor and empress led the imperial clan, maternal kin, commissioners, military governors, and titled ladies of third rank and above in bowing and sacrifice; they circled the tomb three times before descending.

entries.zh: 再奠，如初。
entries.en: The second offering followed the same procedure as the first.
entries.literal: The second offering followed the first.

entries.zh: 辭陵而還。
entries.en: They took leave of the tomb and returned.
entries.literal: They took leave of the tomb and returned.

entries.zh: 宋使祭奠吊慰儀：太皇太后至菆塗殿，服喪服。
entries.en: Rites for Song envoys presenting condolences and comfort: The Grand Empress Dowager came to the Zangtu Hall dressed in mourning.
entries.literal: Song envoy condolence and consolation rite: The Grand Empress Dowager came to the Zangtu Hall in mourning dress.

entries.zh: 太后於北間南面垂簾坐，皇帝於南間北面坐，使至幕次。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager sat behind a curtain on the south side of the north chamber; the emperor sat on the north side of the south chamber facing north; the envoys arrived at the side tents.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager sat behind a curtain on the south side of the north chamber; the emperor sat on the north side of the south chamber facing north; the envoys arrived at the side tents.

entries.zh: 宣賜素服、皂帶，更衣訖，引南北臣僚入班，立定。
entries.en: They were granted plain mourning dress and a black belt; when they had changed, officials of the northern and southern administrations were led in and took their places.
entries.literal: They were granted plain mourning dress and a black belt; when they had changed, officials of north and south were led in and took their places.

entries.zh: 可矮墩以下，並上殿依位立。
entries.en: Those of Aidian rank and below all ascended the hall and stood in their assigned places.
entries.literal: Those from the Aidian rank down all ascended the hall and stood by position.

entries.zh: 先引祭奠使副捧祭文南洞門入，殿上下臣僚並舉哀，至丹墀立定。
entries.en: The condolence envoys were first led in through the south gate bearing the elegy; officials above and below the hall all wailed; they halted on the red steps of the courtyard.
entries.literal: The condolence envoys were first led in through the south gate carrying the elegy; officials above and below the hall all wailed; they halted on the red steps.

entries.zh: 西上閣門使自南階下，受祭文，上殿啟封，置於香案。
entries.en: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the south steps, received the elegy, ascended the hall, broke the seal, and placed it on the incense table.
entries.literal: The Western Upper Gate attendant came down the south steps, received the elegy, ascended, opened the seal, and placed it on the incense table.

entries.zh: 哭止，祭奠禮物列殿前。
entries.en: Wailing ceased, and the condolence gifts were arrayed before the hall.
entries.literal: Wailing ceased and condolence gifts were arrayed before the hall.

entries.zh: 引使副南階上殿，至褥位立，揖，再拜。
entries.en: The envoys were led up the south steps to the cushion and stood; they bowed with a gesture and then bowed twice.
entries.literal: The envoys were led up the south steps to the cushion and stood; they bowed with a motion and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 引太使近前上香，退，再拜。
entries.en: The chief envoy was led forward to burn incense, withdrew, and bowed twice.
entries.literal: The chief envoy advanced to burn incense and withdrew, then bowed twice.

entries.zh: 大使近前跪，捧臺盞，進奠酒三，教坊奏樂，退，再拜，揖，中書二舍人跪捧祭文，引大使近前俯伏跪，讀訖，舉哀。
entries.en: The chief envoy advanced, knelt, and held the offering tray; he presented wine three times while the Music Office played. He withdrew, bowed twice, and bowed with a gesture. Two Zhongshu secretaries knelt bearing the elegy; the chief envoy was led forward, prostrated himself, read it to the end, and wailing rose.
entries.literal: The chief envoy advanced, knelt, and held the offering tray; he presented wine three times while the Music Office played; he withdrew, bowed twice, bowed with a motion; two Zhongshu secretaries knelt holding the elegy; the chief envoy was led forward, prostrated himself, read it, and wailing rose.

entries.zh: 引使副下殿立定，哭止。
entries.en: The envoys were led down from the hall and stood below; wailing ceased.
entries.literal: The envoys were led down and stood below; wailing ceased.

entries.zh: 禮物擔床出畢，引使副近南，面北立。
entries.en: When the gift litters had all been brought out, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.
entries.literal: When the gift litters had all been brought out, the envoys were led southward to stand facing north.

entries.zh: 勾吊慰使副南洞門入。
entries.en: The consolation envoys were summoned to enter through the south gate.
entries.literal: The consolation envoys were summoned to enter through the south gate.

entries.zh: 四使同見大行皇帝靈，再拜。
entries.en: All four envoys together viewed the spirit of the late emperor and bowed twice.
entries.literal: All four envoys together viewed the spirit of the late emperor and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 引出，歸幕次。
entries.en: They were led out and returned to the side tents.
entries.literal: They were led out and returned to the side tents.

entries.zh: 皇太后別殿坐，服喪服。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager sat in a separate hall dressed in mourning.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager sat in a separate hall in mourning dress.

entries.zh: 先引北南面臣僚並於殿上下依位立，吊慰使副捧書匣右入，當殿立。
entries.en: Officials of the northern and southern administrations were first led to stand above and below the hall in their places; the consolation envoys entered carrying the letter casket on the right and stood before the hall.
entries.literal: Officials of the north and south were first led to stand above and below the hall by position; the consolation envoys entered carrying the letter casket on the right and stood before the hall.

entries.zh: 閤門使右下殿受書匣，上殿奏「封全」。
entries.en: The Gate Attendant came down on the right, received the casket, ascended the hall, and reported, "The seal is intact."
entries.literal: The Gate Attendant came down on the right, received the casket, ascended, and reported "the seal is intact."

entries.zh: 開讀訖，引使副南階上殿，傳達吊慰訖，退，下殿立。
entries.en: When it was opened and read, the envoys were led up the south steps, conveyed their condolences, withdrew, and stood below the hall.
entries.literal: When it was opened and read, the envoys were led up the south steps, conveyed their condolences, withdrew, and stood below the hall.

entries.zh: 引禮物擔床過畢，引使副近南，北面立。
entries.en: When the gift litters had passed, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.
entries.literal: When the gift litters had passed, the envoys were led to the south to stand facing north.

entries.zh: 勾祭奠使副入。
entries.en: The condolence envoys were summoned to enter.
entries.literal: The condolence envoys were summoned to enter.

entries.zh: 四使同見。
entries.en: All four envoys were received together.
entries.literal: All four envoys were received together.

entries.zh: 鞠躬，再拜。
entries.en: They bowed with a gesture and then bowed twice.
entries.literal: They bowed with a motion and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 不出班，奏「聖躬萬福」，再拜。
entries.en: Without leaving formation they reported, "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings," and bowed twice.
entries.literal: Without leaving the formation they reported "May Your Majesty enjoy ten thousand blessings" and bowed twice.

entries.zh: 出班，謝面天顏，又再拜，立定。
entries.en: They left formation, thanked him for appearing in person, bowed twice again, and stood at attention.
entries.literal: They left the formation, thanked him for appearing in person, bowed twice again, and stood.

entries.zh: 宣徽傳聖旨撫問，就位謝，再拜。
entries.en: The Palace Commissioner conveyed the imperial message of comfort; they took their places and offered thanks, bowing twice.
entries.literal: The Palace Commissioner conveyed the imperial message of comfort; they took their places and thanked him, bowing twice.

entries.zh: 引出，歸幕次。
entries.en: They were led out and returned to the side tents.
entries.literal: They were led out and returned to the side tents.

entries.zh: 皇帝御南殿，服喪服。
entries.en: The emperor presided in the southern hall dressed in mourning.
entries.literal: The emperor presided in the southern hall in mourning dress.

entries.zh: 使副入見，如見皇太后儀，加謝遠接撫問、湯藥，再拜。
entries.en: The envoys entered for an audience following the same procedure as for the Empress Dowager, with additional thanks for the escort on their journey, expressions of comfort, and provisions of medicine, bowing twice.
entries.literal: The envoys entered for an audience by the same procedure as for the Empress Dowager, with additional thanks for escort on the journey, comfort, and medicine, bowing twice.

entries.zh: 次宣賜使副並從人，祭奠使副別賜讀祭文例物。
entries.en: Next, gifts were bestowed on the envoys and their attendants; the condolence envoys separately received the customary items granted for reading the elegy.
entries.literal: Next gifts were bestowed on the envoys and their attendants; the condolence envoys separately received the customary items for reading the elegy.

entries.zh: 即日就館賜宴。
entries.en: That same day a banquet was given for them at their lodging.
entries.literal: That same day a banquet was given at their lodging.

entries.zh: 高麗、夏國奉吊、進賻等使禮，略如之。
entries.en: The rites for envoys from Goryeo and Western Xia presenting condolences and tribute were much the same.
entries.literal: The rites of Goryeo and Western Xia envoys presenting condolences and tribute were much the same.

entries.zh: 道宗崩，天祚皇帝問禮於耶律固。
entries.en: When Emperor Daozong died, Emperor Tianzuo consulted Ye Lü Gu about the proper rites.
entries.literal: When Emperor Daozong died, Emperor Tianzuo asked Ye Lü Gu about the rites.

entries.zh: 宋國遣使吊及致祭、歸赗，皇帝喪服，禦遊仙之北別殿。
entries.en: The Song court dispatched envoys to offer condolences, present sacrifices, and return funerary gifts; the emperor, dressed in mourning, presided in the separate hall north of the Youxian Hall.
entries.literal: The Song state sent envoys to offer condolences, present sacrifices, and return funerary gifts; the emperor in mourning robes presided in the separate hall north of Youxian.

entries.zh: 使入門，皇帝哭。
entries.en: When the envoys entered, the emperor wept.
entries.literal: When the envoys entered the gate, the emperor wept.

entries.zh: 使者詣柩前上香，讀祭文訖，又哭。
entries.en: The envoys went before the bier to burn incense; when the elegy had been read, they wept again.
entries.literal: The envoys went before the bier to burn incense; when the elegy had been read, they wept again.

entries.zh: 有司讀遺詔，慟哭。
entries.en: The responsible offices read the late emperor's testament, and bitter wailing broke out.
entries.literal: The proper offices read the testament; there was bitter wailing.

entries.zh: 使者出，少頃，復入，陳賻赗於柩前，皇帝入臨哭。
entries.en: The envoys withdrew; after a short while they entered again and presented funerary gifts before the bier; the emperor came in person to mourn and weep.
entries.literal: The envoys withdrew; after a short while they entered again and displayed funerary gifts before the bier; the emperor came in to mourn and weep.

entries.zh: 退，更衣禦遊仙殿南之幄殿。
entries.en: He withdrew, changed his garments, and took his seat in the tent hall south of the Youxian Hall.
entries.literal: He withdrew, changed his garments, and presided in the tent hall south of the Youxian Hall.

entries.zh: 使者入見且辭，敕有司賜宴於館。
entries.en: The envoys entered for an audience and took their leave; he ordered the responsible offices to grant them a banquet at their lodging.
entries.literal: The envoys entered for an audience and took their leave; he ordered the proper offices to grant a banquet at their lodging.

entries.zh: 禮志二 ○凶儀
entries.en: Treatise on Rites II — Mourning and Funeral Rites
entries.literal: Rites Treatise, Part Two ○ Inauspicious Rites

entries.zh: 遼有國樂，有雅樂，有大樂，有散樂，有鐃歌、橫吹樂。
entries.en: The Liao possessed state music, court ritual music, great music, popular miscellaneous music, nao drum songs, and horizontal-flute music.
entries.literal: The Liao had state music, ritual music, great music, miscellaneous music, nao songs, and horizontal-flute music.

entries.zh: 舊史稱聖宗、興宗咸通音律，聲氣、歌辭、舞節，徵諸太常、儀鳳、教坊不可得。
entries.en: Earlier histories report that Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong were fully conversant with pitch and rhythm, yet the timbres, lyrics, and dance patterns could not be recovered from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Office of Ceremonial Phoenixes, or the Training Bureau.
entries.literal: Old histories say that Emperors Shengzong and Xingzong were thoroughly versed in pitch and rhythm, but sounds and airs, song texts, and dance measures—sought from the Court of Imperial Sacrifices, the Office of Ceremonial Phoenixes, and the Training Bureau—could not be obtained.

entries.zh: 按《紀》、《志》、《遼朝雜禮》，參考史籍，定其可知者，以補一代之闕文。
entries.en: Drawing on the annals, treatises, and Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao, and consulting other historical sources, I have set down what can be established, to repair the gaps left in the record of that dynasty.
entries.literal: According to the Annals, Treatises, and Miscellaneous Rites of the Liao Dynasty, consulting historical records, I fix what can be known to fill the lacunae of an age.

entries.zh: 聖宗太平元年，尊號冊禮，設宮懸於殿庭，舉麾位在殿第三重西階之上，協律郎各人就舉麾位，太常博士引太常卿，太常卿引皇帝。
entries.en: In the first year of Taiping, at Emperor Shengzong's ceremony for the bestowal of an honorific title, full suspended bells were installed in the palace courtyard. The baton stations stood on the west steps of the hall's third tier; each pitch-tuning officer took his station; a Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, and the Director led the emperor.
entries.literal: In the first year of Taiping, Emperor Shengzong, at the ceremony for the honorific title, suspended bells were set in the palace courtyard; the baton positions were on the west steps of the third tier of the hall; each pitch-tuning officer took his baton position; Court of Imperial Sacrifices academicians led the Director, the Director led the emperor.

entries.zh: 將仗動，協律郎舉麾，太樂令令撞黃鐘之鐘，左右鐘皆應。
entries.en: As the insignia were about to move, the pitch-tuning officer raised his baton; the Director of Music ordered the Yellow Bell pitch bell struck, and the bells on both sides answered.
entries.literal: When the insignia were about to move, the pitch-tuning officer raised the baton; the Director of Music ordered the Yellow Bell pitch bell struck, and the bells left and right all responded.

entries.zh: 工人舉，樂作；
entries.en: The musicians raised their instruments and the music began;
entries.literal: The musicians raised [their instruments], music sounded;

entries.zh: 皇帝即御坐，扇合，樂止。
entries.en: the emperor took the throne, the fans were closed, and the music ceased.
entries.literal: the emperor took the imperial seat, fans were folded, music stopped.

entries.zh: 王公入門，樂作；
entries.en: When princes and dukes entered the gate, music sounded;
entries.literal: When princes and dukes entered the gate, music sounded;

entries.zh: 至位，樂止。
entries.en: when they reached their places, the music stopped.
entries.literal: when they reached position, music stopped.

entries.zh: 通事舍人引押冊大臣初動，樂作；
entries.en: The protocol officer led the minister bearing the document of investiture at the first movement, and music sounded;
entries.literal: The protocol officer led the minister escorting the register at the first movement, music sounded;

entries.zh: 置冊殿前香案訖，就位，樂止。
entries.en: when the document had been set on the incense table before the hall and they had taken their places, the music stopped.
entries.literal: when the register was placed on the incense table before the hall and they took position, music stopped.

entries.zh: 舁冊官奉冊，初動，樂作；
entries.en: The officers carrying the document of investiture presented it; at the first movement, music sounded;
entries.literal: The officers bearing the register presented it; at the first movement, music sounded;

entries.zh: 升殿，置冊御坐前，就西墉北上位，樂止。
entries.en: they ascended the hall, set the document before the throne, and took their places north of the west parapet; the music stopped.
entries.literal: they ascended the hall, placed the register before the imperial seat, and took position north of the west parapet; music stopped.

entries.zh: 大臣上殿，樂作；
entries.en: When the minister ascended the hall, music sounded;
entries.literal: When the minister ascended the hall, music sounded;

entries.zh: 至殿欄內位，樂止。
entries.en: when he reached his place inside the hall railing, the music stopped.
entries.literal: when he reached position inside the hall railing, music stopped.

entries.zh: 大臣降殿階，樂作；
entries.en: When the minister descended the hall steps, music sounded;
entries.literal: When the minister descended the hall steps, music sounded;

entries.zh: 復位，樂止。
entries.en: when he returned to his place, the music stopped.
entries.literal: when he returned to position, music stopped.

entries.zh: 王公三品以上出，樂作；
entries.en: When princes and dukes of the third rank and above withdrew, music sounded;
entries.literal: When princes and dukes of the third rank and above departed, music sounded;

entries.zh: 太常博士引太常卿，太常卿引皇帝降御坐入閣，樂止。
entries.en: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, and the Director led the emperor down from the throne into the side chamber; the music stopped.
entries.literal: A Court of Imperial Sacrifices academician led the Director, the Director led the emperor down from the imperial seat into the side chamber; music stopped.

entries.zh: 聖宗統和元年，冊承天皇太后，設宮懸、簨虡，太樂工、協律郎入。
entries.en: In the first year of Tonghe, at Emperor Shengzong’s investiture of Empress Dowager Chengtian, full suspended bells and music frames were installed; musicians of the Grand Music Office and pitch-tuning officers took their places.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tonghe, Emperor Shengzong, at the investiture of Empress Dowager Chengtian, suspended bells and music frames were set up; musicians of the Grand Music Office and pitch-tuning officers entered.

entries.zh: 太后儀衛動，舉麾，《太和》樂作；
entries.en: When the empress dowager's guards moved, the baton was raised and the music Taihe began;
entries.literal: When the empress dowager's guards moved, the baton was raised and the music Taihe sounded;

entries.zh: 太樂令、太常卿導引升御坐，簾卷，樂止。
entries.en: the Director of Music and the Director of the Court of Imperial Sacrifices led her up to the throne, the curtains were raised, and the music ceased.
