entries.en: During Emperor Shengzong's Taiping reign, gold and silver deposits were found north of the Yin Mountains along the Huang River and at the headwaters of the Liao River, and smelting operations were opened.
entries.literal: During Shengzong's Taiping era, north of the Yin Mountains along the Huang River and at the source of the Liao River, gold and silver mines were each obtained, and smelting and extraction were undertaken.

entries.zh: 自此以訖天祚，國家皆賴其利。
entries.en: From that time until Tianzuo's reign, the state depended on these revenues.
entries.literal: From this until Tianzuo, the state all relied on their profit.

entries.zh: 鼓鑄之法，先代撒剌的為夷離堇，以土產多銅，始造錢幣。
entries.en: Coinage began in an earlier generation when Saladi served as yilijin: local copper was abundant, and he was the first to cast money.
entries.literal: As for the method of casting coins, in a former generation Saladi served as yilijin; because local products had much copper, he first made currency.

entries.zh: 太祖其子，襲而用之，遂致富強，以開帝業。
entries.en: Taizu, his son, adopted the practice and grew wealthy and powerful enough to found the dynasty.
entries.literal: Taizu was his son; he inherited and used it, and thereby grew rich and strong to open the imperial enterprise.

entries.zh: 太宗置五冶太師，以總四方錢鐵。
entries.en: Taizong appointed a Grand Master of the Five Smelteries to supervise coinage and ironworks throughout the realm.
entries.literal: Taizong established the Five Smelteries Grand Master to oversee money and iron in all directions.

entries.zh: 石敬瑭又獻沿邊所積錢，以備軍實。
entries.en: Shi Jingtang further presented hoarded border-region coin to provision the armies.
entries.literal: Shi Jingtang also presented the accumulated money along the border to prepare military supplies.

entries.zh: 景宗以舊錢不足於用，始鑄乾亨新錢，錢用流布。
entries.en: When old coin proved inadequate, Emperor Jingzong introduced new Qianheng currency, which circulated widely.
entries.literal: Jingzong, because old money was insufficient for use, first cast new Qianheng coins, and currency circulated broadly.

entries.zh: 聖宗鑿大安山，取劉守光所藏錢，散諸五計司，兼鑄太平錢，新舊互用。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong opened Da'an Mountain, recovered the treasure Liu Shouguang had buried there, distributed it among the five accounting offices, and cast Taiping coin alongside the old issues.
entries.literal: Shengzong excavated Da'an Mountain, took the money Liu Shouguang had stored, distributed it among the five accounting offices, and also cast Taiping coins; new and old were used together.

entries.zh: 由是國家之錢，演迤域中。
entries.en: National currency thus spread throughout the realm.
entries.literal: From this the state's money spread throughout the realm.

entries.zh: 所以統和出內藏錢，賜南京諸軍司。
entries.en: During the Tonghe era, funds from the inner treasury were distributed to the military commissions of the Southern Capital.
entries.literal: Therefore in Tonghe internal treasury money was disbursed and bestowed on the various military commissions of the Southern Capital.

entries.zh: 開泰中詔諸道，貧乏百姓，有典質男女，計傭價日以十文，折盡還父母。
entries.en: In the Kaitai era an edict to all circuits ordered that impoverished subjects who had pawned children should redeem them at ten cash per day of service until the debt was cleared and the children restored to their parents.
entries.literal: In Kaitai an edict to all circuits stated that for impoverished commoners who had pawned sons and daughters, hire price was reckoned at ten cash per day, and when fully paid they were returned to their parents.

entries.zh: 每歲春秋，以官錢宴饗將士，錢不勝多，故東京所鑄至清寧中始用。
entries.en: Each spring and autumn the court feasted officers and soldiers with official coin; supply so exceeded demand that Eastern Capital coinage was not brought into circulation until the Qingning era.
entries.literal: Every spring and autumn official money was used to feast and reward officers and soldiers; money was more than could be used up, so what the Eastern Capital cast was not put into use until the Qingning era.

entries.zh: 是時，詔禁諸路不得貨銅鐵，以防私鑄，又禁銅鐵賣入回鶻，法益嚴矣。
entries.en: Edicts then barred all circuits from trading in copper and iron to prevent illicit minting and from selling metal to the Uyghurs—regulations that grew ever stricter.
entries.literal: At that time an edict forbade all circuits from selling copper and iron to prevent private casting, and also forbade selling copper and iron into the Uyghurs; the law grew stricter.

entries.zh: 道宗之世，錢有四等：曰咸雍，曰大康，曰大安，曰壽隆，皆因改元易名。
entries.en: Under Emperor Daozong four coin types were issued—Xianyong, Dakang, Da'an, and Shoulong—each renamed with a new reign era.
entries.literal: In Daozong's age there were four grades of coin: called Xianyong, Dakang, Da'an, and Shoulong, all renamed with each change of reign title.

entries.zh: 其肉好、銖數亦無所考。
entries.en: The dimensions, hole size, and weight in zhu cannot be determined from surviving records.
entries.literal: Their rims, holes, and weight in zhu also have nothing by which they can be examined.

entries.zh: 第詔楊遵勖征戶部司逋戶舊錢，得四十餘萬繦，拜樞密直學士；
entries.en: An edict sent Yang Zunxu to collect delinquent old coin owed to the Households Bureau; he recovered more than four hundred thousand strings and was made privy council academician;
entries.literal: Only an edict ordered Yang Zunxu to collect old money from delinquent households of the Households Bureau, obtaining more than four hundred thousand strings, and he was appointed Academician of the Privy Council;

entries.zh: 劉伸為戶部使，歲入羨余錢三十萬繦，擢南院樞密使。
entries.en: Liu Shen, as households commissioner, delivered three hundred thousand strings in annual surplus and was promoted to privy councilor of the Southern Chancellery.
entries.literal: Liu Shen served as Households Commissioner; annual surplus money of three hundred thousand strings was submitted, and he was promoted to Southern Chancellery Privy Councilor.

entries.zh: 其以災沴，出錢以振貧乏及諸宮分邊戍人戶。
entries.en: When disasters struck, coin was issued to relieve the poor and to support palace estates and frontier garrison households.
entries.literal: Because of disasters and calamities, money was disbursed to relieve the impoverished and the various palace estates and frontier garrison households.

entries.zh: 是時，雖未有貫朽不可較之積，亦可謂富矣。
entries.en: Though the treasury had not yet reached the proverbial heaps of cash rotting on the strings, the state could fairly be called prosperous.
entries.literal: At that time, although there was not yet an accumulation of strings rotting beyond reckoning, it could still be called wealthy.

entries.zh: 至其末年，經費浩穰，鼓鑄仍舊，國用不給。
entries.en: In his final years expenditures swelled while minting continued unchanged, and revenue no longer met demand.
entries.literal: By his final years expenditures were vast and heavy, casting continued as before, and state use was not supplied.

entries.zh: 雖以海雲佛寺千萬之助，受而不拒，尋禁民錢不得出境。
entries.en: Though a donation of tens of millions from Haiyun Monastery was accepted without demur, private coin was soon barred from leaving the realm.
entries.literal: Although aid of tens of millions from Haiyun Buddhist Temple was accepted without refusal, soon commoners' money was forbidden to leave the borders.

entries.zh: 天祚之世，更鑄乾統、天慶二等新錢，而上下窮困，府庫無餘積。
entries.en: Under Emperor Tianzuo new Qiantong and Tianqing coin were minted, yet court and country alike were destitute and the treasuries held no reserve.
entries.literal: In Tianzuo's age, new Qiantong and Tianqing coins of two grades were further cast, yet above and below were impoverished and the treasuries had no surplus accumulation.

entries.zh: 始太祖為叠烈府夷離堇也，懲遙輦氏單弱，於是撫諸部，明賞罰，不妄征討，因民之利而利之，群牧蓄息，上下給足。
entries.en: When Taizu was yilijin of the Dielie prefecture, mindful of the Yaolian clan's weakness, he conciliated the tribes, enforced clear rewards and punishments, refrained from reckless campaigns, and pursued policies that enriched the people. Herds multiplied, and court and camp alike had enough.
entries.literal: When Taizu first served as yilijin of the Dielie Prefecture, he took warning from the weakness of the Yaolian clan; therefore he comforted the various tribes, clarified rewards and punishments, did not rashly campaign, profited where the people profited, herds multiplied and were nurtured, and above and below had sufficient supply.

entries.zh: 及即位，伐河東，下代北郡縣，獲牛、羊、駝、馬十餘萬。
entries.en: After his accession he campaigned in Hedong, seized the commanderies north of Dai, and captured more than a hundred thousand head of cattle, sheep, camels, and horses.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, he campaigned in Hedong, took the commanderies and counties north of Dai, and obtained more than a hundred thousand oxen, sheep, camels, and horses.

entries.zh: 樞密使耶律斜軫討女直，復獲馬二十餘萬，分牧水草便地，數歲所增不勝算。
entries.en: Privy councilor Yelü Xiezhen campaigned against the Jurchen and captured another two hundred thousand horses, which were pastured on favorable grazing grounds; within a few years the herds had grown beyond reckoning.
entries.literal: Privy Councilor Yelü Xiezhen campaigned against the Jurchen and again obtained more than two hundred thousand horses, distributed to pasture at convenient water and grasslands, and within several years the increase could not be calculated.

entries.zh: 當時括富人馬不加多，賜大、小鶻軍萬餘匹不加少，蓋畜牧有法然也。
entries.en: When wealthy households' herds were inventoried, the totals did not swell; when more than ten thousand horses were granted to the Great and Small Hawk Armies, the national herds did not shrink—pasturage was governed by sound regulation.
entries.literal: At that time when rich men's horses were inventoried they were not increased beyond count, and when more than ten thousand were bestowed on the Great and Small Hawk Armies they were not diminished—probably because herding had method.

entries.zh: 咸雍五年，蕭陶隗為馬群太保，上書猶言群牧名存實亡，上下相欺，宜括實數以為定籍。
entries.en: In Xianyong year 5, Xiao Taokui, grand guardian of horse herds, memorialized that herd administration existed in name only, officials and tribesmen deceived one another, and a true census should be taken to establish a fixed register.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Xianyong, Xiao Taokui served as Grand Guardian of Horse Herds and memorialized that the name of herd administration remained but the substance was gone, above and below deceived one another, and real numbers should be inventoried to make a fixed register.

entries.zh: 厥後東丹國歲貢千匹，女直萬匹，直不古等國萬匹，阻卜及吾獨婉、惕德各二萬匹，西夏、室韋各三百匹，越裏篤、剖阿裏、奧裏米、蒲奴裏、鐵驪等諸部三百匹；
entries.en: Thereafter annual tribute included a thousand horses from Dongdan, ten thousand from the Jurchen, ten thousand from Zhibugu and allied states, twenty thousand each from Zubu, Wuduwann, and Tede, three hundred each from Western Xia and the Shiwei, and three hundred each from tribes including Yuelidu, Pou'ali, Aolimi, Punuli, and Tieli;
entries.literal: Thereafter Dongdan State annually presented a thousand horses, Jurchen ten thousand, Zhibugu and other states ten thousand, Zubu and Wuduwann, Tede each twenty thousand, Western Xia and Shiwei each three hundred, Yuelidu, Pou'ali, Aolimi, Punuli, Tieli and other tribes three hundred;

entries.zh: 仍禁朔州路羊馬入宋，吐渾、党項馬鬻於夏。
entries.en: Sheep and horses on the Shuozhou route were barred from sale to Song territory, and Tuhun and Tangut horses from sale to Western Xia.
entries.literal: Sheep and horses on the Shuozhou route were still forbidden to enter Song, and Tuhun and Tangut horses were forbidden to be sold to Xia.

entries.zh: 以故群牧滋繁，數至百有餘萬，諸司牧官以次進階。
entries.en: Herds therefore flourished until they exceeded a million head, and pasture officials were promoted in steady succession.
entries.literal: For this reason herds multiplied and flourished, reaching more than a million in number, and herd officials of the various offices were promoted in turn.

entries.zh: 自太祖及興宗垂二百年，群牧之盛如一日。
entries.en: From Taizu through Emperor Xingzong, nearly two centuries, the herds remained as abundant as on a single prosperous day.
entries.literal: From Taizu through Xingzong, spanning nearly two hundred years, the flourishing of herds was like a single day.

entries.zh: 天祚初年，馬猶有數萬群，每群不下千匹。
entries.en: Early in Tianzuo's reign tens of thousands of herds still remained, each numbering no fewer than a thousand horses.
entries.literal: In the early years of Tianzuo, horses still had tens of thousands of herds, each herd no fewer than a thousand head.

entries.zh: 祖宗舊制，常選南征馬數萬匹，牧於雄、霸、清、滄間，以備燕、雲緩急；
entries.en: By ancestral regulation tens of thousands of campaign horses were pastured between Xiong, Ba, Qing, and Cang to meet emergencies in the Yan and Yun regions;
entries.literal: The ancestral old system regularly selected tens of thousands of southern campaign horses to pasture between Xiong, Ba, Qing, and Cang, to prepare for Yan and Yun emergencies;

entries.zh: 復選數萬，給四時遊畋；
entries.en: another several tens of thousands were set aside for the four seasons of imperial hunts;
entries.literal: and again selected tens of thousands to supply the four seasons of hunting excursions;

entries.zh: 餘則分地以牧。
entries.en: the remainder were distributed to pasture by district.
entries.literal: the remainder were apportioned by land to pasture.

entries.zh: 法至善也。
entries.en: The system was admirably conceived.
entries.literal: The law was most excellent.

entries.zh: 至末年，累與金戰，番漢戰馬損十六七，雖增價數倍，竟無所買，乃冒法買官馬從軍。
entries.en: In his final years, after repeated wars with the Jin, Khitan and Han campaign horses were lost at a rate of six or seven in ten. Prices were raised several times over, yet no horses could be procured; men violated the law by purchasing government horses for military service.
entries.literal: By the final years, after repeated wars with Jin, Khitan and Han campaign horses were lost by six or seven tenths; although prices were raised several fold, in the end nothing could be bought, and they violated the law to buy official horses to follow the army.

entries.zh: 諸群牧私賣日多，畋獵亦不足用，遂為金所敗。
entries.en: Official herds were sold off illicitly with growing frequency, even the hunt lacked mounts, and the dynasty was overrun by the Jin.
entries.literal: The various herds were privately sold day by day, hunting excursions also had insufficient supply, and they were thereby defeated by Jin.

entries.zh: 棄眾播遷，以訖於亡。
entries.en: The emperor abandoned his followers and fled into exile until the state perished.
entries.literal: Abandoning the masses and wandering in exile, it ended in destruction.

entries.zh: 松漠以北舊馬，皆為大石林牙所有。
entries.en: The herds north of Songmo all passed to Yelü Dashi, the linya.
entries.literal: The old horses north of Songmo all came into the possession of Dashi Linya.

entries.zh: 食貨志下
entries.en: Finance and Economics, Part Two
entries.literal: Treatise on Food and Goods, Part Two

entries.zh: 刑也者，始於兵而終於禮者也。
entries.en: Punishment begins with arms and ends with ritual — that is its nature.
entries.literal: Punishment is that which begins with military force and ends with ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 鴻荒之代，生民有兵，如蜂有螫，自衛而已。
entries.en: In the earliest ages, people bore arms as bees bear stings — solely to defend themselves.
entries.literal: In the age of primordial chaos, the living people had arms, like bees have stings — for self-defense alone.

entries.zh: 蚩尤惟始作亂，斯民鴟義，奸宄並作，刑之用豈能已乎？
entries.en: When Chiyou first rose in revolt, the people turned violent and treacherous; with crime rampant, how could punishment be set aside?
entries.literal: Only when Chiyou first raised rebellion did this people turn fierce and lawless; treachery and wickedness arose together — how could the use of punishment ever cease?

entries.zh: 帝堯清問下民，乃命三後恤功於民，伯夷降典，折民惟刑，故曰刑也者，始於兵而終於禮者也。
entries.en: Emperor Yao sought the people's counsel and charged the Three Lords to care for their welfare; Boyi issued the penal code and judged the people by law alone — hence the saying that punishment begins with arms and ends with ritual.
entries.literal: Emperor Yao inquired deeply among the people below, then ordered the Three Lords to show concern for the people's achievements, and Boyi brought down the statutes, adjudicating the people solely by punishment — hence it is said that punishment begins with military force and ends with ritual propriety.

entries.zh: 先王順天地四時以建六卿。
entries.en: The ancient kings aligned the Six Ministries with Heaven, Earth, and the four seasons.
entries.literal: The former kings followed Heaven and Earth and the four seasons in establishing the Six Ministers.

entries.zh: 秋，刑官也，象時之成物焉。
entries.en: Autumn is the season of punishment, when the harvest is gathered in.
entries.literal: Autumn is the minister of punishment, symbolizing the season's completion of things.

entries.zh: 秋傳氣於夏，變色於春，推可知也。
entries.en: Autumn draws its force from summer and takes its hue from spring — from this one may infer the rest.
entries.literal: Autumn transmits its qi from summer and changes color from spring — by extension this may be understood.

entries.zh: 遼以用武立國，禁暴戢奸，莫先於刑。
entries.en: The Liao founded their state by force of arms; to curb violence and suppress crime, punishment came first.
entries.literal: Liao established its state by the use of arms; to restrain violence and suppress wickedness, nothing comes before punishment.

entries.zh: 國初制法，有出於五服、三就之外者，兵之勢方張，禮之用未遑也。
entries.en: At the founding of the realm, some laws went beyond the traditional five degrees of kinship and three places of exile — military power was still ascendant, and ritual governance had yet to take hold.
entries.literal: When the state was first founded and laws were made, some provisions went beyond the five degrees of mourning kinship and the three places of exile — the momentum of arms was still expanding, and the application of ritual had not yet been attended to.

entries.zh: 及阻午可汗知宗室雅裏之賢，命為夷離堇以掌刑辟，豈非士師之官，非賢者不可為乎？
entries.en: When Khan Zuwu saw the talent of Yali in the imperial house, he made him yilijin to oversee justice — was this not the post of chief judge, fit only for a man of merit?
entries.literal: When Khan Zuwu recognized the worth of Yali of the imperial clan, he appointed him yilijin to oversee criminal matters — was this not the office of the Minister of Punishment, which none but the worthy could hold?

entries.zh: 太祖、太宗經理疆土，擐甲之士歲無寧居，威克厥愛，理勢然也。
entries.en: Under Taizu and Taizong, who consolidated the realm, armored men knew no year of rest — severity prevailed over mercy, as the times required.
entries.literal: Taizu and Taizong administered the realm's territory; men in armor had no peaceful year — severity overcame kindness, as reason and circumstance demanded.

entries.zh: 子孫相繼，其法互有輕重；
entries.en: Successive rulers inherited the throne, and the laws varied in severity;
entries.literal: Their descendants succeeded one another, and their laws varied in severity and leniency;

entries.zh: 中間能審權宜，終之以禮者，惟景、聖二宗為優耳。
entries.en: Of those who could weigh circumstances wisely and bring punishment to rest in ritual, only the Jing and Sheng emperors stand out.
entries.literal: Among them, only the Jing and Sheng emperors, who could weigh expedients and conclude with ritual propriety, were truly superior.

entries.zh: 然其制刑之凡有四：曰死，曰流，曰徒，曰杖。
entries.en: Their penal system, however, had four main categories: death, exile, penal servitude, and corporal beating.
entries.literal: Yet in general their punishments were of four kinds: death, exile, penal servitude, and beating.

entries.zh: 死刑有絞、斬、淩遲之屬，又有籍沒之法。
entries.en: Capital crimes were punished by strangulation, beheading, or lingchi, and there was also confiscation of property and kin.
entries.literal: Capital punishment included strangulation, decapitation, and dismemberment by slow slicing, and there was also the law of confiscation and enslavement.

entries.zh: 流刑量罪輕重，置之邊城部族之地，遠則投諸境外，又遠則罰使絕域。
entries.en: Exile was graded by offense: lesser crimes sent one to border garrisons and tribal lands; graver ones beyond the frontier; the gravest to the farthest reaches of the empire.
entries.literal: Exile was meted according to the severity of the crime, placing offenders in border towns and tribal lands; farther still, they were cast beyond the frontier; farther yet, they were punished by dispatch to the remotest regions.

entries.zh: 徒刑一曰終身，二曰五年，三曰一年半；
entries.en: Penal servitude had three terms: lifetime, five years, and eighteen months;
entries.literal: Penal servitude was of three terms: one called lifetime, one five years, and one a year and a half;

entries.zh: 終身者決五百，其次遞減百；
entries.en: the lifetime term carried five hundred strokes, with each lesser term reduced by one hundred;
entries.literal: for lifetime, five hundred strokes were decreed; for the next term, one hundred fewer in succession;

entries.zh: 又有黥刺之法。
entries.en: and branding and tattooing were also prescribed.
entries.literal: there was also the method of tattooing and branding.

entries.zh: 仗刑自五十至三百，凡杖五十以上者，以沙袋決之；
entries.en: Corporal punishment ran from fifty to three hundred strokes; for fifty strokes or more, the sandbag cudgel was used;
entries.literal: Beating ranged from fifty to three hundred strokes; for all beatings of fifty strokes or more, the sandbag was used to administer them;

entries.zh: 又有木劍、大棒、鐵骨朵之法。
entries.en: along with the wooden sword, great club, and iron mace.
entries.literal: there were also the methods of the wooden sword, the great club, and the iron mace.

entries.zh: 木劍、大棒之數三，自十五至三十，鐵骨朵之數，或五、或七。
entries.en: The wooden sword and great club had three grades, from fifteen to thirty blows; the iron mace was used in sets of five or seven.
entries.literal: The wooden sword and great club had three gradations, from fifteen to thirty strokes; the iron mace was applied in numbers of either five or seven.

entries.zh: 有重罪者，將決以沙袋，先於脽骨之上及四周擊之。
entries.en: Before a heavy sandbag sentence was carried out, blows were first delivered to the buttocks and surrounding area.
entries.literal: For those with grave offenses about to be sentenced with the sandbag, blows were first struck upon the buttocks and all around them.

entries.zh: 拷訊之具，有粗、細杖及鞭、烙法。
entries.en: Interrogation employed thick and thin rods, whipping, and branding.
entries.literal: Instruments for interrogation included thick and thin rods, as well as the methods of whipping and branding.

entries.zh: 粗杖之數二十；
entries.en: The thick rod: twenty strokes;
entries.literal: the thick rod was applied in a count of twenty;

entries.zh: 細杖之數三，自三十至於六十。
entries.en: the thin rod: three grades, from thirty to sixty strokes.
entries.literal: the thin rod had three gradations, from thirty to sixty.

entries.zh: 鞭、烙之數，凡烙三十者鞭三百，烙五十者鞭五百。
entries.en: Branding and whipping were paired: thirty brands meant three hundred lashes; fifty brands meant five hundred.
entries.literal: For whipping and branding, whoever received thirty brands was whipped three hundred times; whoever received fifty brands was whipped five hundred times.

entries.zh: 被告諸事應伏而不服者，以此訊之。
entries.en: Defendants who should have confessed but refused were interrogated by these methods.
entries.literal: When the accused in any matter ought to confess but would not submit, they were examined by these means.

entries.zh: 品官公事誤犯，民年七十以上、十五以下犯罪者，聽以贖論。
entries.en: Officials who erred in office, and commoners over seventy or under fifteen who committed crimes, were allowed to commute their sentences by fine.
entries.literal: Ranked officials who erred in public duties, and commoners seventy years of age or above or fifteen and below who committed offenses, were permitted to redeem punishment by payment.

entries.zh: 贖銅之數，杖一百者，輸錢千。
entries.en: The redemption tariff was set at one thousand cash for every hundred strokes.
entries.literal: The scale for redeeming with copper: for one hundred strokes of the rod, one thousand coins were paid.

entries.zh: 亦有八議、八縱之法。
entries.en: The Eight Privileges and Eight Pardons were also in force.
entries.literal: There were also the Eight Privileges and the Eight Pardons.

entries.zh: 籍沒之法，始自太祖為撻馬狘沙裏時，奉痕德堇可汗命，按於越釋魯遇害事，以其首惡家屬沒入瓦裏。
entries.en: Confiscation began when Taizu, still tamag yaglashi, was ordered by Khan Hendejin to investigate the murder of Yuyue Shilu; the ringleader's family was seized and enrolled in the wali.
entries.literal: The law of confiscation began when Taizu, as tamag yaglashi, received orders from Khan Hendejin to investigate the murder of Yuyue Shilu, and the chief culprit's household was confiscated into the wali.

entries.zh: 及淳欽皇后時析出，以為著帳郎君，至世宗詔免之。
entries.en: Under Empress Chunqin they were set apart as registered-account gentlemen; Shizong later issued an edict releasing them.
entries.literal: Under Empress Chunqin they were separated out and made registered-account gentlemen; by Shizong's edict they were finally exempted.

entries.zh: 其後內外戚屬及世官之家，犯反逆等罪，復沒入焉；
entries.en: Later, collateral kin and hereditary official families convicted of treason and like crimes were again subject to confiscation;
entries.literal: Afterward, when collateral kin inside and outside the clan and hereditary official households committed crimes such as treason, they were again confiscated;

entries.zh: 餘人則沒為著帳戶；
entries.en: others were reduced to registered-account households;
entries.literal: the rest were confiscated as registered-account households;

entries.zh: 其沒入宮分、分賜臣下者亦有之。
entries.en: some property went to the palace treasury, some was distributed among officials.
entries.literal: some were confiscated into the palace estates, and some were distributed as gifts to subordinates.

entries.zh: 木劍、大棒者，太宗時制。
entries.en: The wooden sword and great club were introduced under Taizong.
entries.literal: The wooden sword and great club were instituted in Taizong's time.

entries.zh: 木劍面平背隆，大臣犯重罪，欲寬宥則擊之。
entries.en: The wooden sword was flat on one side and ridged on the other; when a senior minister merited death but the emperor wished mercy, he was struck with this instead.
entries.literal: The wooden sword had a flat face and a raised back; when great ministers committed grave offenses and the emperor wished to show leniency, they were struck with it.

entries.zh: 沙袋者，穆宗時制，其制用熟皮合縫之，長六寸，廣二寸，柄一尺許。
entries.en: The sandbag cudgel was introduced under Muzong: cured leather sewn into a bag six inches long and two inches wide, on a handle about a foot long.
entries.literal: The sandbag was instituted in Muzong's time; it was made of cured leather sewn together, six inches long, two inches wide, with a handle about one foot.

entries.zh: 徒刑之數詳於重熙制，杖刑以下之數詳於咸雍制；
entries.en: Penal servitude was codified in detail under the Chongxi code; corporal punishments and lesser penalties under the Xianyong code;
entries.literal: The numbers for penal servitude are detailed in the Chongxi regulations; the numbers for beating and below are detailed in the Xianyong regulations;

entries.zh: 其餘非常用而無定式者，不可殫紀。
entries.en: the rest — irregular punishments without fixed rules — are too numerous to list in full.
entries.literal: as for the rest that were not in regular use and had no fixed form, they cannot all be recorded.

entries.zh: 太祖初年，庶事草創，犯罪者量輕重決之。
entries.en: In Taizu's early reign, with institutions still taking shape, offenders were sentenced according to the gravity of their crimes.
entries.literal: In Taizu's early years, when all affairs were still being established, offenders were judged according to the severity of their crimes.

entries.zh: 其後治諸弟逆黨，權宜立法。
entries.en: Later, in suppressing his brothers' rebellion, he enacted ad hoc laws suited to the emergency.
entries.literal: Later, in punishing the rebellious faction of his younger brothers, he made laws as expedients required.

entries.zh: 親王從逆，不磬諸甸人，或投高崖殺之；
entries.en: Imperial princes who joined the revolt were not publicly executed before the assembled domains, but were sometimes hurled from high cliffs;
entries.literal: Imperial princes who followed the rebellion were not executed by the qing method before the assembled people of the domains, but were sometimes cast from high cliffs to their death;

entries.zh: 淫亂不軌者，五車轘殺之；
entries.en: those guilty of sexual misconduct were torn apart by five teams of horses;
entries.literal: those guilty of licentiousness and misconduct were killed by drawing and quartering with five carts;

entries.zh: 逆父母者視此；
entries.en: those who defied their parents received the same punishment;
entries.literal: those who defied their parents were treated likewise;

entries.zh: 訕詈犯上者，以熟鐵錐摏其口殺之。
entries.en: those who slandered their superiors were killed by driving a red-hot iron spike through the mouth.
entries.literal: those who slandered and reviled their superiors were killed by driving a heated iron awl through the mouth.

entries.zh: 從坐者，量罪輕重杖決。
entries.en: Accomplices were beaten in proportion to their guilt.
entries.literal: Accomplices were beaten according to the severity of their offenses.

entries.zh: 杖有二：大者重錢五百，小者三百。
entries.en: Two grades of rod were used: the heavy rod weighed five hundred cash, the light three hundred.
entries.literal: There were two kinds of beating: the great rod weighed five hundred cash, the small three hundred.

entries.zh: 又為梟磔、生瘞、射鬼箭、炮擲、支解之刑。
entries.en: He also instituted exposure of the head, dismemberment, live burial, ghost-arrow execution, catapulting, and hacking to pieces.
entries.literal: He also established the punishments of exposure of the head, dismemberment, live burial, shooting with ghost arrows, cannon-throwing, and hacking apart.

entries.zh: 歸於重法，閑民使不為變耳。
entries.en: These harsh measures were meant to keep the common people from stirring trouble.
entries.literal: All this came under severe law, to keep the common people from making trouble.

entries.zh: 歲癸酉，下詔曰：「朕自北征以來，四方獄訟，積滯頗多。
entries.en: In the guiyou year, an edict declared: "Since our northern campaigns began, lawsuits from across the realm have piled up in great numbers.
entries.literal: In the year guiyou, an edict was issued: "Since Our northern campaigns began, lawsuits from the four quarters have piled up in considerable backlog.

entries.zh: 今休戰息民，群臣其副朕意，詳決之，無或冤枉。」
entries.en: Now that war has ceased and the people may rest, let my ministers assist my intent, judge cases carefully, and permit no wrongful conviction."
entries.literal: Now that warfare has ceased and the people rest, let the ministers assist Our intent, adjudicate carefully, and allow no wrongful conviction."

entries.zh: 乃命北府宰相蕭敵魯等分道疏決。
entries.en: He then ordered Northern Chancellery Chief Minister Xiao Dilu and others to clear the backlog in separate jurisdictions.
entries.literal: He then ordered Northern Chancellery Chief Minister Xiao Dilu and others to clear the backlog by separate routes.

entries.zh: 有遼欽恤之意，昉見於此。
entries.en: The Liao concern for compassionate review of cases first appears here.
entries.literal: The Liao's intent of compassionate review first appeared in this.

entries.zh: 神冊六年，克定諸夷，上謂侍臣曰：「凡國家庶務，巨細各殊，若憲度不明，則何以為治，群下亦何由知禁。」
entries.en: In the sixth year of Shence, after pacifying the tribes, the emperor told his attendants: "State affairs great and small all differ — if the laws are unclear, how can the realm be governed, and how can subjects know what is forbidden?"
entries.literal: In the sixth year of Shence, after subduing the various tribes, the emperor said to his attending ministers: "In all the state's common affairs, great and small each differ — if statutes and measures are not clear, how can there be governance, and how can subordinates know what is forbidden?"

entries.zh: 乃詔大臣定治契丹及諸夷之法，漢人則斷以《律令》，仍置鐘院以達民冤。
entries.en: He ordered his ministers to codify laws for the Khitan and other tribes; Han subjects were to be judged under the Tang code, and the Bell Court was established so the people's grievances could reach the throne.
entries.literal: He then ordered the great ministers to fix laws for governing the Khitan and the various tribes; Han Chinese were to be judged by the Statutes and Ordinances, and the Bell Court was still established so the people's grievances could reach him.

entries.zh: 至太宗時，治渤海人一依漢法，余無改焉。
entries.en: Under Taizong, the Bohai were governed entirely by Han law; otherwise the system was unchanged.
entries.literal: By Taizong's time, the Bohai people were governed entirely by Han law; the rest remained unchanged.

entries.zh: 會同四年，皇族舍利郎君謀毒通事解裏等，已中者二人，命重杖之，及其妻流於厥拔離弭河，族造藥者。
entries.en: In the fourth year of Huitong, Imperial Clan Sheli Langjun plotted to poison Interpreter Jieli and others; two victims had already succumbed. He was heavily beaten, his wife exiled to the Juebalimi River, and the poison-makers' clan exterminated.
entries.literal: In the fourth year of Huitong, Imperial Clan Sheli Langjun plotted to poison the Interpreter Jieli and others; two had already been poisoned. He was ordered severely beaten, and his wife was exiled to the Juebalimi River; the clan of those who made the drug was exterminated.

entries.zh: 世宗天祿二年，天德、蕭翰、劉哥及其弟盆都等謀反，天德伏誅，杖翰，流劉哥，遣盆都使轄戛斯國。
entries.en: In Shizong's second year of Tianlu, Tiande, Xiao Han, Liuge, and Liuge's brother Pendu plotted rebellion. Tiande was executed, Han beaten, Liuge exiled, and Pendu dispatched as envoy to the Kirghiz.
entries.literal: In the second year of Tianlu under Shizong, Tiande, Xiao Han, Liuge, and Liuge's younger brother Pendu and others plotted rebellion. Tiande was executed, Han was beaten, Liuge was exiled, and Pendu was sent as envoy to the Kirghiz.

entries.zh: 夫四人之罪均而刑異，遼之世，同罪異論者蓋多。
entries.en: Though the four men's crimes were equal, their punishments differed — under the Liao, equal guilt often received unequal sentences.
entries.literal: These four men's crimes were equal yet their punishments differed — in the Liao age, cases of equal guilt but differing sentences were indeed numerous.

entries.zh: 穆宗應歷十二年，國舅帳郎君蕭延之奴海裏強陵拽剌禿裏年未及之女，以法無文，加之宮刑，仍付禿裏以為奴。
entries.en: In Muzong's twelfth year of Yingli, slave Haili of Imperial Uncle-in-Law Tent Langjun Xiao Yan raped Zhuala Tulii's underage daughter. With no statute covering the offense, he was castrated and given to Tulii as a slave.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Yingli under Muzong, the slave Haili of Imperial Uncle-in-Law Tent Langjun Xiao Yan forcibly violated the daughter of Zhuala Tulii, who had not yet reached the age of maturity. Because the law had no provision, he was subjected to castration and handed over to Tulii as a slave.

entries.zh: 因著為令。
entries.en: The case was then codified as precedent.
entries.literal: This was then written into law.

entries.zh: 十六年，諭有司：「自先朝行幸頓次，必高立標識以禁行者。
entries.en: In his sixteenth year, he instructed officials: "On imperial progresses since former times, tall markers were erected to bar unauthorized passage.
entries.literal: In the sixteenth year, he instructed the officials: "Since former dynasties made imperial progresses and encampments, markers were always erected high to forbid passage.

entries.zh: 比聞楚古輩，故低置其標深草中，利人誤入，因之取財。
entries.en: I have lately heard that Chugu and his ilk deliberately set markers low in deep grass, profiting when travelers strayed in by mistake and then extorting them.
entries.literal: Recently I have heard that Chugu and his ilk deliberately set their markers low in deep grass, profiting when people strayed in by mistake and then extorting them.

entries.zh: 自今有復然者，以死論。」
entries.en: Anyone who does so again shall be put to death."
entries.literal: From now on, whoever does so again shall be sentenced to death."

entries.zh: 然帝嗜酒及獵，不恤政事，五坊、掌獸、近侍、奉膳、掌酒人等以獐鹿、野豕、鶻雉之屬亡失傷斃，及私歸逃亡，在告逾期，召不時至，或以奏對少不如意，或以飲食細故，或因犯者遷怒無辜，輒加炮烙鐵梳之刑。
entries.en: Yet the emperor cared only for wine and the hunt, neglecting government. Keepers of the Five Wards, animal handlers, attendants, food servers, and wine stewards — for lost or injured game, unauthorized absence, overstayed leave, or tardiness when summoned; for answers at audience that displeased him, trifles at table, or rage vented on the innocent because of another's fault — he would at once apply branding and iron-comb torture.
entries.literal: Yet the emperor was addicted to wine and hunting and paid no heed to government. Men of the Five Wards, keepers of beasts, close attendants, food servers, wine stewards, and the like — for lost, injured, or dead roe deer, wild boar, falcon-hunted pheasants, and such; for unauthorized departure or flight; for overstaying leave; for failing to appear when summoned — or because answers at audience displeased him slightly, or because of trifles in food and drink, or because he vented anger on the innocent because of an offender — he would at once apply branding-iron torture and iron-comb punishment.

entries.zh: 甚者至於無算。
entries.en: In the worst cases the toll was beyond counting.
entries.literal: In extreme cases the count was beyond reckoning.

entries.zh: 或以手刃刺之，斬擊射燎，斷手足，爛肩股，折腰脛，劃口碎齒，棄屍於野。
entries.en: Sometimes he stabbed them himself, hacked, shot, and burned them, severed limbs, mangled shoulders and thighs, broke backs and shins, slashed mouths and shattered teeth, and left the corpses in the open country.
entries.literal: Sometimes he stabbed them with his own hand, hacked and shot and burned them, severed hands and feet, mangled shoulders and thighs, broke waists and shins, slashed mouths and shattered teeth, and cast the corpses into the wild.

entries.zh: 且命築封於其地，死者至百有餘人。
entries.en: He even ordered burial mounds raised on the spot; the dead numbered more than a hundred.
entries.literal: He even ordered mounds built and sealed on the spot; the dead reached more than a hundred.

entries.zh: 京師置百尺牢以處系囚。
entries.en: In the capital a hundred-foot prison was built to hold detainees.
entries.literal: In the capital a hundred-foot prison was set up to hold bound prisoners.

entries.zh: 蓋其即位未久，惑女巫肖古之言，取人膽合延年藥，故殺人頗眾。
entries.en: Not long after his accession he was swayed by the shamaness Xiaogu, who claimed human gall was needed for an elixir of longevity — hence the many killings.
entries.literal: This was because not long after he took the throne he was deluded by the words of the shamaness Xiaogu, who said human gallbladders were needed to compound an elixir of longevity — hence he killed many people.

entries.zh: 後悟其詐，以鳴鏑叢射、騎踐殺之。
entries.en: When he realized her fraud, he had her shot with whistling arrows and trampled under horses.
entries.literal: Later, realizing her deceit, he had her shot in volleys with whistling arrows and trampled to death under horses.

entries.zh: 及海裏之死，為長夜之飲，五坊、掌獸人等及左右給事誅戮者，相繼不絕。
entries.en: After Haili's execution he held all-night revels, and executions among the Five Wards, beast keepers, and personal attendants continued without pause.
entries.literal: After Haili's death he held all-night drinking; men of the Five Wards, beast keepers, and attendants on left and right who were executed followed one upon another without cease.

entries.zh: 雖嘗悔其因怒濫刑，諭大臣切諫，在廷畏懦，鮮能匡救，雖諫又不能聽。
entries.en: Though he once regretted his angry excesses and urged his ministers to remonstrate, the court was timid and few could save victims; even when they spoke up, he would not listen.
entries.literal: Although he once regretted his angry excess in punishment and instructed the great ministers to remonstrate earnestly, those at court were timid and few could rescue victims; even when they remonstrated, he would not listen.

entries.zh: 當其將殺壽哥、念古，殿前都點檢耶律夷臘葛諫曰：「壽哥等斃所掌雉，畏罪而亡，法不應死。」
entries.en: When he was about to execute Shouge and Nian'gu, Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige remonstrated: "Shouge and the others let their pheasants die and fled in fear of punishment — by law they do not deserve death."
entries.literal: When he was about to execute Shouge and Nian'gu, Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige remonstrated: "Shouge and the others let the pheasants in their charge die; fearing punishment they fled — by law they should not die."

entries.zh: 帝怒，斬壽哥等支解之。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage, beheaded Shouge and the others, and had them hacked apart.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged and beheaded Shouge and the others, hacking them apart.

entries.zh: 命有司盡取鹿人之在系者凡六十五人，斬所犯重者四十四人，余悉痛杖之。
entries.en: He ordered all sixty-five deer keepers in custody seized; forty-four of the worst offenders were beheaded, the rest severely beaten.
entries.literal: He ordered the officials to take all deer keepers in custody, sixty-five in all; forty-four of the gravest offenders were beheaded, and the rest were all severely beaten.

entries.zh: 中有欲置死者，賴王子必攝等諫得免。
entries.en: Some who would have been executed were spared through remonstrance by Princes Bishe and others.
entries.literal: Among them some were about to be put to death, but were spared thanks to remonstrance by Princes Bishe and others.

entries.zh: 已而怒頗德飼鹿不時，致傷而斃，遂殺之。
entries.en: Soon after, enraged that Pode had fed the deer irregularly, causing one to be injured and die, he had him killed.
entries.literal: Soon after, angered that Pode fed the deer irregularly so that one was injured and died, he killed him.

entries.zh: 季年，暴虐益甚，嘗謂太尉化葛曰：「朕醉中有處決不當者，醒當覆奏。」
entries.en: In his final years his cruelty worsened. He once told Grand Marshal Huage: "When I pass improper judgments while drunk, report them again when I am sober."
entries.literal: In his later years his cruelty grew worse. He once told Grand Marshal Huage: "When I am drunk and pass judgments improperly, report them again when I am sober."

entries.zh: 徒能言之，竟無悛意，故及於難。
entries.en: He could say the words but never meant to reform — and so met his end.
entries.literal: He could speak the words but had no intent to reform — hence he met with disaster.

entries.zh: 雖云虐止褻禦，上不及大臣，下不及百姓，然刑法之制，豈人主快情縱意之具邪！
entries.en: Though his cruelty is said to have touched only those close at hand, not reaching ministers above or commoners below, is the penal code an instrument for a ruler to indulge his whims?
entries.literal: Although it is said his cruelty was confined to those close at hand in the inner quarters, not reaching up to great ministers nor down to the common people, yet is the system of penal law an instrument for the ruler to indulge his feelings and give free rein to his will?

entries.zh: 景宗在潛，已鑒其失。
entries.en: Jingzong, while still heir apparent, had already taken note of these excesses.
entries.literal: Jingzong, while still heir apparent, had already taken these failures as a lesson.

entries.zh: 及即位，以宿衛失職，斬殿前都點檢耶律夷臘葛。
entries.en: On his accession, citing dereliction of the palace guard, he beheaded Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, because the palace guard had failed in duty, he beheaded Palace Front Chief Inspector Yelü Yilige.

entries.zh: 趙王喜隱自囚所擅去械鎖，求見自辯，語之曰：「枉直未分，焉有出獄自辯之理？」
entries.en: Prince of Zhao Xiyin removed his own shackles and sought an audience to plead his case. The emperor told him: "Guilt and innocence are not yet settled — what grounds have you to leave prison and plead?"
entries.literal: Prince of Zhao Xiyin, on his own authority, removed his fetters and locks from the prison and sought an audience to plead his case. The emperor told him: "Right and wrong are not yet distinguished — how can there be grounds for leaving prison to plead one's case?"

entries.zh: 命復縶之。
entries.en: He ordered him bound again.
entries.literal: He ordered him bound again.

entries.zh: 既而躬錄囚徒，盡召而釋之。
entries.en: Soon after he personally reviewed the prisoners and released them all.
entries.literal: Soon after he personally reviewed the prisoners and summoned them all to be released.

entries.zh: 保寧三年，以穆宗廢鐘院，窮民有冤者無所訴，故詔復之，仍命鑄鐘，紀詔其上，道所以廢置之意。
entries.en: In the third year of Baoning, because Muzong had abolished the Bell Court and the poor had nowhere to appeal their grievances, Jingzong restored it, ordered a new bell cast, and had the edict inscribed upon it explaining why it had been abolished and restored.
entries.literal: In the third year of Baoning, because Muzong had abolished the Bell Court and the poor with grievances had nowhere to appeal, an edict restored it; he also ordered a bell cast and the edict inscribed upon it, stating the reasons for abolition and restoration.

entries.zh: 吳王稍為奴所告，有司請鞫，帝曰：「朕知其誣，若按問，恐餘人效之。」
entries.en: Prince of Wu Shao was denounced by a slave; officials requested an investigation. The emperor said: "I know this is false — if we investigate, others may follow suit."
entries.literal: Prince of Wu Shao was denounced by a slave; the officials requested an investigation. The emperor said: "I know this is a false accusation — if we conduct an inquiry, I fear others will imitate it."

entries.zh: 命斬以徇。
entries.en: He ordered the slave beheaded as a warning.
entries.literal: He ordered the slave beheaded as a warning.

entries.zh: 五年，近侍實魯裏誤觸神纛，法應死，杖而釋之。
entries.en: In the fifth year, attendant Shiruli accidentally touched the sacred banner — a capital offense by law, but he was beaten and released.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, the close attendant Shiruli accidentally touched the sacred banner — by law he should have died, but he was beaten and released.

entries.zh: 庶幾寬猛相濟。
entries.en: Thus leniency and severity were balanced.
entries.literal: Thus leniency and severity were in some measure balanced.

entries.zh: 然緩於討賊，應歷逆黨至是始獲而誅焉，議者以此少之。
entries.en: Yet he was slow to pursue rebels; the Yingli traitors were only now captured and executed — critics held this against him.
entries.literal: Yet he was slow in pursuing rebels; the Yingli faction of traitors were only now captured and executed — critics for this reason thought less of him.

entries.zh: 聖宗沖年嗣位，睿智皇后稱制，留心聽斷，嘗勸帝宜寬法律。
entries.en: Shengzong succeeded as a child; the Wise Empress Dowager held regency, attended carefully to judgments, and urged him to lighten the laws.
entries.literal: Shengzong succeeded the throne in his youth; the Wise Empress Dowager held regency, attended carefully to hearings and judgments, and once urged the emperor to lighten the laws.

entries.zh: 帝壯，益習國事，銳意於治。
entries.en: When he came of age, he grew adept at statecraft and devoted himself to governance.
entries.literal: When the emperor came of age, he grew ever more practiced in state affairs and was keen on good governance.

entries.zh: 當時更定法令凡十數事，多合人心，其用刑又能詳慎。
entries.en: He revised more than a dozen statutes, most of which won popular approval, and applied punishment with care and deliberation.
entries.literal: At that time he revised statutes and ordinances in more than a dozen matters, most of which accorded with people's hearts; in applying punishment he was also careful and thorough.

entries.zh: 先是，契丹及漢人相毆致死，其法輕重不均，至是一等科之。
entries.en: Previously, when Khitan and Han beat each other to death, the penalties differed; now both were punished alike.
entries.literal: Previously, when Khitan and Han Chinese beat each other to death, the law's severity and leniency were unequal; now they were punished under a single standard.

entries.zh: 統和十二年，詔契丹人犯十惡，亦斷以《律》。
entries.en: In the twelfth year of Tonghe, an edict declared that Khitan who committed the Ten Abominations were also to be judged under the Tang code.
entries.literal: In the twelfth year of Tonghe, an edict declared that when Khitan committed the Ten Abominations, they too were to be judged by the Statutes.

entries.zh: 舊法，死囚屍市三日，至是一宿即聽收瘞。
entries.en: Under the old law, executed prisoners' corpses were displayed in the market for three days; now burial was permitted after a single night.
entries.literal: By the old law, the corpses of condemned prisoners were exposed in the market for three days; now after one night burial was permitted.

entries.zh: 二十四年，詔主非犯謀反大逆及流死罪者，其奴婢無得告首；
entries.en: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict declared that slaves might not denounce masters who had not committed treason, great sedition, or capital or exilable offenses;
entries.literal: In the twenty-fourth year, an edict declared that for masters who had not committed treason, great sedition, or crimes of exile or death, their male and female slaves were not permitted to denounce them;

entries.zh: 若奴婢犯罪至死，聽送有司，其主無得擅殺。
entries.en: if a slave merited death, the case was to be sent to the authorities; masters were forbidden to execute them privately.
entries.literal: if male or female slaves committed offenses warranting death, they were to be sent to the authorities; their masters were not permitted to kill them on their own authority.

entries.zh: 二十九年，以舊法，宰相、節度使世選之家子孫犯罪，徒杖如齊民，惟免黥面，詔自今但犯罪當黥，即準法同科。
entries.en: In the twenty-ninth year, under the old law, descendants of hereditary chancellor and military governor families who committed crimes received the same penal servitude and beating as commoners, though facial tattooing was waived; an edict now required that whenever tattooing was warranted, they be punished like everyone else.
entries.literal: In the twenty-ninth year, under the old law, when descendants of hereditary-selection households of chancellors and military governors committed offenses, penal servitude and beating were like those for common people, only tattooing the face was exempted; an edict declared that from now on, whenever an offense warranted tattooing, they were to be punished by the same standard as the law.

entries.zh: 開泰八年，以竊盜贓滿十貫，為首者處死，其法太重，故增至二十五貫，其首處死，從者決流。
entries.en: In the eighth year of Kaitai, theft of ten strings of cash had meant death for the ringleader — the penalty was judged too harsh, so the threshold was raised to twenty-five strings; the ringleader still faced death, accomplices exile.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Kaitai, because stolen goods in theft reached ten strings of cash, the ringleader was put to death — the law was too severe, so it was increased to twenty-five strings; the ringleader was put to death, accomplices were sentenced to exile.

entries.zh: 嘗敕諸處刑獄有冤，不能申雪者，聽詣御史臺陳訴，委官覆問。
entries.en: He once ordered that prisoners who could not clear wrongful convictions might appeal to the Censorate, with officials commissioned to reinvestigate.
entries.literal: He once ordered that wherever prisons held the wrongfully convicted who could not clear themselves, they were permitted to appeal to the Censorate, and officials were commissioned to re-examine the cases.

entries.zh: 往時大理寺獄訟，凡關覆奏者，以翰林學士、給事中、政事舍人詳決，至是始置少卿及正主之。
entries.en: Formerly, Court of Judicial Review cases requiring imperial review were decided by Hanlin academicians, supervising secretaries, and administrative assistants; only now were a vice director and presiding officer appointed.
entries.literal: Formerly in lawsuits at the Court of Judicial Review, all matters requiring review and memorial to the throne were decided in detail by Hanlin Academicians, Supervising Secretaries, and Administrative Assistants; only now were a Vice Director and a chief presiding officer first appointed.

entries.zh: 猶慮其未盡，而親為錄囚。
entries.en: Still unsatisfied, he personally reviewed the prisoners.
entries.literal: Still fearing this was not enough, he personally reviewed the prisoners.

entries.zh: 數遣使詣諸道審決冤滯，如邢抱樸之屬，所至，人自以為無冤。
entries.en: He repeatedly dispatched envoys to the circuits to clear stale wrongful cases; men like Xing Baopu left people feeling that nowhere did injustice remain.
entries.literal: He repeatedly sent envoys to the various circuits to examine and decide stale wrongful cases; men like Xing Baopu, wherever they went, made people feel they had no grievance left unredressed.

entries.zh: 五院部民有自壞鎧甲者，其長佛奴杖殺之，上怒其用法太峻，詔奪官。
entries.en: When a man of the Five Wards damaged his own armor, his chief Fonu beat him to death; the emperor, angered at such harsh application of the law, stripped Fonu of his post.
entries.literal: Among the people of the Five Wards, one who had damaged his own armor on his own initiative was beaten to death by his chief Fonu; the emperor, angered that the law had been applied too harshly, ordered Fonu's dismissal from office.

entries.zh: 吏以故不敢酷。
entries.en: Officials thereafter dared not be cruel.
entries.literal: Officials for this reason did not dare to be cruel.

entries.zh: 撻剌幹乃方十因醉言宮掖事，法當死，特貰其罪。
entries.en: Tatala Gannai Fangshi spoke of inner-palace matters while drunk — a capital offense by law, but he was specially pardoned.
entries.literal: Tatala Gannai Fangshi, because while drunk he spoke of inner-palace affairs, should by law have died, but was specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 五院部民偶遺火。
entries.en: A man of the Five Wards accidentally started a fire.
entries.literal: A man of the Five Wards accidentally started a fire.

entries.zh: 延及木葉山兆域，亦當死，杖而釋之，因著為法。
entries.en: The fire spread to the sacred precinct of Mount Muye — also a capital offense, but he was beaten and released, and the case was codified as precedent.
entries.literal: It spread to the sacred precinct of Mount Muye; this too should have meant death, but he was beaten and released, and this was then written into law.

entries.zh: 至於敵八哥始竊薊州王令謙家財，及覺，以刃刺令謙，幸不死。
entries.en: Dibage first stole the property of Wang Lingqian of Jizhou; when discovered, he stabbed Lingqian with a blade, but fortunately Lingqian survived.
entries.literal: As for Dibage, he first stole the property of Wang Lingqian of Jizhou; when discovered, he stabbed Lingqian with a blade — fortunately he did not die.

entries.zh: 有司擬以盜論，止加杖罪。
entries.en: Officials proposed treating it as theft, but the emperor imposed only a beating.
entries.literal: The officials proposed judging it as theft, but the emperor only added a beating offense.

entries.zh: 又那母古犯竊盜者十有三次，皆以情不可恕，論棄市。
entries.en: Namugu had committed theft thirteen times; each case was deemed unforgivable, and he was sentenced to public execution.
entries.literal: Also Namugu had committed theft thirteen times; in every case the circumstances were unforgivable, and he was sentenced to execution in the market.

entries.zh: 因詔自今三犯竊盜者，黥額、徒三年；
entries.en: An edict therefore declared that a third theft offense would bring forehead tattooing and three years' penal servitude;
entries.literal: Hence an edict declared that from now on, for a third theft offense, the forehead was tattooed and penal servitude of three years imposed;

entries.zh: 四則黥面、徒五年；
entries.en: a fourth offense, facial tattooing and five years' penal servitude;
entries.literal: a fourth offense brought tattooing the face and five years' penal servitude;

entries.zh: 至於五則處死。
entries.en: a fifth, death.
entries.literal: upon a fifth, execution.

entries.zh: 若是者，重輕適宜，足以示訓。
entries.en: Such gradations were proportionate and sufficient to serve as a warning.
entries.literal: Such gradations of severity and leniency were fitting and sufficient to serve as instruction.

entries.zh: 近侍劉哥、烏古斯嘗從齊王妻而逃，以赦，後會千齡節出首，乃詔諸近侍、護衛集視而腰斬之。
entries.en: Attendants Liuge and Wugusi had once fled with the Prince of Qi's wife; though pardoned, they confessed at the Thousand-Age Festival; the emperor then had all attendants and guards assembled to witness their execution by cutting in two at the waist.
entries.literal: Close attendants Liuge and Wugusi had once fled with the wife of the Prince of Qi; they were pardoned, but later at the Thousand-Age Festival they came forward to confess; he then ordered all close attendants and guards assembled to witness their execution by cutting at the waist.

entries.zh: 於是國無幸民，綱紀修舉，吏多奉職，人重犯法。
entries.en: Thus no one counted on luck to escape justice; discipline was restored, officials performed their duties, and the people feared breaking the law.
entries.literal: Thus the state had no men who counted on luck; discipline was restored, officials mostly performed their duties, and people feared breaking the law.

entries.zh: 故統和中，南京及易、平二州以獄空聞。
entries.en: During Tonghe, the Southern Capital and the prefectures of Yi and Ping were famed for empty prisons.
entries.literal: Therefore during Tonghe, the Southern Capital and the two prefectures of Yi and Ping were famed for empty prisons.

entries.zh: 至開泰五年，諸道皆獄空，有刑措之風焉。
entries.en: By the fifth year of Kaitai, every circuit reported empty prisons — a sign that punishments had fallen largely into disuse.
entries.literal: By the fifth year of Kaitai, every circuit had empty prisons — there was a wind of punishments set aside.

entries.zh: 故事，樞密使非國家重務，未嘗親決，凡獄訟惟夷離畢主之。
entries.en: By precedent, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs never personally decided matters that were not major affairs of state; all lawsuits were handled by the yilibi alone.
entries.literal: By precedent, the Commissioner of the Bureau of Military Affairs never personally decided affairs that were not weighty state matters; all lawsuits were presided over only by the yilibi.

entries.zh: 及蕭合卓、蕭樸相繼為樞密使，專尚吏才，始自聽訟。
entries.en: When Xiao Hezhuo and Xiao Pu successively served as commissioners, prizing administrative talent, they began hearing lawsuits themselves.
entries.literal: When Xiao Hezhuo and Xiao Pu succeeded one another as Commissioners of the Bureau of Military Affairs, valuing administrative talent exclusively, they began to hear lawsuits themselves.

entries.zh: 時人轉相效習，以狡智相高，風俗自此衰矣。
entries.en: Others followed suit, competing in cunning, and public morals declined from that point.
entries.literal: People of the time imitated one another in turn, competing in cunning intelligence, and custom declined from this.

entries.zh: 故太平六年下詔曰：「朕以國家有契丹、漢人，故以南、北二院分治之，蓋欲去貪枉，除煩擾也；
entries.en: Therefore in the sixth year of Taiping an edict declared: "Our state has Khitan and Han subjects, whom we govern through separate Southern and Northern Courts, intending to remove corruption and eliminate vexation;
entries.literal: Therefore in the sixth year of Taiping an edict was issued: "We, considering that the state has Khitan and Han Chinese, therefore govern them separately through the Southern and Northern Courts, intending to remove corruption and injustice and eliminate vexatious trouble;

entries.zh: 若貴賤異法，則怨必生。
entries.en: if noble and humble are judged by different laws, resentment is sure to follow.
entries.literal: if noble and humble are judged by different laws, resentment is sure to arise.

entries.zh: 夫小民犯罪，必不能動有司以達於朝，惟內族、外戚多恃恩行賄，以圖茍免，如是則法廢矣。
entries.en: Commoners who commit crimes cannot move the authorities to reach the throne; only imperial kin and affines rely on favor to bribe their way free — and thus the law falls into disuse.
entries.literal: When common people commit offenses, they surely cannot move the authorities to reach the court; only inner-clan kin and outer-clan affines mostly rely on favor to offer bribes, seeking careless exemption — if so, the law is abandoned.

entries.zh: 自今貴戚以事被告，不以事之大小，並令所在官司按問，具申北、南院覆問得實以聞；
entries.en: Henceforth, when nobles and affines are accused, regardless of the gravity of the offense, local offices must investigate and report to the Northern and Southern Courts for review before memorializing the throne;
entries.literal: From now on, when nobles and affines are accused in any matter, regardless of its size, all local offices are ordered to investigate, report in full to the Northern and Southern Courts for re-examination, and memorialize the verified facts;

entries.zh: 其不按輒申，及受請托為奏言者，以本犯人罪罪之。」
entries.en: anyone who investigates improperly, memorializes rashly, or accepts bribes to speak on a defendant's behalf shall be punished with the same offense as the accused."
entries.literal: whoever investigates without due process and memorializes rashly, or accepts entreaties to speak on another's behalf, is to be punished with the same offense as the original criminal."

entries.zh: 七年，詔中外大臣曰：「《制》條中有遺闕及輕重失中者，其條上之，議增改焉。」
entries.en: In the seventh year, an edict to all ministers declared: "Where provisions in the Regulations are missing or penalties are imbalanced, submit the articles for discussion of additions and revisions."
entries.literal: In the seventh year, an edict to ministers inside and outside the court said: "Where provisions in the Regulations have omissions or where severity and leniency are imbalanced, memorialize the articles for discussion of additions and revisions."

entries.zh: 刑法志上
entries.en: Punishment and Law, Part One
entries.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law, Part One

entries.zh: 重熙元年，詔職事官公罪聽贖，私罪各從本法；
entries.en: In the first year of Chongxi, an edict allowed functional officials to redeem public offenses, while private offenses were punished under the usual statutes;
entries.literal: In the first year of Chongxi, an edict stated that functional officials' public offenses might be redeemed, while private offenses were each punished according to the applicable statute;

entries.zh: 子弟及家人受賕，不知情者，止坐犯人。
entries.en: when sons, younger brothers, or household members took bribes, those who did not know were not punished—only the guilty party was.
entries.literal: when sons, younger brothers, and household members accepted bribes, those who did not know were punished only as to the offender himself.

entries.zh: 先是，南京三司銷錢作器皿三斤，持錢出南京十貫，及盜遺火家物五貫者處死；
entries.en: Previously, melting three jin of coin into vessels at the Nanjing Three Departments, carrying ten strings of cash out of Nanjing, or stealing—or through fire, destroying—household goods worth five strings were capital crimes;
entries.literal: Previously, at the Nanjing Three Departments, melting coin to make vessels of three jin, carrying ten strings of cash out of Nanjing, and stealing or leaving fire-damaged household goods worth five strings were punished by death;

entries.zh: 至是，銅逾三斤，持錢及所盜物二十貫以上處死。
entries.en: now death applied only when copper exceeded three jin, or when cash carried or goods stolen amounted to twenty strings or more.
entries.literal: at this time, copper exceeding three jin, and carrying cash or stolen goods of twenty strings or more, were punished by death.

entries.zh: 二年，有司奏：「元年詔曰，犯重罪徒終身者，加以捶楚，而又黥面。
entries.en: In the second year, the responsible offices reported: "The first-year edict provides that offenders guilty of serious crimes and sentenced to lifetime penal servitude are beaten and also tattooed on the face.
entries.literal: In the second year, the responsible offices memorialized: "The edict of the first year states that those guilty of serious crimes and sentenced to lifetime penal servitude are to receive beating in addition, and also facial tattooing.

entries.zh: 是犯一罪而具三刑，宜免黥。
entries.en: One offense thus carries three punishments; facial tattooing should be waived.
entries.literal: This is one offense bearing three punishments; facial tattooing should be waived.

entries.zh: 其職事官及宰相、節度使世選之家子孫，犯奸罪至徒者，未審黥否？」
entries.en: For functional officials and descendants of hereditary chancellor and military commissioner families, when adultery is punished by penal servitude, should facial tattooing still apply?"
entries.literal: As for functional officials and the descendants of hereditary-selection families of chancellors and military commissioners, when guilty of adultery punishable by penal servitude, it is not yet clear whether they are to be tattooed?"

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「犯罪而悔過自新者，亦有可用之人，一黥其面，終身為辱，朕甚憫焉。」
entries.en: The emperor replied: "Some who commit crimes and truly repent may still be useful; a single mark on the face is a lifelong disgrace, and We pity them deeply."
entries.literal: The emperor instructed: "Those who offend yet repent and renew themselves may still be of use; once the face is tattooed, it is a lifelong disgrace — We are deeply moved to pity."

entries.zh: 後犯終身徒者，止刺頸。
entries.en: Thereafter, lifetime penal servitude was marked by tattoo on the neck alone.
entries.literal: Thereafter, those guilty of lifetime penal servitude were tattooed only on the neck.

entries.zh: 奴婢犯逃，若盜其主物，主無得擅黥其面，刺臂及頸者聽。
entries.en: When slaves fled or stole their master's property, masters might not tattoo their faces on their own authority; tattooing the arm or neck was permitted.
entries.literal: When male and female slaves committed flight or theft of their master's goods, the master might not on his own authority tattoo their faces; tattooing the arm or neck was permitted.

entries.zh: 犯竊盜者，初刺右臂，再刺左，三刺頸之後，四刺左，至於五則處死。
entries.en: Petty thieves were first marked on the right arm, then the left, then the neck, then the left again; on the fifth offense they were executed.
entries.literal: Petty thieves were first tattooed on the right arm, a second time on the left, after a third on the neck a fourth on the left; upon the fifth offense they were executed.

entries.zh: 五年，《新定條制》成，詔有司凡朝日執之，仍頒行諸道。
entries.en: In the fifth year the "Newly Fixed Regulations" were completed; officials were ordered to apply them at every court session and to promulgate them throughout all circuits.
entries.literal: In the fifth year, the "Newly Fixed Regulations" were completed; the emperor ordered the responsible offices to apply them on every court day and also to promulgate them through all circuits.

entries.zh: 蓋纂修太祖以來法令，參以古制。
entries.en: They compiled statutes from Taizu onward and drew on ancient models.
entries.literal: They compiled and revised statutes from Taizu onward, with reference to ancient institutions.

entries.zh: 其刑有死、流、杖及三等之徒而五，凡五百四十七條。
entries.en: The code defined death, exile, beating, and five grades of penal servitude in three terms—five hundred forty-seven articles in all.
entries.literal: Its punishments were death, exile, beating, and five grades of penal servitude in three terms, five hundred forty-seven articles in all.

entries.zh: 時有群牧人竊易官印以馬與人者，法當死，帝曰：「一馬殺二人，不亦甚乎？」
entries.en: Some herd-masters had secretly swapped official seals to trade government horses; the statute called for death. The emperor said, "To execute two men over one horse—is that not excessive?"
entries.literal: At the time there were herd-masters who secretly exchanged official seals to trade horses to others; by law they should die. The emperor said: "To kill two men for one horse — is that not excessive?"

entries.zh: 減死論。
entries.en: The sentence was commuted from death.
entries.literal: Their sentence was reduced from death.

entries.zh: 又有兄弟犯強盜當死，以弟從兄，且俱無子，特原其弟。
entries.en: Two brothers guilty of armed robbery faced execution; because the younger had followed the elder and neither had sons, the younger was specially spared.
entries.literal: There were also brothers guilty of armed robbery who should die; because the younger followed the elder and both were without sons, the younger was specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 至於枉法受賕，詐敕走遞，偽學御書，盜外國貢物者，例皆免死。
entries.en: Those who perverted the law for bribes, forged edicts to flee by relay post, counterfeited imperial calligraphy, or stole foreign tribute were routinely spared execution.
entries.literal: As for perverting the law to accept bribes, forging edicts to flee by relay post, counterfeiting imperial calligraphy, and stealing tribute goods from foreign states — by precedent all were spared death.

entries.zh: 郡王貼不家奴彌裏吉告其主言涉怨望，鞫之無驗，當反坐，以欽哀皇后裏言，竟不加罪，亦不斷付其主，僅籍沒焉。
entries.en: Miliji, a slave of Prince Junwang Tiebu, accused his master of disloyal speech; the charge could not be proved and the accuser should have been punished in turn, but at Qin'ai's private word he escaped punishment, was not returned to his master, and only had his property confiscated.
entries.literal: The household slave Miliji of Prince Junwang Tiebu reported his master for words suggesting resentment; interrogation found no proof, and by law the accuser should be punished in turn; because of Empress Dowager Qin'ai's private word, he was in the end not punished, nor adjudged and returned to his master — only his property was registered for confiscation.

entries.zh: 寧遠軍節度使蕭白強掠烏古敵烈都詳穩敵魯之女為妻，亦以後言免死，杖而奪其官。
entries.en: Xiao Bai, commissioner of Ningyuan Army, forcibly took Dile's daughter as his wife; he too was spared death on the empress's word, beaten, and dismissed from office.
entries.literal: Xiao Bai, military commissioner of Ningyuan Army, forcibly seized the daughter of Dile, detailed commander of the Uighur and Tatar tribes, as wife; he too was spared death on the empress's word, beaten, and stripped of office.

entries.zh: 梅裏狗丹使酒殺人而逃，會永壽節出首，特赦其罪。
entries.en: Meilidoudan killed a man in a drunken rage and fled; he surrendered on the Eternal Longevity festival and received a special pardon.
entries.literal: Meilidoudan, drunk, killed a man and fled; it happened to be the Eternal Longevity festival, and he surrendered himself; his crime was specially pardoned.

entries.zh: 皇妹秦國公主生日，帝幸其第，伶人張隋，本宋所遣汋者，大臣覺之以聞。
entries.en: On his sister the Princess of Qin's birthday the emperor visited her residence; the actor Zhang Sui, originally a Song spy, was detected and reported by a senior minister.
entries.literal: On the birthday of the emperor's sister, Princess of Qin, the emperor visited her residence; the actor Zhang Sui, originally a spy sent by Song, was detected by a great minister who reported it.

entries.zh: 召詰，款伏，乃遽釋之。
entries.en: Summoned and questioned, he confessed fully—and was immediately released.
entries.literal: Summoned and questioned, he confessed fully, yet was forthwith released.

entries.zh: 後詔諸職官私取官物者，以正盜論。
entries.en: Later an edict ruled that officials who privately took government property were guilty of full theft.
entries.literal: Later an edict stated that functional officials who privately took government goods were to be judged as full theft.

entries.zh: 諸帳郎君等於禁地射鹿，決杖三百，不徵償；
entries.en: Account gentlemen who shot deer in the imperial preserve were sentenced to three hundred strokes, without compensation;
entries.literal: Various account gentlemen who shot deer in forbidden ground were sentenced to three hundred strokes, without compensation levied;

entries.zh: 小將軍決二百已下；
entries.en: junior generals received two hundred strokes or fewer;
entries.literal: junior generals received two hundred strokes or less;

entries.zh: 至百姓犯者決三百。
entries.en: commoners who offended received three hundred strokes.
entries.literal: commoners who offended received three hundred strokes.

entries.zh: 聖宗之風替矣。
entries.en: The standards of Shengzong's reign were gone.
entries.literal: The style of Emperor Shengzong had declined.

entries.zh: 道宗清寧元年，詔諸宮都部署曰：「凡有機密事，即可面奏；
entries.en: In the first year of Qingning, Daozong ordered the palace chief deployments: "Report confidential matters to Us in person;
entries.literal: In the first year of Qingning, Emperor Daozong issued an edict the palace chief deployments: "Whenever there are confidential matters, you may memorialize in person;

entries.zh: 餘所訴事，以法施行，有投誹訕之書，其受及讀者皆棄市。」
entries.en: all other suits shall follow the law. Anyone who receives or reads a slanderous writing shall be executed in the marketplace."
entries.literal: all other suits are to be carried out according to law. Whoever submits writings of slander — both the receiver and the reader are to be executed in the marketplace."

entries.zh: 二年，命諸郡長吏如諸部例，與僚屬同決罪囚，無致枉死獄中。
entries.en: In the second year he ordered prefectural administrators, following tribal precedent, to decide criminal cases jointly with their staffs so that no one would die wrongfully in prison.
entries.literal: In the second year, he ordered prefectural chief administrators, following the tribal precedent, to decide criminal cases together with their subordinates, so that none should die wrongfully in prison.

entries.zh: 下詔曰：「先時諸路死刑皆待決於朝，故獄訟留滯；
entries.en: An edict declared: "Formerly all capital sentences in the circuits awaited court decision, and litigation piled up;
entries.literal: An edict stated: "Formerly capital sentences in all circuits awaited decision at court, so litigation was delayed;

entries.zh: 自今凡強盜得實者，聽即決之。」
entries.en: from now on, wherever armed robbery is proved, the local office may execute judgment at once."
entries.literal: from now on, wherever armed robbery is proved, let judgment be immediate."

entries.zh: 四年，復詔左夷離畢曰：「比詔外路死刑，聽所在官司即決。
entries.en: In the fourth year he again instructed the Left Yilipin: "The recent edict allowed local offices on the outer circuits to decide capital cases on the spot.
entries.literal: In the fourth year, he again issued an edict the Left Yilipin: "The recent edict allowed capital punishment on outer circuits to be decided on the spot by the local office.

entries.zh: 然恐未能悉其情，或有枉者。
entries.en: Yet We fear the facts may not be fully known and innocents wronged.
entries.literal: Yet We fear the circumstances may not be fully known, and some may be wronged.

entries.zh: 自今雖已款伏，仍令附近官司覆問，無冤然後決之，有冤者即具以聞。」
entries.en: Henceforth, even after full confession, nearby offices must re-examine the case; only when no injustice is found may sentence be carried out; any sign of wrongful conviction must be reported."
entries.literal: From now on, even when confession is complete, nearby offices are still to re-examine; only when there is no injustice shall sentence be carried out; where injustice exists, report in full."

entries.zh: 咸雍元年，詔獄囚無家者，給以糧。
entries.en: In the first year of Xianyong, prisoners without families were supplied with grain.
entries.literal: In the first year of Xianyong, an edict provided grain to prisoners without families.

entries.zh: 六年，帝以契丹、漢人風俗不同，國法不可異施，於是命惕隱蘇、樞密使乙辛等更定《條制》。
entries.en: In the sixth year the emperor held that Khitan and Han customs differed and national law could not be applied in two ways; he ordered Tiyin Su, Privy Councilor Yixin, and others to revise the "Regulations."
entries.literal: In the sixth year, the emperor held that Khitan and Han customs differed and state law could not be applied differently; he therefore ordered Tiyin Su, Privy Councilor Yixin, and others to revise the "Regulations."

entries.zh: 凡合於《律令》者，具載之；
entries.en: Whatever accorded with the "Statutes and Ordinances" was fully recorded;
entries.literal: Whatever accorded with the "Statutes and Ordinances" was fully recorded;

entries.zh: 其不合者，別存之。
entries.en: what did not accord was kept in a separate register.
entries.literal: what did not accord was kept separately.

entries.zh: 時校定官即重熙舊制，更竊盜贓二十五貫處死一條，增至五十貫處死；
entries.en: The revisers, working from the Chongxi code, raised the death penalty for theft from twenty-five to fifty strings of booty;
entries.literal: The revising officers, taking the Chongxi old system, changed the article on theft punishing twenty-five strings of booty with death to fifty strings for death;

entries.zh: 又刪其重復者二條，為五百四十五條；
entries.en: deleted two duplicate articles, leaving five hundred forty-five;
entries.literal: deleted two duplicate articles, making five hundred forty-five;

entries.zh: 取《律》一百七十三條，又創增七十一條，凡七百八十九條，增重編者至千餘條。
entries.en: they took one hundred seventy-three articles from the "Statutes" and added seventy-one new ones—seven hundred eighty-nine in all; with further additions and revisions the total exceeded a thousand.
entries.literal: took one hundred seventy-three articles from the "Statutes," and newly added seventy-one, seven hundred eighty-nine in all; with additions and heavy revisions the total reached more than a thousand articles.

entries.zh: 皆分類列。
entries.en: All were arranged by category.
entries.literal: All were arranged by category.

entries.zh: 以大康間所定，復以《律》及《條例》參校，續增三十六條。
entries.en: Building on the Dakang code, they collated it again against the "Statutes" and "Regulations" and added thirty-six articles.
entries.literal: Based on what had been fixed in the Dakang period, they again collated against the "Statutes" and "Regulations," adding thirty-six articles.

entries.zh: 其後因事續校，至大安三年止，又增六十七條。
entries.en: Revision continued case by case until the third year of Da'an, when sixty-seven more articles were added.
entries.literal: Thereafter they continued revision as cases arose; by the third year of Da'an they stopped, having added sixty-seven more articles.

entries.zh: 條約既繁，典者不能遍習，愚民莫知所避，犯法者眾，吏得因緣為奸。
entries.en: As the code grew bloated, officials could not master it, common people did not know what to avoid, offenses multiplied, and clerks exploited the confusion for private gain.
entries.literal: Once the regulations grew numerous, custodians of the law could not master them all; simple people did not know what to avoid; offenders were many, and clerks used the occasion to practice deceit.

entries.zh: 故五年詔曰：「法者所以示民信而致國治，簡易如天地，不忒如四時，使民可避而不可犯。
entries.en: Therefore in the fifth year an edict declared: "Law exists to win the people's trust and bring order to the state—it should be as plain as Heaven and Earth, as steady as the four seasons, so that people may know what to avoid and dare not transgress.
entries.literal: Therefore in the fifth year an edict stated: "Law is that by which the people's trust is shown and the state brought to order — simple as Heaven and Earth, unerring as the four seasons, so that the people may avoid offense yet not dare to violate it.

entries.zh: 此命有司纂修刑法，然不能明體朕意，多作條目，以罔民於罪，朕甚不取。
entries.en: We ordered the offices to revise the penal code, yet they failed to grasp Our intent and multiplied articles to trap the people in crime—We will not accept this.
entries.literal: We ordered the responsible offices to compile and revise penal law, yet they could not make clear Our intent, and made many articles to entangle the people in guilt — We greatly disapprove.

entries.zh: 自今復用舊法，余悉除之。」
entries.en: Henceforth the old law alone shall apply; all additions are abolished."
entries.literal: From now on the old law is again to be used; all the rest is abolished."

entries.zh: 然自大康元年，北院樞密使耶律乙辛等用事，宮婢單登等誣告宣懿皇后，乙辛以聞，即詔乙辛劾狀，因實其事。
entries.en: Yet from the first year of Dakang, Northern Privy Councilor Yelü Yixin held power; palace maid Shan Deng falsely accused Empress Xuanyi; Yixin reported it, and the emperor ordered him to investigate—thereby making the charge stick.
entries.literal: Yet from the first year of Dakang, Northern Privy Councilor Yelü Yixin and his faction held power; palace maid Shan Deng and others falsely accused Empress Xuanyi; Yixin reported it, and an edict at once ordered Yixin to investigate the charge — thereby making the accusation fact.

entries.zh: 上怒，族伶人趙惟一，斬高長命，皆籍其家，仍賜皇后自盡。
entries.en: The emperor flew into a rage: the actor Zhao Weiyi and his entire clan were destroyed, Gao Changming was beheaded, both families' property was confiscated, and the empress was ordered to take her own life.
entries.literal: The emperor was enraged; the actor Zhao Weiyi was punished with extinction of kin; Gao Changming was beheaded; both households were registered for confiscation; the empress was still ordered to take her own life.

entries.zh: 三年，乙辛又與其黨謀構昭懷太子，陰令右護衛太保耶律查剌，告知樞密院事蕭速撒等八人謀立皇太子。
entries.en: In the third year Yixin and his faction framed Crown Prince Zhaohuai, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to accuse Privy Councilor Xiao Susa and eight others of plotting to enthrone the crown prince.
entries.literal: In the third year, Yixin again plotted with his faction to frame Crown Prince Zhaohuai, secretly ordering Right Guard Commissioner Yelü Chala to report that Privy Councilor Xiao Susa and eight others plotted to enthrone the crown prince.

entries.zh: 詔按無狀，出速撒、達不也外補，流護衛撒撥等六人。
entries.en: Investigation found no substance; Susa and Dabuye were posted elsewhere; six guards including Sapo were exiled.
entries.literal: An edict investigated and found no substance; Susa and Dabuye were sent out for external appointment; six guards including Sapo were exiled.

entries.zh: 詔告首謀逆者，重加官賞；
entries.en: An edict promised heavy promotion and reward to whoever reported the chief plotters of treason;
entries.literal: An edict stated that whoever reported the chief plotters of rebellion would receive heavy promotion and reward;

entries.zh: 否則悉行誅戮。
entries.en: otherwise all involved would be executed.
entries.literal: otherwise all would be put to death.

entries.zh: 乙辛教牌印郎君蕭訛都斡自首「臣嘗預速撒等謀」，因籍姓名以告。
entries.en: Yixin coached Seal Office Gentleman Xiao Eduo to confess: "I once took part in Susa's plot," and Eduo denounced others by name.
