entries.literal: Yixin coached Seal Office Gentleman Xiao Eduo to surrender himself, saying "Your servant once took part in Susa's plot," and thereby registered names to inform against them.

entries.zh: 帝信之，以乙辛等鞫按，至杖皇太子，囚之宮中別室，殺撻不也、撒剌等三十五人，又殺速撒等諸子；
entries.en: The emperor believed them; Yixin conducted the inquiry, had the crown prince beaten and imprisoned in a separate palace chamber, executed Tabuye, Sala, and thirty-five others, and killed Susa's sons as well;
entries.literal: The emperor believed it; Yixin and others conducted the inquiry, going so far as to beat the crown prince and imprison him in a separate chamber within the palace; Tabuye, Sala, and thirty-five others were killed, and Susa's sons were also killed;

entries.zh: 其幼稚及婦女、奴婢、家產，皆籍沒之，或分賜群臣。
entries.en: their children, wives, slaves, and property were confiscated or distributed among the ministers.
entries.literal: their infants, women, male and female slaves, and household property were all registered for confiscation, or distributed as gifts among the ministers.

entries.zh: 燕哥等詐為太子爰書以聞，上大怒，廢太子，徙上京，乙辛尋遣人弒於囚所。
entries.en: Yange and others forged the crown prince's confession; the emperor deposed him and sent him to Shangjing, where Yixin soon had him murdered in prison.
entries.literal: Yange and others forged the crown prince's written pledge and reported it; the emperor was greatly enraged, deposed the crown prince, and transferred him to Shangjing; Yixin soon sent men to assassinate him in prison.

entries.zh: 帝猶不寤，朝廷上下，無復紀律。
entries.en: The emperor still did not see the truth, and discipline vanished from the court.
entries.literal: The emperor still did not awaken; above and below the court, discipline was no more.

entries.zh: 天祚乾統元年，凡大康三年預乙辛所害者悉復官爵，籍沒者出之，流放者還鄉里。
entries.en: In Tianzuo's first year of Qiantong, all whom Yixin had harmed in the third year of Dakang had rank and titles restored, confiscated property returned, and exiles sent home.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qiantong under Tianzuo, all who in the third year of Dakang had suffered at Yixin's hands had rank and titles restored; those whose property had been registered were released; those exiled returned to their home districts.

entries.zh: 至二年，始廢乙辛等墓，剖棺戮屍，誅其子孫，餘黨子孫減死，徙邊，其家屬奴婢皆分賜被害之家。
entries.en: In the second year Yixin's tomb was destroyed, his coffin opened and corpse flogged, his descendants executed; other faction members' descendants had sentences reduced and were exiled, their families and slaves given to the victims' kin.
entries.literal: By the second year, Yixin's tomb and others were at last destroyed, coffins opened and corpses flogged, his descendants executed; descendants of the remaining faction had death reduced and were moved to the border; their household members and slaves were all distributed as gifts to the families of the victims.

entries.zh: 如耶律撻不也、蕭達魯古等，黨人之尤凶狡者，皆以賂免。
entries.en: Men such as Yelü Tabuye and Xiao Dalugu, the faction's most vicious members, all bought their way free.
entries.literal: Such men as Yelü Tabuye and Xiao Dalugu — the most vicious and cunning of the faction — all escaped through bribery.

entries.zh: 至於覆軍失城者，第免官而已。
entries.en: Generals who lost armies or cities were merely dismissed.
entries.literal: As for those who lost armies or cities, they were merely dismissed from office.

entries.zh: 行軍將軍耶律涅裏三人有禁地射鹿之罪，皆棄市。
entries.en: Campaign General Yelü Nieli and two others who shot deer in the imperial preserve were all executed in the marketplace.
entries.literal: Campaign General Yelü Nieli and two others were guilty of shooting deer in forbidden ground; all three were executed in the marketplace.

entries.zh: 其職官諸局人有過者，鐫降決斷之外，悉從軍。
entries.en: Officials and bureau staff who offended, beyond demotion and formal judgment, were all sent to the army.
entries.literal: Functional officials and bureau personnel who offended, beyond inscription, demotion, and judgment, were all sent to the army.

entries.zh: 賞罰無章，怨讟日起；
entries.en: Rewards and punishments had no rhyme or reason; resentment mounted daily;
entries.literal: Rewards and punishments lacked rule; resentment and complaint arose daily;

entries.zh: 劇盜相挺，叛亡接踵。
entries.en: banditry spread and defections followed one after another.
entries.literal: fierce bandits rose one after another, and defection and flight followed in succession.

entries.zh: 天祚大恐，益務繩以嚴酷，由是投崖、炮擲、釘割、臠殺之刑復興焉。
entries.en: Tianzuo, terrified, tightened the law with ever greater cruelty; casting from cliffs, cannon-throwing, nailing, cutting, and dismemberment were revived.
entries.literal: Tianzuo was greatly afraid and strove all the more to bind men with severity; thereby casting from cliffs, cannon-throwing, nailing and cutting, and dismemberment killings revived.

entries.zh: 或有分戶五京，甚者至取其心以獻祖廟。
entries.en: Some offenders' families were split among the Five Capitals; in the worst cases their hearts were taken as offerings at the ancestral temple.
entries.literal: Some had their households divided among the Five Capitals; in extreme cases hearts were taken to offer at the ancestral temple.

entries.zh: 雖由天祚救患無策，流為殘忍，亦由祖宗有以啟之也。
entries.en: Though Tianzuo, lacking any strategy to save the realm, drifted into cruelty, his ancestors had shown him the way.
entries.literal: Although Tianzuo, having no strategy to save the realm from disaster, drifted into cruelty, the ancestors too had given him cause to begin it.

entries.zh: 遼之先代，用法尚嚴。
entries.en: The early Liao rulers applied the law with notable severity.
entries.literal: Liao's early generations still valued severity in applying law.

entries.zh: 使其子孫皆有君人之量，知所自擇，猶非祖宗貽謀之道；
entries.en: Even if every descendant possessed true kingly stature and knew how to choose wisely, severity alone is not how ancestors bequeath good counsel;
entries.literal: Even if their descendants all possessed the measure of rulers and knew how to choose for themselves, this would still not be the way ancestors bequeath counsel;

entries.zh: 不幸一有昏暴者，少引以藉口，何所不至。
entries.en: but let one benighted tyrant cite that precedent, and there is no limit to what he may do.
entries.literal: if by misfortune there should be one benighted and violent, he need only cite it slightly as pretext — what limit would there be?

entries.zh: 然遼之季世，與其先代用刑同，而興亡異者何歟？
entries.en: Yet the late Liao applied punishment much as the early dynasty had—why did one flourish and the other perish?
entries.literal: Yet Liao's final age applied punishment like its forebears — why were rise and fall different?

entries.zh: 蓋創業之君，施之於法未定之前，民猶未敢測也；
entries.en: The founding ruler enforced severity before the law was fully codified, and the people still could not predict his will;
entries.literal: The founding ruler applied it before the law was fixed; the people still did not dare to fathom him;

entries.zh: 亡國之主，施之於法既定之後，民復何所賴焉。
entries.en: the last ruler enforced it after the law was fixed, and the people had nothing left to rely on.
entries.literal: the ruler who lost the state applied it after the law was already fixed — upon what could the people again rely?

entries.zh: 此其所為異也。
entries.en: That is the difference.
entries.literal: This is wherein their conduct differed.

entries.zh: 傳曰：「新國輕典。」
entries.en: The Documents says, "A new state uses light statutes."
entries.literal: The Classic of Documents says: "A new state uses light statutes."

entries.zh: 豈獨權事宜而已乎？
entries.en: Was that merely a matter of expedience?
entries.literal: Was this merely weighing expedients for the occasion?

entries.zh: 天祚未年，遊畋無度，頗有倦勤意。
entries.en: In his last years Tianzuo hunted without restraint and showed signs of weariness with rule.
entries.literal: In Tianzuo's last years he hunted without measure and showed considerable weariness of governing.

entries.zh: 諸子惟文妃所生敖盧斡最賢。
entries.en: Of all his sons, only Aoluwo, born of Consort Wen, was truly worthy.
entries.literal: Among his sons, only Aoluwo, born of Consort Wen, was most worthy.

entries.zh: 蕭奉先乃元妃兄，深忌之。
entries.en: Xiao Fengxian, elder brother of the Primary Consort, deeply resented him.
entries.literal: Xiao Fengxian was the elder brother of the Primary Consort and deeply envied him.

entries.zh: 會文妃之女兄適耶律撻曷裏，女弟適耶律余睹，奉先乃誣告余睹等謀立晉王，尊天祚為太上皇。
entries.en: Consort Wen's elder sister was married to Yelü Tahieli and her younger sister to Yelü Yudu; Fengxian then falsely accused Yudu and others of plotting to enthrone the Prince of Jin and make Tianzuo Retired Emperor.
entries.literal: It happened that Consort Wen's elder sister was wed to Yelü Tahieli and her younger sister to Yelü Yudu; Fengxian then falsely reported that Yudu and others plotted to enthrone the Prince of Jin and honor Tianzuo as Retired Emperor.

entries.zh: 遂戮撻曷裏及其妻，賜文妃自盡。
entries.en: Tahieli and his wife were executed, and Consort Wen was ordered to take her own life.
entries.literal: Tahieli and his wife were thereupon executed; Consort Wen was ordered to take her own life.

entries.zh: 敖盧斡以不與謀得免。
entries.en: Aoluwo was spared because he had not joined the plot.
entries.literal: Aoluwo escaped because he had not joined the plot.

entries.zh: 及天祚西狩奉聖州，又以耶律撒八等欲劫立敖盧斡，遂誅撒八，盡其黨與。
entries.en: When Tianzuo marched west to Fengshengzhou, he was told that Yelü Saba and others meant to seize him and enthrone Aoluwo; Saba was executed and his entire faction destroyed.
entries.literal: When Tianzuo went west on campaign to Fengshengzhou, it was again reported that Yelü Saba and others wished to seize him and enthrone Aoluwo; Saba was executed and his entire faction destroyed.

entries.zh: 敖盧斡以有人望，即日賜死。
entries.en: Because Aoluwo enjoyed popular esteem, he was ordered to die that same day.
entries.literal: Because Aoluwo enjoyed popular esteem, that same day he was granted death.

entries.zh: 當時從行百官、諸局承應人及軍士聞者，皆流涕。
entries.en: Every official, bureau attendant, and soldier on the march who heard of it wept.
entries.literal: All the officials on the march, bureau attendants, and soldiers who heard it wept.

entries.zh: 蓋自興宗時，遽起大獄，仁德皇后戕於幽所，遼政始衰。
entries.en: From Xingzong's reign great purges began; Empress Ren'ade died in confinement—and Liao governance began its decline.
entries.literal: From the time of Xingzong, great prisons were suddenly raised; Empress Ren'ade perished in confinement — Liao government began to decline.

entries.zh: 道宗殺宣懿皇后，遷昭懷太子，太子尋被害。
entries.en: Daozong killed Empress Xuanyi and banished Crown Prince Zhaohuai, who was soon murdered.
entries.literal: Daozong killed Empress Xuanyi, transferred Crown Prince Zhaohuai, and the crown prince was soon murdered.

entries.zh: 天祚知其父之冤，而己亦幾殆，至是又自殺其子敖盧斡。
entries.en: Tianzuo knew the injustice done to his father and had himself nearly died for it; now he killed his own son Aoluwo.
entries.literal: Tianzuo knew his father's wrongful death, and he himself had nearly perished; at this point he again killed his own son Aoluwo.

entries.zh: 《傳》曰：「於所厚者薄，無所不薄矣。」
entries.en: The Commentary says, "He who is sparing toward those he favors will be sparing toward everyone."
entries.literal: The "Commentary" says: "Where one is sparing toward those he favors, he will be sparing toward all."

entries.zh: 遼二百餘年，骨肉屢相殘滅。
entries.en: For more than two hundred years the Liao royal house repeatedly destroyed its own kin.
entries.literal: For more than two hundred years Liao, flesh and bone repeatedly destroyed one another.

entries.zh: 天祚荒暴尤甚，遂至於亡，噫！
entries.en: Tianzuo was more benighted and violent than any before him, and so the dynasty fell — alas!
entries.literal: Tianzuo was especially benighted and violent, and thus came to ruin — alas!

entries.zh: 刑法志下
entries.en: Punishment and Law, Part Two
entries.literal: Treatise on Punishment and Law, Part Two

entries.zh: 天開於子，地闢於丑，人生於寅。
entries.en: Heaven came into being in the hour of zi, earth was shaped in the hour of chou, and humankind arose in the hour of yin.
entries.literal: Heaven opened at zi, earth was carved at chou, and humanity was born at yin.

entries.zh: 天地人之初，一焉耳矣。
entries.en: In the beginning, heaven, earth, and humanity were one and the same.
entries.literal: At the beginning of heaven, earth, and humanity, they were one — that is all.

entries.zh: 天動也，有恆度；
entries.en: Heaven is in motion and keeps to fixed cycles;
entries.literal: Heaven moves and has constant measures;

entries.zh: 地靜也，有恆形；
entries.en: earth is at rest and holds to fixed shapes;
entries.literal: earth is still and has constant forms;

entries.zh: 人動靜無方，居止靡常。
entries.en: but humankind moves and settles without fixed pattern, with no constant place to live.
entries.literal: humanity moves and rests without fixed direction; dwelling and stopping are without constancy.

entries.zh: 天主流行，地主蓄泄，二氣無往而弗達，亦惟人之所在而畀付焉。
entries.en: Heaven presides over circulation, earth over storage and release; the two vital forces penetrate everywhere, and only where people dwell are they bestowed.
entries.literal: Heaven governs circulation; earth governs storing and releasing. The two qi go nowhere without reaching through, and only wherever humanity is located is the entrustment made.

entries.zh: 庖犧氏降，炎帝氏、黃帝氏子孫眾多，王畿之封建有限，王政之布濩無窮，故君四方者，多二帝子孫，而自服土中者本同出也。
entries.en: After Fuxi came down to rule, the lines of the Flame and Yellow Emperors multiplied. Royal fiefs within the heartland were finite, yet royal authority spread without limit; so most who held sway over the four directions were kin of those two emperors, and those who acknowledged rule within the central realm shared the same ancestry.
entries.literal: When Fuxi descended, the descendants of the Flame Emperor and Yellow Emperor were numerous. Enfeoffments within the royal domain were limited, but the spread of royal government was unbounded. Thus those who ruled the four quarters were mostly descendants of the two emperors, and those who submitted within the central lands were fundamentally of the same origin.

entries.zh: 考之宇文周之書，遼本炎帝之後，而耶律儼稱遼為軒轅後。
entries.en: Consulting the histories of Northern Zhou, Liao was originally a line of the Flame Emperor, whereas Yelü Yan in his chronicle called Liao a line of the Yellow Emperor.
entries.literal: Examining the books of Yuwen Zhou, Liao was originally descended from the Flame Emperor, yet Yelü Yan called Liao descended from Xuan Yuan.

entries.zh: 儼志晚出，盍從周書。
entries.en: Yan's chronicle appeared later; we ought rather to follow the Zhou history.
entries.literal: Yan's chronicle came out late — better to follow Zhou Shu.

entries.zh: 蓋炎帝之裔曰葛烏菟者，世雄朔陲，後為冒頓可汗所襲，保鮮卑山以居，號鮮卑氏。
entries.en: A scion of the Flame Emperor named Gewu-tu had long dominated the northern marches; Modun, the Xiongnu chanyu, later overran him, and his people sheltered on the Xianbei Mountains and took the name Xianbei.
entries.literal: A descendant of the Flame Emperor named Gewu-tu had long been powerful on the northern frontier; later he was attacked by Chanyu Modun, took refuge on the Xianbei Mountains to dwell, and was called the Xianbei clan.

entries.zh: 既而慕容燕破之，析其部曰宇文，曰庫莫奚，曰契丹。
entries.en: The Murong state of Former Yan later defeated them and divided their people into the Yuwen, Kumoxi, and Khitan.
entries.literal: Then the Murong state of Yan defeated them and split their tribes into Yuwen, Kumoxi, and Khitan.

entries.zh: 契丹之名，昉見于此。
entries.en: The name Khitan makes its first appearance at this point.
entries.literal: The name Khitan first appears here.

entries.zh: 隋、唐之際，契丹之君號大賀氏。
entries.en: In the Sui and Tang periods, the Khitan rulers bore the clan name Dahe.
entries.literal: Between Sui and Tang, the Khitan rulers were of the Dahe clan.

entries.zh: 武后遣將擊潰其眾，大賀氏微，別部長過折代之。
entries.en: Empress Wu dispatched generals who shattered their armies; the Dahe line waned, and Guo-zhe, chief of a collateral tribe, took their place.
entries.literal: Empress Wu sent generals who routed their forces; the Dahe clan declined, and the allied-chieftain Guo-zhe replaced them.

entries.zh: 過折尋滅，迭剌部長涅里立迪輦組里為阻午可汗，更號遙輦氏。
entries.en: Guo-zhe was soon eliminated; Nieli, head of the Yila tribe, enthroned Dilian Zuli as Zuwu Khan and adopted the clan name Yaolian.
entries.literal: Guo-zhe was soon destroyed; Nieli, chief of the Yila tribe, installed Dilian Zuli as Zuwu Khan and changed the name to Yaolian.

entries.zh: 唐賜國姓，曰李懷秀。
entries.en: Tang granted the imperial surname Li, and he was known as Li Huaixiu.
entries.literal: Tang bestowed the imperial surname; he was called Li Huaixiu.

entries.zh: 既而懷秀叛唐，更封楷落為王。
entries.en: Huaixiu later rebelled against Tang, and Kai-luo was enfeoffed as king in his stead.
entries.literal: Huaixiu then rebelled against Tang; Kai-luo was enfeoffed as king instead.

entries.zh: 而涅里之後曰耨里思者，左右懷秀。
entries.en: Among Nieli's descendants was Noulishi, who supported Huaixiu.
entries.literal: Among Nieli's descendants was Noulishi, who stood at Huaixiu's side.

entries.zh: 楷落至于屈戍幾百年，國勢復振。
entries.en: From Kai-luo down to Qushu spanned nearly a century, and the kingdom's strength revived.
entries.literal: From Kai-luo to Qushu was nearly a hundred years; the state's power revived.

entries.zh: 至耨里思之孫曰阿保機，功業勃興，號世里氏，是為遼太祖。
entries.en: Noulishi's grandson Abaoji raised a flourishing realm, took the clan name Shili, and became Taizu of Liao.
entries.literal: To Noulishi's grandson Abaoji, whose achievements flourished — styled the Shili clan — this was Liao Taizu.

entries.zh: 於是世里氏與大賀、遙輦號「三耶律」。
entries.en: The Shili line together with Dahe and Yaolian were henceforth known as the "Three Yelü."
entries.literal: Thus the Shili clan together with Dahe and Yaolian were called the "Three Yelü."

entries.zh: 自時厥後，國日益大。
entries.en: From that time on the realm grew ever greater.
entries.literal: From that time onward the state grew daily larger.

entries.zh: 起唐季，涉五代、宋，二百餘年。
entries.en: It arose in late Tang, endured through the Five Dynasties and Song, and lasted more than two hundred years.
entries.literal: Beginning in late Tang, passing through the Five Dynasties and Song — more than two hundred years.

entries.zh: 名隨代遷，字傳音轉，此其言語文字之相通，可考而知者也。
entries.en: Names shifted with each dynasty and written forms followed changing sounds; such links between their speech and writing can be traced and verified.
entries.literal: Names changed with the era and characters shifted with pronunciation; this is how their language and script correspond, knowable through investigation.

entries.zh: 其所不可知者，有若奇首可汗、胡剌可汗、蘇可汗、昭古可汗，皆遼之先，而世次不可考矣。
entries.en: What remains unknowable includes such early khans as Qishou, Hula, Su, and Zhaogu — all forebears of Liao — whose order of succession cannot be established.
entries.literal: What cannot be known includes Qishou Khan, Hula Khan, Su Khan, and Zhaogu Khan — all predecessors of Liao — but their generations cannot be traced.

entries.zh: 摭其可知者，作遼世表。
entries.en: Collecting what can be established, I have compiled this Lineage Table of Liao.
entries.literal: Gathering what can be known, this Lineage Table of Liao was composed.

entries.zh: 唐
entries.en: Tang
entries.literal: Tang

entries.zh: 契丹地直京師東北五千里而贏，東距高麗，西奚，南營州，北靺鞨、室韋，阻冷陘山以自固。射獵居處無常。其君大賀氏有勝兵四萬，析八部，臣于突厥，以為俟斤。凡調發攻戰，則諸部畢會，獵則部得自行。與奚不平，每鬬不利，輒遁保鮮卑山。武德初，武德初 初原作「中」，據下文二年及舊唐書一九九下契丹傳改。大帥孫敖曹與靺鞨長突地稽俱來朝。二年，入犯平州境。六年，君長咄羅獻名馬、豐貂。貞觀二年，摩會來降，突厥請以梁師都易契丹，太宗曰：「契丹、突厥不同類，師都唐編戶，我將擒之，不可易降者。」三年，摩會入朝，賜鼓纛，由是有常貢。帝伐高麗，悉發契丹、奚首領從軍。還過營州，以窟哥為左武衞將軍。大帥辱紇主據曲率眾來歸，辱紇主據曲 辱紇主原誤「紇主」，據新唐書二一九契丹傳改。據曲，參卷三二校勘記[七]。即其部為玄州，以據曲為刺史，隸營州都督府。窟哥舉部內屬，乃置松漠都督府，以窟哥為都督，封無極男，賜姓李氏。以達稽部為峭落州，紇便部為彈汗州，獨活部為無逢州，芬問部羽陵州，突便部為日連州，芮奚部為徒河州，墜斤部為萬丹州，伏部為匹黎、赤山二州，俱隸松漠府，以辱紇主為刺史。窟哥死，與奚叛，行軍總管阿史德樞賓執松漠都督阿不固，阿不固 按新唐書契丹傳作阿卜固。獻于東都。窟哥二孫：曰枯莫離，彈汗州刺史、歸順郡王；曰盡忠，松漠都督。敖曹曾孫曰萬榮，敖曹曾孫曰萬榮 曾孫，舊唐書契丹傳同。新唐書契丹傳作「有孫曰萬榮」。歸誠州刺史。時營州都督趙文翽數侵侮其下，盡忠等怨望，與萬榮共舉兵，殺文翽，據營州，自號「無上可汗」，推萬榮為帥。不二旬，眾數萬，攻崇州，執擊討副使許欽寂。武后怒，詔將軍曹仁師等二十八將擊之，更號萬榮曰「萬斬」，盡忠曰「盡滅」。戰西硤石黃獐谷，王師敗績。進攻平州，不克。武后益發兵擊契丹。萬榮夜襲檀州，清邊道副總管張九節拒戰，萬榮敗走。俄盡忠死，突厥默啜襲破其部。萬榮收散兵，復振。別將駱務整、何阿小入冀州，殺刺史陸寶積，掠數千人。武后聞盡忠死，詔夏官尚書王孝傑等率兵十七萬討萬榮，戰東硤石，敗績，孝傑死之，萬榮進屠幽州。又詔御史大夫婁師德等率兵二十萬擊之，萬榮乘銳，鼓行而南，殘瀛州屬縣。神兵道總管楊玄基率奚掩擊，神兵道總管楊玄基 原作神兵總管楊立基，據新唐書契丹傳改。大破萬榮，執何阿小，別將李楷固、駱務整降。萬榮委軍走，玄基與奚四面合擊，萬榮眾潰，東走。張九節設三伏待之。萬榮窮蹙，與家奴輕騎走潞河東，憊甚，臥林下。奴斬其首以獻，九節傳東都。契丹餘眾不能立，遂附突厥。開元二年，盡忠從父弟失活率部落歸唐。 : 失活，玄宗賜丹書鐵券。開元四年，與奚長李大酺偕來，詔復置松漠府，以失活為都督，封松漠郡王；仍置靜析軍；以失活為經略大使，八部長皆為刺史。五年，以楊氏為永樂公主下嫁失活。五年以楊氏為永樂公主下嫁失活 按舊唐書契丹傳，「開元三年，其首領李失活率種落內附。明年，失活入朝，封宗室外甥女楊氏為永樂公主以妻之。」六年，卒。 : 娑固，失活之弟，帝以娑固襲爵。開元七年十一月，娑固與公主來朝。衙官可突于勇悍，得眾心，娑固欲除之；事泄，可突于攻之，娑固奔營州。都督許欽澹及奚君李大酺攻可突于，不勝，娑固、大酺皆死。（韓愈作可突干，劉昫、宋祁及唐會要皆作可突于。） : 鬱于，娑固從父弟也，可突于推以為主，遣使謝罪，玄宗冊立襲娑固位。開元十年，鬱于入朝，以慕容氏為燕郡公主下嫁鬱于，卒。 : 咄于，咄于 按新、舊唐書契丹傳及通考三四五並作吐于。鬱于之弟，襲官爵。開元十三年，咄于復與可突于猜阻，與公主來奔，改封遼陽王。遼陽王 按新、舊唐書契丹傳作遼陽郡王。 : 邵固，咄于之弟，邵固咄于之弟 按新、舊唐書契丹傳作李盡忠之弟。國人共立之。開元十三年冬，朝于行在，從封禪泰山，改封廣化郡王，以陳氏為東光公主下嫁邵固。東光公主 新、舊唐書契丹傳作東華公主。十八年，為可突于所弒，以其眾降突厥，東光公主走平盧。 : 屈列，屈列 新唐書契丹傳作屈烈，張九齡曲江集八作據埒。不知其世系，可突于立之。開元二十二年六月，幽州節度使張宇珪大破可突于。幽州節度使張守珪 新、舊唐書契丹傳並作幽州長史張守珪。按當時張守珪官銜為「幽州節度副大使、幽州長史兼御史大夫」，見曲江集九。十二月，又破之，斬屈列及可突于等，傳首東都，餘眾散走山谷。 過折，過折 按曲江集卷五、卷八作鬱捷，卷九、卷十一作過折。遇、鬱音同，過似應作遇。本契丹部長，為松漠府衙官，斬可突于及屈列歸唐。幽州節度使張守珪立之，封北平郡王。是年，可突于餘黨泥禮弒過折，屠其家，一子剌乾走安東，拜左驍衞將軍。自此，契丹中衰，大賀氏附庸於奚王，以通于唐，朝貢歲至。至德、寶應間再至，大曆中十三至，大曆中十三至 原誤「大曆十二年」，據新唐書契丹傳改。按大曆凡十四年，約每年一次。貞元九年、十年、十一年三至，元和中七至，太和、開成間四至。泥禮，耶律儼遼史書為涅里，陳大任書為雅里，蓋遼太祖之始祖也。 李懷秀，唐賜姓名，契丹名迪輦俎里，契丹名迪輦俎里 按上文作迪輦組里。本八部大帥。天寶四年降唐，拜松漠都督。安祿山表請討契丹，懷秀發兵十萬，懷秀發兵十萬 按新唐書契丹傳，安祿山發幽州、雲中、平盧、河東兵十餘萬。非懷秀發兵十萬。與祿山戰潢水南，祿山大敗，自是與祿山兵連不解。耶律儼紀云，太祖四代祖耨里思為迭剌部夷離菫，遺將只里姑、括里，大敗范陽安祿山于潢水，適當懷秀之世。則懷秀固遙輦氏之首君，為阻午可汗明矣。 楷落，以唐封恭仁王，代松漠都督，遂稱契丹王。其後寖大，貞元四年，犯北邊，幽州以聞。自祿山反，河北割據，道隔不通，世次不可悉考。世次不可悉考 按百官志一，遙輦九帳大常袞司已列遙輦九世可汗世次。 : 契丹王屈戍，武宗會昌二年授雲麾將軍，是為耶瀾可汗。授雲麾將軍是為耶瀾可汗 「是為耶瀾可汗」原在下文「幽州節度使」下，誤以屈戍為幽州節度使。據新唐書契丹傳改。幽州節度使張仲武奏契丹舊用回鶻印，乞賜聖造，詔以「奉國契丹」為文。（高麗古今錄作屈戌。） : 契丹王習爾，習爾 新唐書契丹傳作習爾之。是為巴剌可汗。咸通中，再遣使貢獻，部落寖強。 : 契丹王欽德，習爾之族也，是為痕德蓳可汗。光啟中，鈔掠奚、室韋諸部，皆役服之，數與劉仁恭相攻。晚年政衰。八部大人，法常三歲代，迭剌部耶律阿保機建旗鼓，自為一部，不肯受代，自號為王，盡有契丹國，遙輦氏遂亡。 : 蕭韓家奴有言，先世遙輦可汗洼之後，國祚中絕，自夷離菫雅里立阻午可汗，大位始定。今以唐史、遼史參考，大賀氏絕于邵固，雅里所立則懷秀也，其間唯屈列、過折二世。屈列乃可突于所立，過折以別部長為雅里所殺。唐史稱泥里為可突于餘黨，則洼可汗者，殆為屈列耶？
entries.en: Khitan territory lay five thousand li northeast of the capital, stretching east to Goguryeo, west to the Xi, south to Yingzhou, and north to the Mohe and Shiwei, with the Lengling range as their barrier. They hunted for a living and moved their camps at will. The Dahe chiefs commanded forty thousand warriors organized in eight tribes; they acknowledged the Turks as overlords and served as irkin. All tribes mustered for war, but each could hunt on its own. They feuded constantly with the Xi, usually lost, and retreated to the Xianbei Mountains. Early in the Wude era — the opening "chu" was originally written "zhong," corrected from the year-2 notice and Jiu Tang Shu 199b — Grand Chief Sun Aocao and the Mohe leader Tudi Ji presented themselves at court. In year 2 they raided Pingzhou. In year 6 Chief Zhuoluo offered fine horses and pelts. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui surrendered; when the Turks asked to swap Liang Shidu for the Khitan, Taizong replied, "Khitan and Turk are not kin; Shidu is a subject household of Tang — I mean to take him — and I will not trade away those who have submitted." Mo Hui visited court in year 3, received drums and banners, and thereafter paid regular tribute. Campaigning against Goguryeo, the emperor drafted every Khitan and Xi leader. On the return through Yingzhou he appointed Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The grand chieftain Quju brought his people in; ruhezhu was his chiefly title, while the parallel account reverses the transmitted name Juqu to Quju. See Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 note [7]. His band became Xuan Prefecture under Juqu, attached to Yingzhou. When Kuge led the whole tribe inward, Songmo Protectorate was founded: Kuge became protector, was enfeoffed Lord of Wuji, and received the surname Li. The Daqi became Qiaoluo Prefecture, Hebian Tanhan, Duhuo Wufeng, Fenwen Yuling, Tubian Rilian, Ruixi Tuhe, Zhuijin Wandan, and the Fu line the twin prefectures Pili and Chishan — all under Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. After Kuge's death they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo protector Abu Gu (A Bu Gu in Xin Tang Shu) and sent him to Luoyang. Kuge left two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun, and Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson Wanrong — the line repeats; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — held Guicheng Prefecture. Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi bullied their people until Jinzhong and Wanrong rose together, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, proclaimed themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days they mustered tens of thousands, took Chongzhou, and captured suppression vice-commissioner Xu Qinji. Empress Wu sent Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial force was routed. They failed to capture Pingzhou. Wu sent more troops. Wanrong struck Tanzhou by night; Zhang Jiujie of the Qingbian command drove him off. Jinzhong soon died and Turk Mokchuo shattered the tribe. Wanrong regrouped. Lieutenants Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed prefect Lu Baoji, and carried off thousands. Learning of Jinzhong's death, Wu ordered Wang Xiaojie and one hundred seventy thousand men against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were beaten, Xiaojie was killed, and Wanrong sacked Youzhou. Lou Shide followed with two hundred thousand; Wanrong marched south in full vigor and ravaged Yingzhou's counties. Shenbing commander Yang Xuanji — the text's Yang Liji is wrong per Xin Tang Shu — led Xi auxiliaries, crushed Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and accepted the surrender of Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng. Wanrong abandoned his army; Xuanji and the Xi closed in from four sides until his host broke and fled east. Zhang Jiujie laid three ambushes. Cornered, Wanrong fled east of the Lu River with a household slave; exhausted, he lay under trees while the slave took his head to Jiujie, who sent it to Luoyang. The Khitan remnant could not endure and joined the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's cousin Shihuo brought the tribe back. : Shihuo received an iron certificate from Xuanzong. In Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; the court restored Songmo, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-created the Jingxi Army, appointed him frontier commissioner, and made the eight chiefs prefects. In year 5 the Yang clanswoman became Princess Yongle and married him — per Jiu Tang Shu, "In Kaiyuan year 3 their chief Li Shihuo led his tribes to submit inward; the next year Shihuo entered court, and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made Princess Yongle and given to him in marriage." He died in year 6. : Suogu, Shihuo's brother, inherited. In Kaiyuan 7/11 Suogu and the princess attended court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was bold and popular; Suogu tried to kill him, the plot failed, Ketuyu attacked, and Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu, failed, and both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's cousin, was set up by Ketuyu, apologized to court, and Xuanzong confirmed him in Suogu's place. In Kaiyuan 10 Yuyu came to court; a Murong clanswoman became Princess of Yancheng and married him; he died. : Tuyu (Zhuoyu in this text; Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345), Yuyu's brother, succeeded. In Kaiyuan 13 he quarreled with Ketuyu and fled with the princess; the court enfeoffed him Prince of Liaoyang (Commandery in both Tang histories). : Shaogu, Tuyu's brother — both Tang histories say Li Jinzhong's brother — was raised by the people. In Kaiyuan 13 winter he attended the mobile court, joined the Fengshan at Mount Tai, became Prince of Guanghua, and a Chen clanswoman became Princess Dongguang (Donghua in both Tang histories) and married him. In year 18 Ketuyu murdered him, led the people to the Turks, and the princess fled to Pinglu. : Qulie (Qulie in Xin Tang Shu; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 has Julei), lineage unknown, enthroned by Ketuyu. In Kaiyuan 22/6 Zhang Shougui of Youzhou — both histories say chief administrator; his title was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator of Youzhou, and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9 — routed Ketuyu. In month 12 he won again, beheaded Qulie, Ketuyu, and others, sent heads to Luoyang; survivors hid in the hills. Guo-zhe (Yujie in Qujiang ji 5 and 8; guo may stand for yu) was a Khitan chief and Songmo yamen officer who killed Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted. Zhang Shougui made him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's follower Ni-li killed Guo-zhe and exterminated his house; son Lagan escaped to Andong as Left Xiaowei General. Thereafter the Khitan waned; the Dahe clung to the Xi king to reach Tang with yearly tribute: twice in Zhide–Baoying, thirteen visits in the Dali era (not "the twelfth year of Dali"; the era lasted fourteen years), thrice in Zhenyuan 9–11, seven in Yuanhe, four in Taihe and Kaicheng. Ni-li — Nieli in Yelü Yan, Yali in Chen Daren — was ancestor to Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, given Tang name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli (Zuli above), was chief of the eight tribes. In Tianbao 4 he surrendered and became Songmo protector. An Lushan asked to campaign against the Khitan; the text says Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand — Xin Tang Shu says Lushan raised over one hundred thousand from four commands, not Huaixiu's army — and defeated Lushan south of the Huangshui, after which war with Lushan never ceased. Yelü Yan records that Taizu's fourth-generation forebear Noulishi, yilijin of the Yila, sent Zhiligu and Kulie to rout Fan Yang Lushan at the Huangshui in Huaixiu's day; Huaixiu was thus the first Yaolian lord and Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was called Khitan king. The state grew; in Zhenyuan 4 it raided the north and Youzhou reported. After Lushan's rebellion Hebei warlords blocked the roads and many generations are lost — yet Officials Treatise 1 lists nine Yaolian khans in the Nine Accounts office. : King Qushu, in Huichang 2 made Cloud-Banner General, was Yelan Khan — the title was misplaced under a Youzhou commissioner entry and is corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu said the Khitan still used Uyghur seals and begged a new imperial seal inscribed "Khitan Serving the State" (Goryeo's record has Quxu). : King Xier (Xierzhi in Xin Tang Shu) was Bala Khan; in Xiantong he twice sent tribute and the tribes strengthened. : King Qinde of Xier's line was Hendejin Khan; in Guangqi he raided Xi and Shiwei until all served him and fought Liu Rengong repeatedly; late in life his rule failed. Great men of the eight tribes rotated every three years, but Yila chief Yelü Abaoji raised his own banners, refused rotation, called himself king, seized all Khitan lands, and ended the Yaolian. : Xiao Hanjianu held that after Yaolian Khan Wa the line broke until yilijin Yali enthroned the Zuwu Khan. Comparing Tang and Liao sources, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali's enthronement was Huaixiu; only Qulie and Guo-zhe lay between. Qulie was Ketuyu's puppet; Guo-zhe, a collateral chief, was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant — so was Wa perhaps Qulie?
entries.literal: The Khitan lands lay five thousand li northeast of the capital and were expansive; east they bordered Goguryeo, west the Xi, south Yingzhou, north Mohe and Shiwei, securing themselves behind the Lengling Mountains. They hunted and had no fixed dwellings. Their ruler of the Dahe clan had forty thousand effective troops, divided into eight tribes, and submitted to the Turks as irkin. Whenever mobilized for attack or war all tribes assembled; for hunting each tribe could act on its own. They were at odds with the Xi; whenever they fought they fared poorly and fled to shelter on the Xianbei Mountains. At the beginning of Wude — chu was originally zhong, corrected per the account below for year 2 and Jiu Tang Shu 199b Khitan Account — Grand Chieftain Sun Aocao and the Mohe chief Tudi Ji both came to court. In year 2 they invaded Pingzhou territory. In year 6 Chieftain Zhuoluo presented famous horses and rich sables. In Zhenguan year 2 Mo Hui came to surrender; the Turks asked to exchange Liang Shidu for the Khitan, and Taizong said: "The Khitan and Turks are not the same kind; Shidu is a Tang registered household — I will capture him — one cannot exchange a surrendered people." In year 3 Mo Hui entered court and was given drums and banners; thereafter there was regular tribute. When the emperor campaigned against Goguryeo he mobilized all Khitan and Xi leaders to follow the army. Returning through Yingzhou he made Kuge Left Martial Guard General. The ruhezhu Quju, a grand chieftain, led his people to submit — the transmitted name Juqu is reversed to Quju in the parallel account, while ruhezhu is the Khitan chiefly title; see Xin Tang Shu 219 and juan 32 collation [7]. His tribe was made Xuanzhou with Juqu as prefect, subordinate to Yingzhou Protectorate. Kuge brought his whole tribe to submit inward; Songmo Protectorate was then established with Kuge as protector, enfeoffed as Lord of Wuji, surname Li bestowed. The Daqi tribe became Qiaoluo Prefecture, the Hebian tribe Tanhan Prefecture, the Duhuo tribe Wufeng Prefecture, the Fenwen tribe Yuling Prefecture, the Tubian tribe Rilian Prefecture, the Ruixi tribe Tuhe Prefecture, the Zhuijin tribe Wandan Prefecture, the Fu tribe the two prefectures Pili and Chishan — all subordinate to Songmo, with their respective chieftains as prefects. When Kuge died they rebelled with the Xi; campaigning general Ashide Shubin seized Songmo Protector Abu Gu — Xin Tang Shu reads A Bu Gu — and presented him in the eastern capital. Kuge's two grandsons: Kumoli, Tanhan prefect and Prince of Guishun; Jinzhong, Songmo protector. Aocao's great-grandson was Wanrong — duplicated; Jiu Tang Shu agrees; Xin Tang Shu reads "had a grandson Wanrong" — Guicheng prefect. The Yingzhou protector Zhao Wenbi repeatedly insulted their subordinates; Jinzhong and others resented it and with Wanrong jointly raised troops, killed Wenbi, seized Yingzhou, styled themselves "Supreme Khans," and made Wanrong commander. Within twenty days their force numbered tens of thousands; they attacked Chongzhou and captured Vice Commissioner for Suppression Xu Qinji. Empress Wu was enraged and ordered Generals Cao Renshi and twenty-seven others to attack them, renaming Wanrong "Wan the Beheaded" and Jinzhong "Jin the Exterminated." At Huangzhang Valley west of Xiashi the imperial army was defeated. Advancing on Pingzhou they could not take it. Empress Wu sent more troops against the Khitan. Wanrong raided Tanzhou by night; Qingbian Circuit Vice Commander Zhang Jiujie resisted and Wanrong fled. Soon Jinzhong died and the Turk Mokchuo struck and broke their tribe. Wanrong gathered scattered troops and revived. Lieutenant-generals Luo Wuzheng and He Axiao entered Jizhou, killed Prefect Lu Baoji, and plundered several thousand people. Hearing Jinzhong had died, Empress Wu ordered Minister of Summer Works Wang Xiaojie and others with one hundred seventy thousand troops against Wanrong; at East Xiashi they were defeated, Xiaojie died, and Wanrong advanced to slaughter Youzhou. She also ordered Censor-in-Chief Lou Shide and others with two hundred thousand troops; Wanrong with sharp momentum marched south in drum-order and ravaged counties subordinate to Yingzhou. Shenbing Circuit Commander Yang Xuanji led Xi in a flanking strike — originally Shenbing Commander Yang Liji, corrected per Xin Tang Shu — greatly defeated Wanrong, captured He Axiao, and lieutenants Li Kaigu and Luo Wuzheng surrendered. Wanrong abandoned his army and fled; Xuanji and the Xi struck from four sides, Wanrong's host collapsed and fled east. Zhang Jiujie set three ambushes. Wanrong in extremity fled east of the Lu River with a household slave on light horses, utterly exhausted, lying under a grove; the slave cut off his head and presented it, and Jiujie sent it to the eastern capital. The Khitan remnant could not stand and attached to the Turks. In Kaiyuan year 2 Jinzhong's younger cousin Shihuo led the tribe back to Tang. : Shihuo — Xuanzong bestowed an iron certificate. Kaiyuan year 4 he came with Xi chief Li Dachi; an edict restored Songmo Prefecture, made Shihuo protector and Prince of Songmo, re-established the Jingxi Army, made Shihuo frontier commissioner, and the eight tribal chiefs all became prefects. Year 5 the Yang clanswoman was made Princess Yongle and married to Shihuo — per Jiu Tang Shu, year 3 Shihuo submitted, year 4 he attended court and the emperor's clanswoman Yang was made princess. Year 6 he died. : Suogu, Shihuo's younger brother — the emperor had Suogu inherit the title. Kaiyuan year 7 month 11 Suogu and the princess came to court. Yamen officer Ketuyu was fierce and won the people's hearts; Suogu wished to remove him; the plot leaked and Ketuyu attacked; Suogu fled to Yingzhou. Protector Xu Qindan and Xi lord Li Dachi attacked Ketuyu without success; Suogu and Dachi both died. (Han Yu writes Ketugan; Liu Xu, Song Qi, and Tang Huiyao all write Ketuyu.) : Yuyu, Suogu's younger cousin — Ketuyu pushed him as leader, sent envoys to apologize, and Xuanzong enfeoffed him to succeed Suogu. Kaiyuan year 10 Yuyu entered court; the Murong clanswoman was made Princess of Yancheng and married to Yuyu; he died. : Tuyu — written Zhuoyu in this text but Tuyu in both Tang histories and Tongkao 345 — Yuyu's younger brother, inherited office and title. Kaiyuan year 13 Tuyu again clashed with Ketuyu and fled to court with the princess, enfeoffed Prince of Liaoyang — both Tang histories read Prince of Liaoyang Commandery. : Shaogu, Tuyu's younger brother — both Tang histories read younger brother of Li Jinzhong — the people jointly enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 13 winter he attended the traveling palace, followed the Fengshan at Mount Tai, was changed to Prince of Guanghua, and the Chen clanswoman was made Princess Dongguang and married to Shaogu — both Tang histories read Donghua Princess. Year 18 he was assassinated by Ketuyu, who led his people to surrender to the Turks; Princess Dongguang fled to Pinglu. : Qulie — Xin Tang Shu reads Qulie; Zhang Jiuling's Qujiang ji 8 reads Julei — lineage unknown; Ketuyu enthroned him. Kaiyuan year 22 month 6 Youzhou Military Commissioner Zhang Shougui greatly defeated Ketuyu — both Tang histories read Youzhou Chief Administrator Zhang Shougui; his title then was "Vice Military Commissioner of Youzhou, Chief Administrator and Censor-in-Chief," per Qujiang ji 9. Month 12 he defeated them again, beheaded Qulie and Ketuyu and others, sent heads to the eastern capital; the remainder scattered into the valleys. Guo-zhe — Qujiang ji 5 and 8 read Yujie, 9 and 11 read Guo-zhe; yu and yu sound alike; guo should perhaps be yu — was originally a Khitan tribal chief, Songmo yamen officer, who beheaded Ketuyu and Qulie and submitted to Tang. Zhang Shougui enthroned him and enfeoffed him Prince of Beiping. That year Ketuyu's remnant Ni-li assassinated Guo-zhe and slaughtered his family; one son Lagan fled to Andong and was appointed Left Xiaowei General. From this the Khitan declined; the Dahe attached themselves as vassals to the Xi king to reach Tang, tribute coming yearly. Between Zhide and Baoying they came twice; in Dali thirteen times — originally miswritten Dali year 12, corrected per Xin Tang Shu; Dali had fourteen years, roughly once a year — Zhenyuan years 9–11 three times, Yuanhe seven times, Taihe and Kaicheng four times. Ni-li — Yelü Yan's Liao history writes Nieli, Chen Daren writes Yali — was the progenitor of Liao Taizu. Li Huaixiu, Tang bestowed name and surname, Khitan name Dilian Zuli — above written Zuli — originally great chief of the eight tribes. Tianbao year 4 he surrendered to Tang and was appointed Songmo protector. An Lushan memorialized to campaign against the Khitan; Huaixiu raised one hundred thousand troops — per Xin Tang Shu An Lushan raised more than one hundred thousand from Youzhou, Yunzhong, Pinglu, and Hedong; not Huaixiu's one hundred thousand — fought Lushan south of the Huangshui; Lushan was greatly defeated, and thereafter fighting with Lushan was unceasing. Yelü Yan's annals say Taizu's fourth-generation ancestor Noulishi as Yila tribe yilijin sent generals Zhiligu and Kulie to greatly defeat Fan Yang An Lushan at the Huangshui, exactly in Huaixiu's time; thus Huaixiu was clearly the first lord of the Yaolian and the Zuwu Khan. Kai-luo, enfeoffed by Tang as Prince Gongren, replaced the Songmo protector and was then called Khitan king. Thereafter they gradually grew; Zhenyuan year 4 they raided the northern frontier and Youzhou reported it. From Lushan's rebellion the Hebei was carved up and communications cut; generations cannot all be traced — per Officials Treatise 1 the Yaolian Nine Accounts Grand Constant already lists nine generations of khans. : Khitan King Qushu — in Wuzong's Huichang year 2 appointed Cloud-Banner General — this is Yelan Khan. The phrase "is Yelan Khan" was originally placed under "Youzhou Military Commissioner," mistaking Qushu for commissioner; corrected per Xin Tang Shu. Youzhou Commissioner Zhang Zhongwu memorialized that the Khitan formerly used Uyghur seals and begged a newly made imperial seal; an edict used the text "Khitan Serving the State." (Goryeo's ancient record writes Quxu.) : Khitan King Xier — Xin Tang Shu reads Xierzhi — was Bala Khan. In Xiantong he twice sent envoys with tribute and the tribes grew stronger. : Khitan King Qinde, of Xier's clan, was Hendejin Khan. In Guangqi he raided the Xi and Shiwei tribes and made them all serve; he repeatedly fought Liu Rengong. In his later years government declined. The eight tribal great men were by law replaced every three years; Yila tribe Yelü Abaoji raised banners and drums, made himself a separate tribe, refused rotation, styled himself king, possessed the whole Khitan state, and the Yaolian perished. : Xiao Hanjianu said that after the Yaolian Khan Wa the royal line was cut off, and from yilijin Yali enthroning the Zuwu Khan the great throne was first fixed. Comparing Tang and Liao histories now, the Dahe ended with Shaogu; Yali enthroned Huaixiu; between them were only Qulie and Guo-zhe. Qulie was enthroned by Ketuyu; Guo-zhe as collateral chief was killed by Yali. Tang history calls Ni-li Ketuyu's remnant; then Khan Wa was perhaps Qulie?

entries.zh: 契丹國在庫莫奚東，異族同類，東部鮮卑之別支也，至是始自號契丹。為慕容氏所破，俱竄松漠之間。道武帝登國間，大破之，遂與庫莫奚分背。經數十年，稍滋蔓，有部落於和龍之北數百里。太武帝太平真君以來，歲致名馬。獻文時，使莫弗紇何辰來獻，始班諸國末，欣服。始班諸國末欣服 按此源於魏書一００契丹傳：「得班饗於諸國之末」，「心皆忻慕」，「莫不思服」，欣服二字，語義不完。萬丹部、何大何部、伏弗郁部、羽陵部、日連部、匹絜部、黎部萬丹部（至）黎部 萬丹部，按營衞志中及魏書一００、新唐書二一九契丹傳並作悉萬丹部。日連部，連原誤「速」，據營衞志中及魏書、新唐書契丹傳改。伏弗郁、羽陵、匹絜、黎等部參卷三二校勘記[二][三]。吐六于部以名馬文皮來貢，得交市于和龍、密雲之間。太和三年，高句麗與蠕蠕謀取地豆于以分之，契丹懼，莫弗賀勿于率其部落車三千乘、眾萬餘口內附，止於白狼水東。
entries.en: The Khitan lay east of the Kumoxi: a distinct people of the same stock, an offshoot of the eastern Xianbei, and only then did they first call themselves Khitan. Broken by the Murong, they all fled into the Songmo steppe. Emperor Daowu crushed them during his Dengguo campaigns, after which they parted from the Kumoxi. Within decades they spread again, with camps several hundred li north of Helong. From Taiping Zhenjun of Emperor Taiwu they sent tribute horses each year. Under Emperor Xianwen the envoy Mofu Hechen presented tribute and was seated last among the tributary states in delighted submission — the text's "delighted submission" is corrupt; Wei Shu 100 reads that they were feasted after all other states and came away admiring and willing to obey. Tribes named Wandan (properly Xiwandan), Hedah, Fufuyu, Yuling, Rilian (not Su), Pijie, and Li — see juan 32 collation notes — joined the Tuliuyu in offering horses and furs and trading near Helong and Miyun. In Taihe year 3, when Goguryeo and Rouran schemed to seize and partition Didouyu, the Khitan were alarmed; Mofu Hewuyu led three thousand carts and more than ten thousand people to submit and settled east of the Bailang River.
entries.literal: The Khitan state lay east of the Kumoxi — a different tribe of the same kind, a separate branch of the eastern Xianbei — and only then first styled themselves Khitan. They were broken by the Murong and all fled into the Songmo region. During Emperor Daowu's Dengguo reign they were greatly defeated and then split from the Kumoxi. After several decades they gradually spread; there were tribes several hundred li north of Helong. From Emperor Taiwu's Taiping Zhenjun reign onward they sent famous horses yearly. In Emperor Xianwen's time the envoy Mofu Hechen came to offer tribute and was first ranked last among the states, rejoicing in submission — "rejoicing in submission" is an incomplete phrase; per Wei Shu 100 Khitan Account it derives from "received banquets last among the states," "all admired in heart," and "none failed to submit in thought." The Wandan, Hedah, Fufuyu, Yuling, Rilian, Pijie, and Li clans — Wandan should read Xiwandan per Yingwei Records, Wei Shu 100, and Xin Tang Shu 219; Rilian was miswritten Su. See collation notes to juan 32 [2][3] for Fufuyu, Yuling, Pijie, and Li. The Tuliuyu clan brought famous horses and patterned pelts as tribute and traded at Helong and Miyun. In Taihe year 3 Goguryeo and Rouran plotted to seize Didouyu and divide it; the Khitan feared this. Mofu Hewuyu led his tribes — three thousand carts and more than ten thousand people — to submit inward and halted east of the Bailang River.

entries.zh: 開皇四年，率諸莫弗賀來謁。五年，悉衆款塞，高祖納之，聽居故地。六年，諸部相攻不止，又與突厥相侵，高祖使使諭解之。別部出伏等違高麗，率眾內附，置於渴奚那頡之北。開皇末，別部四千餘戶違突厥來降，高祖給糧遣還；固辭不去，部落漸眾。遂北徙，逐水草，當遼西正北二百里，依紇臣水而居。紇臣水 按隋書八四、北史九四契丹傳作託紇臣水。東西亙五百里，南北三百里，分為十部，兵多者三千，少者千餘。有征伐，酋帥相與議之，興兵則合符契。突厥沙鉢略可汗遣吐屯潘垤統之，契丹殺吐屯。大業七年，貢方物。
entries.en: In Kaihuang year 4 their Mohehe leaders came to court. The next year the entire people tendered submission at the border; Gaozu received them and let them remain on their old lands. In year 6 inter-tribal fighting and clashes with the Turks continued until Gaozu sent mediators. A collateral branch under Chufu broke with Goguryeo, submitted with its followers, and was settled north of Kexina. Late in Kaihuang more than four thousand households left the Turks and surrendered; Gaozu supplied grain for their return, but they refused to go back and their numbers swelled. They moved north along the pastures, two hundred li north of Liaoxi, settling on the Tuo Ge-chen River — so named in Sui Shu 84 and Beishi 94. Their territory ran five hundred li east–west and three hundred li north–south, divided into ten tribes with between one and three thousand fighters each. War was decided in council among the chiefs, who joined tallies to mobilize. Shabolue of the Turks sent Tutun Pan Chi to oversee them, but the Khitan killed Tutun. In Daye year 7 they sent tribute goods.
entries.literal: In Kaihuang year 4 they led all the Mohehe to pay court. In year 5 the whole people submitted at the frontier; Emperor Gaozu accepted them and allowed them to dwell in their former lands. In year 6 the tribes attacked one another without cease and also encroached on each other with the Turks; Gaozu sent envoys to admonish and reconcile them. The collateral tribe Chufu and others broke with Goguryeo, led their people to submit inward, and were placed north of Kexina. At the end of Kaihuang a collateral tribe of more than four thousand households broke from the Turks and came to surrender; Gaozu gave grain and sent them back, but they firmly refused to leave and the tribe gradually grew. They then moved north following pasture and water, two hundred li due north of Liaoxi, dwelling along the Ge-chen River — per Sui Shu 84 and Beishi 94 this is the Tuo Ge-chen River. East to west it stretched five hundred li, north to south three hundred li; they were divided into ten tribes, the strongest fielding three thousand warriors, the weakest over a thousand. When there was campaigning the chiefs deliberated together; to raise troops they joined tally-tokens. The Turk Shabolue Khan sent Tutun Pan Chi to command them; the Khitan killed Tutun. In Daye year 7 they presented local products.

entries.en: Sagezhi, the first.
entries.literal: Sagezhi, the first.

entries.zh: 封鄭國公主。咸雍中，徙封魏國。咸雍中徙封魏國 雍原作「和」，陳大任避金世宗雍名改，元人回改遺漏，今回改。
entries.en: She was enfeoffed Princess of Zheng State; during the Xianyong era she was transferred to Wei State—the received text had "He" for Yong, altered by Chen Daren to avoid Jin Shizong's taboo and incompletely restored under the Yuan; the text is corrected accordingly.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Princess of Zheng State. During Xianyong, transferred to Wei State—the received text Xianyong was originally written "He"; Chen Daren changed it to avoid the taboo name of Jin Shizong Yong, and Yuan editors restored incompletely; corrected here.

entries.zh: 下嫁蕭末。下嫁蕭末 紀大康二年六月作蕭霞抹。
entries.en: She was given in marriage to Xiao Mo; the annals for the sixth month of Dakang year 2 write Xiao Xiamo.
entries.literal: Given in marriage to Xiao Mo—per the annals, in the sixth month of Dakang year 2 this is written Xiao Xiamo.

entries.zh: 端麗有智。
entries.en: She was graceful in bearing and quick of mind.
entries.literal: Comely and intelligent.

entries.zh: 大康初薨。
entries.en: She died at the beginning of the Dakang era.
entries.literal: Died at the beginning of Dakang.

entries.zh: 糺里，第二。
entries.en: Jiuli, the second.
entries.literal: Jiuli, the second.

entries.zh: 封齊國公主，進封趙國。
entries.en: She was enfeoffed Princess of Qi State and advanced to Princess of Zhao State.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Princess of Qi State, advanced to Zhao State.

entries.zh: 下嫁蕭撻不也。
entries.en: She was given in marriage to Xiao Tabuye.
entries.literal: Given in marriage to Xiao Tabuye.

entries.zh: 駙馬都尉撻不也坐昭懷太子事被害，其弟訛都斡欲逼尚公主，公主以訛都斡黨乙辛，惡之。未幾，訛都斡以事伏誅。天祚幼，乙辛用事。公主每以匡救為心，竟誅乙辛。
entries.en: Imperial Son-in-law Tabuye was executed for involvement in Prince Zhaohuai's affair; his younger brother Eduwo tried to force a marriage to the princess, but she detested him as a partisan of Yixin. Before long Eduwo was executed. Tianzuo was still young and Yixin held power; the princess constantly worked to rescue the court, and in the end Yixin was put to death.
entries.literal: Imperial Son-in-law Tabuye was killed for involvement in Prince Zhaohuai's affair; his younger brother Eduwo wished to force marriage to the princess, but the princess detested Eduwo as a partisan of Yixin. Before long Eduwo was executed for his crimes. Tianzuo was young and Yixin held power; the princess constantly sought to save and restore order, and in the end Yixin was executed.

entries.zh: 大安五年，以疾薨。
entries.en: In the fifth year of the Da'an era she died of illness.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Da'an, died of illness.

entries.zh: 特里，第三。
entries.en: Teri, the third.
entries.literal: Teri, the third.

entries.zh: 封越國公主。乾統初，進封秦晉國大長公主。徙封梁宋國大長公主。
entries.en: She was enfeoffed Princess of Yue State; at the beginning of the Qiantong era she was advanced to Grand Princess of Qin-Jin State and then transferred to Grand Princess of Liang-Song State.
entries.literal: Enfeoffed Princess of Yue State. At the beginning of Qiantong, advanced to Grand Princess of Qin-Jin State. Transferred to Grand Princess of Liang-Song State.

entries.zh: 下嫁蕭酬斡。
entries.en: She was given in marriage to Xiao Chouwo.
entries.literal: Given in marriage to Xiao Chouwo.

entries.zh: 公主從天祚出奔。明年，攻應州，留公主守輜重。金人圍之，公主奔行在所，天祚潛遁，為金人所獲。
entries.en: The princess fled with Tianzuo. The next year, when he attacked Ying Prefecture, he left her to guard the baggage train. Jin forces surrounded her; she fled to the traveling court while Tianzuo slipped away in secret and was captured by the Jin.
entries.literal: The princess followed Tianzuo in flight. The next year, attacking Ying Prefecture, he left the princess to guard the baggage train. Jin troops surrounded them; the princess fled to the traveling court, Tianzuo slipped away secretly, and was captured by Jin.

entries.zh: 大康八年，以駙馬都尉蕭酬斡得罪，離之。大安初，改適蕭特末。為都統，與金人戰，敗于石輦鐸，被擒。
entries.en: In the eighth year of the Dakang era she divorced Imperial Son-in-law Xiao Chouwo when he was punished; at the beginning of the Da'an era she remarried Xiao Temo. As commander-in-chief he fought the Jin, was defeated at Shinian Duo, and was captured.
entries.literal: In the eighth year of Dakang, because Imperial Son-in-law Xiao Chouwo was punished, she divorced him. At the beginning of Da'an she remarried Xiao Temo. As commander-in-chief he fought Jin and was defeated at Shinian Duo and captured.

entries.zh: 春秋之法，王姬下嫁書于策，以魯公同姓之國為之婚主故爾。
entries.en: According to the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a royal daughter was given in marriage the event was entered in the chronicle because Lu, a state of the same surname as the Zhou king, acted as ceremonial marriage host.
entries.literal: In the method of the Spring and Autumn Annals, when a king's daughter married down it was written in the chronicle, because the state of Lu, sharing the lord's surname, served as marriage host—hence this.

entries.zh: 古者，婦諱不出門，內言不出梱。
entries.en: In ancient times a woman's personal name never left the household, and family matters were not spoken of beyond the inner quarters.
entries.literal: In antiquity a woman's tabooed name did not leave the door, and domestic talk did not pass beyond the threshold-curtain.

entries.zh: 公主悉列于傳，非禮也。
entries.en: Recording every princess at length in biographical chapters was not proper ritual.
entries.literal: To list all princesses fully in biographies is not ritual-proper.

entries.zh: 然遼國專任外戚，公主多見紀、傳間，不得不表見之。
entries.en: Yet the Liao gave sole weight to maternal kin, and princesses appear so often in annals and biographies that they must be set out here in tabular form.
entries.literal: Yet the Liao state relied exclusively on maternal kin, and princesses often appear between annals and biographies; one cannot but set them forth in a table.

entries.zh: 禮，男女異長，不當與皇子同列，別為公主附表。
entries.en: By ritual propriety men and women follow different lines of seniority; princesses should not be listed with imperial sons, so they are given this separate appended table.
entries.literal: By rites men and women differ in seniority; they ought not share a column with imperial sons—a separate appended table for princesses.

entries.zh: ◎皇族表 遼太祖建國，諸弟窺覦，含容誘掖，弗忍致辟，古聖人猶難之。
entries.en: ◎Imperial Family Table. When the Liao Taizu founded his realm, his younger brothers coveted the throne; he forbearingly harbored them, won them with kindness, and could not bring himself to punish them with death—a dilemma even the sage kings of antiquity found hard to resolve.
entries.literal: ◎Imperial Family Table. When Taizu of Liao founded the state, his younger brothers cast covetous eyes upon it; he bore with them, enticed and supported them, and could not bear to execute them—even ancient sages found this difficult.

entries.zh: 雖其度量恢廓，然經國之慮遠矣。
entries.en: Magnanimous though he was, his calculations for governing the realm reached far beyond the moment.
entries.literal: Although his magnanimity was vast and accommodating, his forethought in governing the state extended much further.

entries.zh: 終遼之世，其出於橫帳、五院、六院之間者，大憝固有，元勛實多。
entries.en: Down to the end of the Liao, the lines that sprang from the Horizontal Tent and from the Five and Six Courts produced great villains to be sure, but they also yielded a host of founding meritorious servants.
entries.literal: Throughout the Liao dynasty, among those who came from the Horizontal Tent and from between the Five Courts and Six Courts, great villains indeed existed, but meritorious founding officials were truly many.

entries.zh: 不表見之，莫知源委。
entries.en: Without tabular presentation, their origins and lineages would remain unknown.
entries.literal: Unless set forth in a table, one cannot know origins and affiliations.

entries.zh: 作《皇族表》。
entries.en: The 《Imperial Family Table》 has therefore been composed.
entries.literal: I therefore compile the 《Imperial Family Table》.

entries.zh: ◎外戚表 漢外戚有新室之患，晉宗室有八王之難。
entries.en: ◎Families of Imperial Consorts Table. Han history warns of the danger consort families posed when Wang Mang seized power; Jin history records the catastrophe of the Rebellion of the Eight Princes.
entries.literal: ◎Table of Imperial Consorts' Kin. Under the Han, consort kin had the affliction of the New House; under the Jin, the imperial clan had the calamity of the Eight Princes.

entries.zh: 遼史耶律、蕭氏十居八九，宗室、外戚，勢分力敵，相為唇齒，以翰邦家。
entries.en: In the Liao annals the Yelü and Xiao families account for nearly all high officeholders; the imperial lineage and the empresses' kin were evenly matched in strength and acted as mutual safeguards of the dynasty.
entries.literal: In the Liao histories, the Yelü and Xiao clans make up eight or nine tenths; the imperial clan and consort kin, their power evenly divided, served as each other's lips and teeth to defend the state and house.

entries.zh: 是或一道。
entries.en: This may have been one workable approach to statecraft.
entries.literal: This too was one method.

entries.zh: 然以是而興，亦以是而亡，又其法之弊也。
entries.en: Yet what raised them also destroyed them—a defect inherent in the system.
entries.literal: Yet by this they rose, and by this they perished as well—again a flaw in their law.

entries.zh: 契丹外戚，其先曰二審密氏、曰拔里、曰乙室已。
entries.en: The Khitan empresses' kin traced their origins to the Two Shimi clans, the Bali, and the Yishi.
entries.literal: The Khitan consort kin, their forebears were called the Two Shimi clans, Bali, and Yishi.

entries.zh: 至遼太祖，娶述律氏。
entries.en: Taizu of Liao took a wife from the Shulü clan.
entries.literal: Reaching Liao Taizu, he married a woman of the Shulü clan.

entries.zh: 述律，本回鶻糯思之後。
entries.en: The Shulü were originally descended from the Uyghur chieftain Nusi.
entries.literal: Shulü, originally a descendant of the Uyghur Nusi.

entries.zh: 大同元年，太宗自汴將還，留外戚小漢為汴州節度使，賜姓名曰蕭翰，以從中國之俗，由是拔裏、乙室已、述律三族皆為蕭姓。
entries.en: In the first year of Datong (947), as Emperor Taizong prepared to withdraw from Kaifeng, he left the consort kinsman Xiaohan as military governor of Bianzhou and bestowed on him the Chinese-style name Xiao Han; thereafter the Bali, Yishi, and Shulü lineages all adopted the surname Xiao in keeping with Chinese custom.
entries.literal: In the first year of Datong, when Taizong was about to return from Bian, he left the consort kin Xiao Han as Military Governor of Bianzhou and bestowed the surname and given name Xiao Han, to follow Chinese custom; from this the three clans Bali, Yishi, and Shulü all took the surname Xiao.

entries.zh: 拔裏二房，曰大父、小父；
entries.en: The Bali were divided into two houses, the Great Father and Little Father lines;
entries.literal: The Bali had two branches, called Great Father and Little Father;

entries.zh: 乙室已亦二房，曰大翁、小翁；
entries.en: the Yishi likewise into the Great Elder and Little Elder lines;
entries.literal: Yishi likewise had two branches, called Great Elder and Little Elder;

entries.zh: 世宗以舅氏塔列葛為國舅別部。
entries.en: Emperor Shizong established his uncle Taliege as head of a separate Imperial Uncle division.
entries.literal: Emperor Shizong made his maternal uncle Taliege head of the Separate Division of Imperial Uncles.

entries.zh: 三族世預北宰相之選，自太祖神冊二年命阿骨只始也。
entries.en: All three clans held hereditary claim to the office of Northern Chancellor from Shence 2 (917), when Taizu first appointed Agu Zhi.
entries.literal: The three clans from generation to generation were favored in the selection for Northern Chancellor, beginning when Taizu in Shence year 2 appointed Agu Zhi.

entries.zh: 聖宗合拔裏、乙室已二國舅帳為一，與別部為二。
entries.en: Emperor Shengzong consolidated the Bali and Yishi imperial-uncle households into a single registry, leaving two divisions when the Separate Division is counted.
entries.literal: Emperor Shengzong merged the two Imperial Uncle registries of Bali and Yishi into one, making two together with the Separate Division.

entries.zh: 此遼外戚之始末也。
entries.en: Such is the full account of how the Liao empresses' kin took shape.
entries.literal: This is the beginning and end of Liao consort kin.

entries.zh: 作《外戚表》。
entries.en: Hence the compilation of the Families of Imperial Consorts Table.
