entries.zh: ○肅祖昭烈皇后蕭氏懿祖莊敬皇后蕭氏玄祖簡獻皇后蕭氏德祖宣簡皇后蕭氏太祖淳欽皇后述律氏太宗靖安皇后蕭氏世宗懷節皇后蕭氏世宗妃甄氏穆宗皇后蕭氏景宗睿智皇后蕭氏聖宗仁德皇后蕭氏聖宗欽哀皇后蕭氏興宗仁懿皇后蕭氏興宗貴妃蕭氏道宗宣懿皇后蕭氏道宗惠妃蕭氏天祚皇后蕭氏天祚德妃蕭氏天祚文妃蕭氏天祚元妃蕭氏
entries.en: ○ This chapter treats: Empress Zhaolie (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Su; Empress Zhuangjing (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Yi; Empress Jianxian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor Xuan; Empress Xuanjian (Xiao), wife of Ancestor De; Empress Chunqin (Shulü), wife of Taizu; Empress Jing'an (Xiao), wife of Taizong; Empress Huaijie (Xiao), wife of Shizong; Consort Zhen of Shizong; the Muzong empress (Xiao); Empress Ruizhi (Xiao), wife of Jingzong; Empress Rendé (Xiao), wife of Shengzong; Empress Qin'ai (Xiao), wife of Shengzong; Empress Renyi (Xiao), wife of Xingzong; Xingzong's imperial consort (Xiao); Empress Xuanyi (Xiao), wife of Daozong; Daozong's Consort Hui (Xiao); the Tianzuo empress (Xiao); Tianzuo's Virtuous Consort, Literary Consort, and Primary Consort (all Xiao).
entries.literal: ○ Empress Zhaolie of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Su; Empress Zhuangjing of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Yi; Empress Jianxian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor Xuan; Empress Xuanjian of the Xiao clan, consort of Ancestor De; Empress Chunqin of the Shulü clan, consort of Taizu; Empress Jing'an of the Xiao clan, consort of Taizong; Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Shizong; Consort Zhen of Shizong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Muzong; Empress Ruizhi of the Xiao clan, consort of Jingzong; Empress Rendé of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong; Empress Qin'ai of the Xiao clan, consort of Shengzong; Empress Renyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Xingzong; Imperial Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Xingzong; Empress Xuanyi of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong; Imperial Consort Hui of the Xiao clan, consort of Daozong; Empress of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Virtuous Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Literary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo; Primary Consort of the Xiao clan, consort of Tianzuo.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，后稱制，攝軍國事。
entries.en: After Taizu's death she ruled in her own name and directed military and civil affairs.
entries.literal: When Taizu died, the empress assumed regency and handled military and state affairs.

entries.zh: 及葬，欲以身殉，親戚百官力諫，因斷右腕納於柩。
entries.en: At the funeral she meant to follow him in death; kin and officials pleaded until she severed her right wrist and laid it in the coffin.
entries.literal: At the burial she wished to follow him in death; kin and officials strongly remonstrated, so she cut off her right wrist and placed it in the coffin.

entries.zh: 太宗即位，尊為皇太后。
entries.en: When Taizong succeeded, she was styled Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: When Taizong took the throne, she was honored as Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 會同初，上尊號曰廣德至仁昭烈崇簡應天皇太后。
entries.en: Early in Huitong she received the grand title Broad Virtue, Utmost Benevolence, Illustrious Martyr, Honored and Simple, Responsive-to-Heaven Imperial Empress Dowager.
entries.literal: At the beginning of Huitong, she was honored with the title Guangde Zhiren Zhaolie Chongjian Yingtian Imperial Empress Dowager.

entries.zh: 初，太祖嘗謂太宗必興我家，后欲令皇太子倍避之，太祖冊倍為東丹王。
entries.en: Taizu had once said Taizong would raise their line; the empress wanted Crown Prince Bei to step aside, and Taizu made Bei king of Eastern Dan.
entries.literal: Earlier Taizu had said Taizong would surely revive our house; the empress wished the crown prince Bei to yield to him, and Taizu enfeoffed Bei as King of Eastern Dan.

entries.zh: 太祖崩，太宗立，東丹王避之唐。
entries.en: After Taizu's death Taizong took the throne, and the Eastern Dan king fled to Tang.
entries.literal: When Taizu died, Taizong succeeded, and the King of Eastern Dan withdrew to Tang.

entries.zh: 太后常屬意於少子李胡。
entries.en: The dowager empress favored her younger son Lihu.
entries.literal: The empress dowager often set her hopes on the younger son Lihu.

entries.zh: 太宗崩，世宗即位於鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡以兵逆擊。
entries.en: When Taizong died Shizong was enthroned at Zhenyang; the dowager, enraged, sent Lihu with an army against him.
entries.literal: When Taizong died, Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang; the empress dowager was angry and sent Lihu with troops to strike him.

entries.zh: 李胡敗，太后親率師遇於潢河之橫渡。
entries.en: Lihu was beaten; the dowager herself led forces and met the enemy at Hengdu ford on the Huang River.
entries.literal: Lihu was defeated; the empress dowager personally led troops and met the foe at Hengdu on the Huang River.

entries.zh: 賴耶律屋質諫，罷兵。
entries.en: Only Yelü Wuzhi's counsel stopped the fighting.
entries.literal: Thanks to Yelü Wuzhi's remonstrance, the armies were halted.

entries.zh: 遷太后於祖州。
entries.en: The dowager was relocated to Zuzhou.
entries.literal: The empress dowager was moved to Zuzhou.

entries.zh: 應歷三年崩，年七十五，祔祖陵，謚曰貞烈。
entries.en: She died in Yingli 3, aged seventy-five, was buried at Zu Mausoleum, and received the posthumous name Steadfast Martyr.
entries.literal: She died in the third year of Yingli, aged seventy-five, and was buried at Zu Mausoleum with posthumous title Zhenlie.

entries.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。
entries.en: In Chongxi 21 her current posthumous title was adopted.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.

entries.zh: 世宗懷節皇后蕭氏，小字撒葛只，淳欽皇后弟阿古只之女。
entries.en: Empress Huaijie (Xiao), wife of Shizong, childhood name Sagezhi, daughter of Aguzhi, younger brother of Empress Chunqin.
entries.literal: Empress Huaijie of the Xiao clan, consort of Shizong, childhood name Sagezhi, daughter of Empress Chunqin's younger brother Aguzhi.

entries.zh: 帝為永康王，納之，生景宗。
entries.en: While he was Prince of Yongkang he wed her; she bore Jingzong.
entries.literal: When the emperor was Prince of Yongkang, he took her in marriage and she bore Jingzong.

entries.zh: 天祿末，立為皇后。
entries.en: Late in Tianlu she was made empress.
entries.literal: At the end of Tianlu, she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 明年秋，生萌古公主。
entries.en: The following autumn she bore Princess Menggu.
entries.literal: The next autumn she bore Princess Menggu.

entries.zh: 在蓐，察割作亂，弒太后及帝。
entries.en: Still in her lying-in, Chage rose in revolt and murdered the dowager and the emperor.
entries.literal: While she was in childbed, Chage rebelled and assassinated the empress dowager and the emperor.

entries.zh: 后乘步輦，直詣察割，請畢收殮。
entries.en: The empress took a litter straight to Chage and begged leave to finish the funeral rites.
entries.literal: The empress rode in a palanquin straight to Chage and asked that the burial rites be completed.

entries.zh: 明日遇害。
entries.en: The next day she too was slain.
entries.literal: The next day she was killed.

entries.zh: 謚曰孝烈皇后。
entries.en: Her posthumous title was Filial and Martyr Empress.
entries.literal: Posthumous title: Empress Xiaolie.

entries.zh: 重熙二十一年，更今謚。
entries.en: In Chongxi 21 her current posthumous title was adopted.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi, her present posthumous title was granted.

entries.zh: 世宗妃甄氏，後唐宮人，有姿色。
entries.en: Shizong's consort Zhen, a Later Tang palace woman, was strikingly beautiful.
entries.literal: Consort Zhen of Shizong, a palace woman of Later Tang, possessed beauty of form.

entries.zh: 帝從太宗南征得之，寵遇甚厚，生寧王只沒。
entries.en: The emperor took her on Taizong's southern campaign and favored her deeply; she bore Prince of Ning Zhimie.
entries.literal: The emperor obtained her on Taizong's southern campaign and favored her greatly; she bore Prince of Ning Zhimie.

entries.zh: 及即位，立為皇后。
entries.en: At his accession she was made empress.
entries.literal: When he took the throne, she was established as empress.

entries.zh: 嚴明端重，風神閑雅。
entries.en: She was strict yet dignified, her manner calm and elegant.
entries.literal: Severe and bright, dignified and grave, her bearing was easy and refined.

entries.zh: 內治有法，莫幹以私。
entries.en: She ran the inner court by rule, and no one could bend her with private pleas.
entries.literal: In inner governance she had method; none could sway her with private interest.

entries.zh: 劉知遠、郭威稱帝，世宗承強盛之資，奄奄歲時。
entries.en: When Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei took imperial titles, Shizong, though he held a mighty inheritance, let year after year pass without action.
entries.literal: Liu Zhiyuan and Guo Wei declared themselves emperors; Shizong, inheriting a time of great strength, let the years slip idly by.

entries.zh: 后與參帷幄，密贊大謀，不果用。
entries.en: The empress joined council in the command tent and secretly urged bold plans, but none were adopted.
entries.literal: The empress joined in the command tent and secretly supported great plans, but they were not carried out.

entries.zh: 察割作亂，遇害。
entries.en: When Chage rebelled, she was killed.
entries.literal: When Chage rebelled, she met with disaster.

entries.zh: 景宗立，葬二后於醫巫閭山，建廟陵寢側。
entries.en: When Jingzong succeeded, he buried both empresses on Mount Yiwulü and raised shrines beside the royal tombs.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he buried the two empresses at Mount Yiwulü and built temples beside the mausoleum.

entries.zh: 義宗，名倍，小字圖欲，太祖長子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。
entries.en: Yizong, whose personal name was Bei and childhood name Tuyu, was Taizu's eldest son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
entries.literal: Yizong, personal name Bei, childhood name Tuyu, eldest son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

entries.zh: 幼聰敏好學，外寬內摯。
entries.en: As a boy he was quick-witted and studious, mild in manner yet ardent at heart.
entries.literal: In youth clever and eager to learn; outwardly lenient, inwardly earnest.

entries.zh: 神冊元年春，立為皇太子。
entries.en: In the spring of Shence year 1 (916) he was made crown prince.
entries.literal: In spring of the first year of Shence, he was installed as crown prince.

entries.zh: 時太祖問侍臣曰：「受命之君，當事天敬神。
entries.en: Once Taizu asked his ministers, "A ruler who has received Heaven's mandate ought to honor Heaven and the spirits.
entries.literal: At that time Taizu asked his attending ministers, saying: "A ruler who has received the Mandate should serve Heaven and revere the spirits.

entries.zh: 有大功德者，朕欲祀之，何先？」
entries.en: Among the figures of greatest merit, whom should I worship first?"
entries.literal: Among those of great merit and virtue, whom does Your Majesty wish to sacrifice to first?"

entries.zh: 皆以佛對。
entries.en: They all named the Buddha.
entries.literal: All answered with the Buddha.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「佛非中國教。」
entries.en: Taizu said, "Buddhism is not a teaching native to China."
entries.literal: Taizu said: "Buddhism is not the teaching of the Central States."

entries.zh: 倍曰：「孔子大聖，萬世所尊，宜先。」
entries.en: Bei replied, "Confucius is the supreme sage, revered through the ages—he should come first."
entries.literal: Bei said: "Confucius the great sage, honored for ten thousand generations, should come first."

entries.zh: 太祖大悅，即建孔子廟，詔皇太子春秋釋奠。
entries.en: Taizu was delighted, had a Confucian temple built at once, and ordered the crown prince to conduct the spring and autumn rites of sacrifice.
entries.literal: Taizu was greatly pleased, immediately built a temple to Confucius, and decreed that the crown prince perform the spring and autumn sacrificial offerings.

entries.zh: 章肅皇帝，小字李胡，一名洪古，字奚隱，太祖第三子，母淳欽皇后蕭氏。
entries.en: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, also called Honggu, style Xiyin, was Taizu's third son; his mother was Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.
entries.literal: Emperor Zhangsu, childhood name Li Hu, another name Honggu, style Xiyin, third son of Taizu, mother Empress Chunqin of the Xiao clan.

entries.zh: 少勇悍多力，而性殘酷，小怒輒黥人面，或投水火中。
entries.en: As a youth he was fierce and powerful, but cruel by nature; the least provocation could bring facial tattooing or being thrown into water or fire.
entries.literal: In youth brave, fierce, and strong, yet cruel by nature; at a slight anger he would tattoo faces or cast people into water or fire.

entries.zh: 太祖嘗觀諸子寢，李胡縮項臥內，曰：「是必在諸子下。」
entries.en: Taizu once watched his sons sleep. Li Hu lay curled up with his neck drawn in, and Taizu said, "This one will surely rank below his brothers."
entries.literal: Taizu once watched his sons sleep; Li Hu lay inside with neck drawn in, and said: "This one is sure to rank below the other sons."

entries.zh: 又嘗大寒，命三子采薪。
entries.en: On another bitterly cold day he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.
entries.literal: On another occasion in severe cold he ordered the three sons to gather firewood.

entries.zh: 太宗不擇而取，最先至；
entries.en: Taizong gathered without picking and came back first;
entries.literal: Taizong took without choosing and arrived first;

entries.zh: 人皇王取其乾者束而歸，後至；
entries.en: the Human Emperor King chose the dry wood, bound it into a bundle, and returned later;
entries.literal: the Human Emperor King took the dry pieces, bound them, and returned, arriving later;

entries.zh: 李胡取少而棄多，既至，袖手而立。
entries.en: Li Hu took little and threw away much; when he arrived he stood with empty hands in his sleeves.
entries.literal: Li Hu took little and discarded much; when he arrived he stood with hands in sleeves.

entries.zh: 太祖曰：「長巧而次成，少不及矣。」
entries.en: Taizu said, "The eldest is clever, the second gets things done; the youngest falls short."
entries.literal: Taizu said: "The eldest is clever, the second accomplishes; the youngest does not measure up."

entries.zh: 而母篤愛李胡。
entries.en: Yet his mother doted on Li Hu.
entries.literal: Yet the mother dearly loved Li Hu.

entries.zh: 嘗從征烏古、党項，為先鋒都統，及經略燕地。
entries.en: He once campaigned against the Wugu and Tangut as vanguard commander-in-chief and directed operations in the Yan region.
entries.literal: He once followed campaigns against the Wugu and Tangut, served as vanguard commander-in-chief, and directed operations in the Yan region.

entries.zh: 太祖西征，留倍守京師，因陳取渤海計。
entries.en: When Taizu marched west, he left Bei to guard the capital and urged a plan to conquer Bohai.
entries.literal: When Taizu campaigned west, he left Bei to guard the capital and presented a plan for taking Bohai.

entries.zh: 天顯元年，從征渤海。
entries.en: In Tianxian year 1 he joined the expedition against Bohai.
entries.literal: In the first year of Tianxian he followed the campaign against Bohai.

entries.zh: 拔扶餘城，上欲括戶口，倍諫曰：「今始得地而料民，民必不安。
entries.en: After Fuyu city fell the emperor wished to register households; Bei remonstrated, "Having just taken the land, a census will unsettle the people.
entries.literal: Fuyu city was taken; the sovereign wished to register households, and Bei remonstrated, saying, "Having just gained the land and now counting the people, the people are sure to be unsettled.

entries.zh: 若乘破竹之勢，徑造忽汗城，克之必矣。」
entries.en: If we press the advantage like splitting bamboo and march straight on Hohan city, we are sure to take it."
entries.literal: If we ride the momentum of splitting bamboo and strike straight for Hohan city, we are certain to take it."

entries.zh: 太祖從之。
entries.en: Taizu accepted his advice.
entries.literal: Taizu followed his counsel.

entries.zh: 倍與大元帥德光為前鋒，夜圍忽汗城，大諲譔窮蹙，請降。
entries.en: Bei and Great Marshal Deguang led the vanguard and besieged Hohan city by night; Dayinzan, cornered, offered surrender.
entries.literal: Bei and the Great Marshal Deguang served as vanguard; they besieged Hohan city by night, and Dayinzan, hard pressed, begged to surrender.

entries.zh: 尋復叛，太祖破之。
entries.en: He soon rebelled again, and Taizu put him down.
entries.literal: Soon he rebelled again, and Taizu defeated him.

entries.zh: 改其國曰東丹，名其城曰天福，以倍為人皇王主之。
entries.en: The state was renamed Eastern Dan, the city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was installed as Human Emperor King to rule it.
entries.literal: Its state was renamed Eastern Dan, its city renamed Tianfu, and Bei was made Human Emperor King to rule it.

entries.zh: 仍賜天子冠服，建元甘露，稱制，置左右大次四相及百官，一用漢法。
entries.en: He was also granted imperial cap and robes, adopted the era name Ganlu, ruled in his own right, and set up left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the full bureaucracy—all on the Han model.
entries.literal: He was further granted the cap and robes of the Son of Heaven, adopted the era name Ganlu, exercised regency, and established left and right great secondary halls, four chancellors, and the hundred offices—all following Han institutions.

entries.zh: 歲貢布十五萬端，馬千匹。
entries.en: Each year he paid tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.
entries.literal: Each year he rendered tribute of one hundred fifty thousand bolts of cloth and one thousand horses.

entries.zh: 上諭曰：「此地瀕海，非可久居，留汝撫治，以見朕愛民之心。」
entries.en: The emperor told him, "This land lies on the sea and cannot be held long; I leave you to govern it and show my care for the people."
entries.literal: The sovereign instructed him, saying, "This land borders the sea and cannot be long occupied; I leave you to govern and soothe it, that my love for the people may be seen."

entries.zh: 駕將還，倍作歌以獻。
entries.en: As the emperor prepared to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.
entries.literal: As the imperial carriage was about to return, Bei composed a song and presented it.

entries.zh: 陛辭，太祖曰：「得汝治東土，吾復何憂。」
entries.en: As he took leave at court, Taizu said, "With you governing the east, what have I left to fear?"
entries.literal: Taking leave at the steps, Taizu said, "With you governing the eastern lands, what further worry have I?"

entries.zh: 倍號泣而出。
entries.en: Bei wept aloud as he departed.
entries.literal: Bei wailed and wept as he went out.

entries.zh: 遂如儀坤州。
entries.en: He then went on to Yikun Prefecture as ordered.
entries.literal: He then proceeded to Yikun Prefecture as prescribed.

entries.zh: 未幾，諸部多叛，大元帥討平之。
entries.en: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal put them down.
entries.literal: Before long many tribes rebelled; the Great Marshal suppressed and pacified them.

entries.zh: 太祖訃至，倍即日奔赴山陵。
entries.en: When word of Taizu's death arrived, Bei set out the same day for the imperial tomb.
entries.literal: When Taizu's death notice arrived, Bei set out that same day to hurry to the imperial tomb.

entries.zh: 倍知皇太后意欲立德光，乃謂公卿曰：「大元帥功德及人神，中外攸屬，宜主社稷。」
entries.en: Knowing the Empress Dowager meant to elevate Deguang, Bei told the chief ministers, "The Great Marshal's achievements touch both men and spirits; court and country alike look to him—he ought to rule the realm."
entries.literal: Bei knew the Empress Dowager wished to install Deguang, and therefore said to the dukes and ministers: "The Great Marshal's merit reaches men and spirits; within and without all look to him—he should hold the altars of state."

entries.zh: 乃與群臣請於太后而讓位焉。
entries.en: He and the officials petitioned the Empress Dowager, and he yielded the throne.
entries.literal: He then joined the officials in petitioning the Empress Dowager and yielded the throne.

entries.zh: 於是大元帥即皇帝位，是為太宗。
entries.en: The Great Marshal then took the throne as Emperor Taizong.
entries.literal: Thereupon the Great Marshal assumed the imperial position—this was Taizong.

entries.zh: 太宗既立，見疑，以東平為南京，徙倍居之，盡遷其民。
entries.en: After Taizong's accession Bei fell under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was relocated there, and the entire population was moved away.
entries.literal: Once Taizong was established, Bei came under suspicion; Dongping was made the Southern Capital, Bei was moved to dwell there, and all its people were relocated.

entries.zh: 又置衛士陰伺動靜。
entries.en: Guards were also set to spy on his movements in secret.
entries.literal: Guards were also posted to watch his movements in secret.

entries.zh: 倍既歸國，命王繼遠撰《建南京碑》，起書樓於西宮，作《樂田園詩》。
entries.en: Once back in his domain, Bei had Wang Jiyuan draft the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," built a book tower in the Western Palace, and composed "Joy in the Garden."
entries.literal: After Bei returned to his domain, he ordered Wang Jiyuan to compose the "Stele on Building the Southern Capital," raised a book tower in the Western Palace, and wrote the poem "Joy in the Garden."

entries.zh: 唐明宗聞之，遣人跨海持書密召倍。
entries.en: When Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of it, he sent envoys across the sea with a secret letter inviting Bei.
entries.literal: Tang Emperor Mingzong heard of this and sent men across the sea with a letter to summon Bei in secret.

entries.zh: 倍因畋海上。
entries.en: Bei happened to be hunting at sea.
entries.literal: Bei happened to be hunting on the sea.

entries.zh: 使再至，倍謂左右曰：「我以天下讓主上，今反見疑；
entries.en: When the envoys came again, Bei told his attendants, "I gave the empire to our sovereign, yet now I am distrusted;
entries.literal: When the envoys came a second time, Bei said to those beside him: "I yielded the realm to our lord; now I am met with suspicion instead;

entries.zh: 不如適他國，以成吳太伯之名。」
entries.en: better to go abroad and earn a name like Wu Taibo's."
entries.literal: better to go to another state and fulfill the name of Wu Taibo."

entries.zh: 立木海上，刻詩曰：「小山壓大山，大山全無力。
entries.en: He erected a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill weighs on the great hill—the great hill has no strength at all.
entries.literal: He set up a post on the sea and carved a poem: "A little hill presses the great hill; the great hill is wholly without strength.

entries.zh: 羞見故鄉人，從此投外國。」
entries.en: Too ashamed to face the folk of home—from this I go to a foreign land."
entries.literal: Ashamed to face the people of my homeland, from this I cast myself to a foreign land."

entries.zh: 攜高美人，載書浮海而去。
entries.en: Taking Lady Gao with him, he loaded his books and sailed away across the sea.
entries.literal: Taking Lady Gao the fair, he loaded his books and went off across the sea.

entries.zh: 天顯五年，遣徇地代北，攻寰州，多俘而還，遂立為皇太弟，兼天下兵馬大元帥。
entries.en: In Tianxian year 5 he was sent to campaign in the Dai north, attacked Huan Prefecture, returned with many captives, and was made Imperial Younger Brother Heir while also serving as commander-in-chief of all forces.
entries.literal: In the fifth year of Tianxian he was sent to traverse the land north of Dai, attacked Huan Prefecture, took many captives and returned, and was then installed as Imperial Younger Brother Heir and concurrently Great Marshal of All Armies Under Heaven.

entries.zh: 太宗親征，常留守京師。
entries.en: Whenever Taizong led campaigns in person, Li Hu usually stayed behind as regent in the capital.
entries.literal: When Taizong campaigned in person, he regularly remained to guard the capital.

entries.zh: 世宗即位鎮陽，太后怒，遣李胡將兵擊之。
entries.en: When Shizong assumed the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager in anger sent Li Hu with an army against him.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne at Zhenyang, the Empress Dowager was angry and sent Li Hu to lead troops against him.

entries.zh: 至泰德泉，為安端、留哥所敗。
entries.en: At Taidé Spring he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.
entries.literal: Reaching Taidé Spring, he was defeated by Anduan and Liuge.

entries.zh: 太后與世宗隔潢河而陣，各言舉兵意。
entries.en: The Empress Dowager and Shizong drew up on opposite banks of the Huang River and each explained why he had taken up arms.
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager and Shizong faced each other across the Huang River in battle array, each stating the reason for raising troops.

entries.zh: 耶律屋質入諫太后曰：「主上已立，宜許之。」
entries.en: Yelü Wuzhi went in and urged the Empress Dowager, "The emperor is already enthroned—you ought to accept him."
entries.literal: Yelü Wuzhi entered and remonstrated with the Empress Dowager, saying: "The sovereign is already established—you should acknowledge him."

entries.zh: 時李胡在側，作色曰：「我在，兀欲安得立？」
entries.en: Li Hu stood at her side, flushed with anger, and said, "As long as I live, how can Wuyue take the throne?"
entries.literal: At that time Li Hu was at her side; he changed color and said: "While I am here, how can Wuyue be established?"

entries.zh: 屋質曰：「奈公酷暴失人心何！」
entries.en: Wuzhi replied, "What can be done when you are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts?"
entries.literal: Wuzhi said: "What of it that you, sir, are cruel and violent and have lost the people's hearts!"

entries.zh: 太后顧李胡曰：「昔我與太祖愛汝異於諸子，諺云：『偏憐之子不保業，難得之婦不主家。』
entries.en: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said, "Taizu and I once loved you more than your brothers. As the proverb runs, 'The child too fondly indulged cannot keep the estate; the wife too hard won cannot keep the house.'
entries.literal: The Empress Dowager turned to Li Hu and said: "In the past I and Taizu loved you differently from the other sons. A proverb says: 'A child over-favored cannot keep the estate; a wife hard to win does not manage the household.'

entries.zh: 我非不欲立汝，汝自不能矣。」
entries.en: It is not that I would not make you emperor—you simply could not hold it."
entries.literal: It is not that I did not wish to install you—you yourself could not do it."

entries.zh: 及會議，世宗使解劍而言。
entries.en: At the council Shizong had his sword taken before he addressed them.
entries.literal: When they met in council, Shizong had his sword removed before he spoke.

entries.zh: 和約既定，趨上京。
entries.en: Once peace was agreed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: Once the peace pact was fixed, they hurried to the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 會有告李胡與太后謀廢立者，徙李胡祖州，禁其出入。
entries.en: When word came that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager were plotting to depose the emperor, Li Hu was exiled to Zuzhou and forbidden to leave.
entries.literal: Soon someone reported that Li Hu and the Empress Dowager plotted deposition and installation; Li Hu was moved to Zuzhou and his coming and going forbidden.

entries.zh: 穆宗時，其子喜隱謀反，辭逮李胡，囚之，死獄中，年五十，葬玉峰山西谷。
entries.en: Under Muzong his son Xiyin rebelled; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at fifty, and was buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.
entries.literal: In Muzong's time his son Xiyin plotted rebellion; testimony implicated Li Hu, who was imprisoned and died in jail at age fifty, buried in the western valley of Mount Yufeng.

entries.zh: 統和中，追謚欽順皇帝。
entries.en: In the Tonghe era he was posthumously styled Emperor Qinshun.
entries.literal: During Tonghe he was posthumously titled Emperor Qinshun.

entries.zh: 重熙二十一年，更謚章肅，后曰和敬。
entries.en: In Chongxi year 21 his title was changed to Zhangsu; his consort was styled Hejing.
entries.literal: In the twenty-first year of Chongxi the title was changed to Zhangsu; the consort was called Hejing.

entries.zh: 二子：宋王喜隱、衛王宛。
entries.en: He had two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.
entries.literal: Two sons: Prince of Song Xiyin and Prince of Wei Wan.

entries.zh: 論曰：李胡殘酷驕盈，太祖知其不才而不能教，太后不知其惡而溺愛之。
entries.en: Commentary: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant. Taizu knew he lacked talent but could not teach him; the Empress Dowager did not see his wickedness and spoiled him.
entries.literal: The commentary says: Li Hu was cruel and arrogant; Taizu knew he lacked talent yet could not instruct him, and the Empress Dowager did not know his wickedness and doted on him.

entries.zh: 初以屋質之言定立世宗，而復謀廢立。
entries.en: At first Wuzhi's counsel secured Shizong's enthronement, yet mother and son plotted deposition again.
entries.literal: At first through Wuzhi's words Shizong's enthronement was settled, yet they again plotted deposition and installation.

entries.zh: 子孫繼以逆誅，並及其身，可哀也已。
entries.en: Descendants were executed one after another for treason, and ruin reached him as well—a lamentable end.
entries.literal: Descendants in succession met execution for treason, reaching even to his person—pitiable indeed.

entries.zh: 夫自太祖之世，剌葛、安端首倡禍亂，太祖既不之誅，又復用之，固為有君人之量，然惟太祖之才足以駕馭，庶乎其可也。
entries.en: From Taizu's reign Cige and Anduan were the first to stir rebellion; Taizu neither executed them outright nor cast them off permanently, which showed true magnanimity as a ruler—yet only Taizu's ability could keep them in hand, and even that was barely enough.
entries.literal: From Taizu's age, Cige and Anduan first raised calamity and disorder; Taizu neither punished them to the full, yet employed them again—this truly showed the measure of a ruler of men, yet only Taizu's talent could rein them in; perhaps that could suffice.

entries.zh: 李胡而下，宗王反側，無代無之，遼之內難，與國始終。
entries.en: From Li Hu onward, imperial princes were forever restless; no reign was free of it—Liao's internal strife dogged the dynasty from start to finish.
entries.literal: From Li Hu downward, imperial princes were restless; no reign lacked this—Liao's internal troubles ran with the state from beginning to end.

entries.zh: 厥後嗣君，雖嚴法以繩之，卒不可止。
entries.en: Later emperors bound them with harsh law, yet still could not stop it.
entries.literal: Later successor rulers, though they bound them with stern law, ultimately could not stop it.

entries.zh: 烏乎，創業垂統之主，所以貽厥孫謀者，可不審歟！
entries.en: Alas! Founders who establish a dynasty and pass it on—what they leave their heirs demands the utmost care!
entries.literal: Alas! A founding ruler who hands down the succession—what he bequeaths to his descendants' plans: can it go unexamined!

entries.zh: 唐以天子儀衛迎倍，倍坐船殿，眾官陪列上壽。
entries.en: Tang received Bei with imperial ceremonial guard; he sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering congratulations.
entries.literal: Tang received Bei with the ceremonial guard of the Son of Heaven; Bei sat in the boat-palace while officials stood in attendance offering longevity wishes.

entries.zh: 至汴，見明宗。
entries.en: On reaching Bian he was received by Emperor Mingzong.
entries.literal: Reaching Bian, he met Mingzong.

entries.zh: 明宗以莊宗后夏氏妻之，賜姓東丹，名之曰慕華。
entries.en: Mingzong gave him Zhuangzong's consort, Lady Xia, in marriage and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.
entries.literal: Mingzong gave him in marriage Empress Xia of Zhuangzong and granted the surname Eastern Dan, naming him Muhua.

entries.zh: 改瑞州為懷化軍，拜懷化軍節度使、瑞慎等州觀察使。
entries.en: Ruizhou was made Huaihua Army, and he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.
entries.literal: Ruizhou was changed to Huaihua Army; he was appointed military commissioner of Huaihua Army and surveillance commissioner of Ruizhou, Shen, and other prefectures.

entries.zh: 復賜姓李，名贊華。
entries.en: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.
entries.literal: He was again granted the surname Li and named Zanhua.

entries.zh: 移鎮滑州，遙領虔州節度使。
entries.en: He was transferred to Huazhou and concurrently held the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.
entries.literal: He was transferred to garrison Huazhou and held concurrently the post of military commissioner of Qianzhou in absentia.

entries.zh: 倍雖在異國，常思其親，問安之使不絕。
entries.en: Though abroad, Bei never ceased thinking of his family, and messengers sending greetings home never stopped.
entries.literal: Though Bei was in a foreign land, he constantly thought of his kin, and envoys sending inquiries after their welfare never ceased.

entries.zh: 後明宗養子從珂弒其君自立，倍密報太宗曰：「從珂弒君，盍討之。」
entries.en: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized power; Bei secretly informed Taizong, "Congke has murdered his lord—we ought to punish him."
entries.literal: Later Mingzong's adopted son Congke murdered his sovereign and seized the throne; Bei secretly reported to Taizong, saying, "Congke murdered his lord—why not punish him?"

entries.zh: 及太宗立石敬瑭為晉主，加兵於洛。
entries.en: When Taizong set up Shi Jingtang as Jin emperor and sent additional troops against Luoyang.
entries.literal: When Taizong installed Shi Jingtang as Jin sovereign and added troops at Luoyang.

entries.zh: 從珂欲自焚，召倍與俱，倍不從，遣壯士李彥紳害之，時年三十八。
entries.en: Congke meant to burn himself and summoned Bei to die with him; Bei refused, and Congke sent the strongman Li Yanzhen to kill him. Bei was thirty-eight.
entries.literal: Congke wished to burn himself, summoned Bei to join him, and Bei refused; he sent the strong man Li Yanzhen to kill him—he was thirty-eight years old.

entries.zh: 有一僧為收瘞之。
entries.en: A monk gathered and buried his remains.
entries.literal: A monk gathered and buried his remains.

entries.zh: 敬瑭入洛，喪服臨哭，以王禮權厝。
entries.en: When Jingtang entered Luoyang he came in mourning to weep at the coffin and provisionally interred Bei with royal rites.
entries.literal: Jingtang entered Luoyang, came in mourning garb to weep before the coffin, and provisionally interred him with the rites due a king.

entries.zh: 後太宗改葬於醫巫閭山，謚曰文武元皇王。
entries.en: Later Taizong had him reburied on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously styled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.
entries.literal: Later Taizong reburied him on Mount Yiwulü and posthumously titled him King Yuanhuang the Civil and Martial.

entries.zh: 世宗即位，謚讓國皇帝，陵曰顯陵。
entries.en: When Shizong succeeded, Bei was posthumously styled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was named Xianling.
entries.literal: When Shizong took the throne, he was posthumously titled Emperor Who Yielded the Realm; his tomb was called Xianling.

entries.zh: 統和中，更謚文獻。
entries.en: In the Tonghe era his posthumous title was changed to Wenxian.
entries.literal: During Tonghe his title was changed to Wenxian.

entries.zh: 重熙二十年，增謚文獻欽義皇帝，廟號義宗，及謚二后曰端順，曰柔貞。
entries.en: In Chongxi year 20 his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and his two consorts were posthumously styled Duanshun and Rouzhen.
entries.literal: In the twentieth year of Chongxi his honorific was advanced to Emperor Wenxian, Qinyi; his temple name was Yizong, and the two empresses were posthumously titled Duanshun and Rouzhen.

entries.zh: 倍初市書至萬卷，藏於醫巫閭絕頂之望海堂。
entries.en: Bei had once bought books until his collection reached ten thousand scrolls, which he kept in the Wanghai Hall on the summit of Mount Yiwulü.
entries.literal: Bei at first bought books until they reached ten thousand scrolls, storing them in the Wanghai Hall atop the summit of Mount Yiwulü.

entries.zh: 通陰陽，知音律，精醫藥、砭焫之術。
entries.en: He understood yin and yang, knew music and pitch, and was skilled in medicine, acupuncture, and moxibustion.
entries.literal: He mastered yin and yang, understood music and pitch, and was expert in medicine and the arts of acupuncture and moxibustion.

entries.zh: 工遼、漢文章，嘗譯《陰符經》。
entries.en: He wrote well in both Khitan and Chinese and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."
entries.literal: He was accomplished in Khitan and Han writing and once translated the "Classic of the Hidden Talisman."

entries.zh: 善畫本國人物，如《射騎》、《獵雪騎》、《千鹿圖》，皆入宋秘府。
entries.en: He excelled at painting Khitan subjects; works such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer" all entered the Song imperial collection.
entries.literal: He was skilled at painting figures of his own country, such as "Mounted Archers," "Hunting Snow Cavalry," and "A Thousand Deer"—all entered the Song imperial treasury.

entries.zh: 然性刻急好殺，婢妾微過，常加刲灼。
entries.en: Yet he was harsh and quick-tempered and prone to cruelty; for the slightest slip by maids or concubines he often branded or cauterized them.
entries.literal: Yet his nature was harsh and impatient and he loved killing; for slight faults in maidservants and concubines he often applied branding and cautery.

entries.zh: 夏氏懼而求削髮為尼。
entries.en: Lady Xia, terrified, begged to shave her head and take vows as a nun.
entries.literal: Lady Xia, in fear, begged to shave her head and become a nun.

entries.zh: 五子：長世宗，次婁國、稍、隆先、道隱，各有傳。
entries.en: He had five sons: the eldest was Shizong, followed by Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each treated in his own biography.
entries.literal: Five sons: the eldest Shizong, next Louguo, Shao, Longxian, and Daoyin—each has a separate biography.

entries.zh: 平王隆先，字團隱，母大氏。
entries.en: Longxian, Prince of Ping, whose style was Tuanyin, was born to the Da clan.
entries.literal: Prince of Ping Longxian, style Tuanyin, mother the Da clan.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，始封平王。
entries.en: When Jingzong succeeded he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was first enfeoffed as Prince of Ping.

entries.zh: 未幾，兼政事令，留守東京。
entries.en: Soon afterward he was made chief of governmental affairs while also serving as regent of the Eastern Capital.
entries.literal: Before long he concurrently served as chief of governmental affairs and remained to guard the Eastern Capital.

entries.zh: 薄賦稅，省刑獄，恤鰥寡，數薦賢能之士。
entries.en: He eased taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for the widowed and orphaned, and repeatedly recommended able men.
entries.literal: He lightened taxes, reduced penal cases, cared for widowers and widows, and repeatedly recommended worthy and capable men.

entries.zh: 後與統軍耶律室魯同討高麗有功，還薨，葬醫巫閭山之道隱谷。
entries.en: Later he joined army commander Yelu Shilu in a successful campaign against Goryeo; on his return he died and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.
entries.literal: Later he campaigned against Goryeo together with army commander Yelu Shilu with merit; returning, he died, and was buried in Daoyin Valley on Mount Yiwulü.

entries.zh: 平王為人聰明，博學能詩，有《閬苑集》行於世。
entries.en: The Prince of Ping was clever, broadly learned, and skilled in poetry; his Collection of the Lang Garden circulated widely.
entries.literal: Prince of Ping was clever by nature, broadly learned and skilled in poetry; his "Collection of the Lang Garden" circulated in the world.

entries.zh: 保寧之季，其子陳哥與渤海官屬謀殺其父，舉兵作亂，上命轘裂於市。
entries.en: Late in the Baoning era his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to murder him and rose in rebellion; the emperor ordered Chenge executed by dismemberment in the market.
entries.literal: Late in Baoning his son Chenge plotted with Bohai officials to kill his father, raised troops in rebellion, and the sovereign ordered him torn apart by carriages in the market.

entries.zh: 晉王道隱，字留隱，母高氏。
entries.en: Daoyin, Prince of Jin, whose style was Liuyin, was born to the Gao clan.
entries.literal: Prince of Jin Daoyin, style Liuyin, mother the Gao clan.

entries.zh: 道隱生於唐，人皇王遭李從珂之害，時年尚幼，洛陽僧匿而養之，因名道隱。
entries.en: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King was killed by Li Congke he was still a child, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.
entries.literal: Daoyin was born in Tang; when the Human Emperor King met harm at the hands of Li Congke he was still young, and a Luoyang monk hid and raised him—hence the name Daoyin.

entries.zh: 太宗滅唐，還京，詔賜外羅山地居焉。
entries.en: After Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him residence on Mount Wailuo.
entries.literal: When Taizong destroyed Tang and returned to the capital, an edict granted him land on Mount Wailuo to dwell.

entries.zh: 性沈靜，有文武才，時人稱之。
entries.en: Calm and reserved by nature, he had both civil and military talent, and contemporaries praised him.
entries.literal: His nature was calm and reserved; he had civil and military talent, and men of the time praised him.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，封蜀王，為上京留守。
entries.en: When Jingzong succeeded he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and appointed regent of the Upper Capital.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, he was enfeoffed as Prince of Shu and made regent of the Upper Capital.

entries.zh: 乾亨元年，遷守南京，號令嚴肅，民獲安業。
entries.en: In Qianheng year 1 he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his rule was strict and orderly, and the people lived in peace.
entries.literal: In the first year of Qianheng he was transferred to guard the Southern Capital; his orders were stern and disciplined, and the people found security in their livelihoods.

entries.zh: 居數年，徙封荊王。
entries.en: After several years his title was changed to Prince of Jing.
entries.literal: After several years he was moved to the enfeoffment of Prince of Jing.

entries.zh: 統和初，病薨，追封晉王。
entries.en: Early in the Tonghe era he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.
entries.literal: Early in Tonghe he died of illness and was posthumously enfeoffed as Prince of Jin.

entries.zh: 喜隱，字完德，雄偉善騎射，封趙王。
entries.en: Xiyin, whose style was Wande, was imposing and skilled in mounted archery and was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.
entries.literal: Xiyin, style Wande, imposing and skilled in mounted archery, was enfeoffed as Prince of Zhao.

entries.zh: 應歷中，謀反，事覺，上臨問有狀，以親釋之。
entries.en: During the Yingli era he plotted rebellion; when the plot was exposed the emperor questioned him in person, found the charge proved, yet released him as a kinsman.
entries.literal: During Yingli he plotted rebellion; when the affair was discovered the sovereign questioned him in person and found the facts established, yet released him because of kinship.

entries.zh: 未幾，復反，下獄。
entries.en: Before long he rebelled again and was thrown into prison.
entries.literal: Before long he rebelled again and was cast into prison.

entries.zh: 景宗即位，聞有赦，自去其械而朝。
entries.en: When Jingzong succeeded, hearing that an amnesty had been declared, he removed his own shackles and came to court.
entries.literal: When Jingzong took the throne, hearing there was an amnesty, he removed his own fetters and came to court.
